## Problem statement

In Hex War (the Hangar War ring) a between-sortie frontier tick can launch an attack **from** the very hex the player's current sortie is attacking. A hex that is fighting off the player — "too busy defending" — should not simultaneously press an attack on a neighbouring player-held hex.

## Users

- **Hangar War player (mid-ring).** "I deploy at hex X to take it. On landing I find X also hit one of my held hexes during the tick — it was supposed to be defending against me, not attacking me." The player experiences a defence that cannot be answered: the origin hex is the hex they just fought.
- **Product/design owner.** Wants the rule "an attacked hex defends, it does not attack" so committing to a sortie has a legible, fair consequence instead of a free counter-punch.

Example user stories:

1. As a player attacking hex *X*, I want *X* to be unable to launch an attack this tick, so that my defence push cannot be punished by the hex I am pushing.
2. As a player attacking hex *X* whose neighbouring held hex is also reachable from unheld hex *Y*, I still expect pressure from *Y*, so the ring keeps squeezing me even while I commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A between-sortie tick resolved for a hex the player is attacking never records that hex as an attack origin: every entry in the tick record's `attacks` names a different unheld neighbour, and a held target whose **only** unheld neighbour is the attacked hex draws no attack at all (no record entry, no throw).
- When another unheld neighbour of the target exists, the attack still happens from the neighbour the existing selection order names next (most aggressive, ties settled by sorted id), so the rule suppresses only the origin, not the attack: the recorded force, aggression multiplier, jitter, attack strength and margin are the ones that neighbour produces.
- A tick resolved without a player-attacking hex (the arcade run, a deployment whose `hexId` is `null`, a hex id absent from the ring) is byte-identical to today's behaviour: the existing `resolveDefence`, `attackingNeighbour` and `runFrontierTick` tests, and the queued-attack (pending) cases, pass unchanged.
- `PlayScene` passes the current deployment's target hex on **both** tick paths — the winning path (tick resolved at mini-boss defeat, before the capture) and the losing path (tick resolved at run end) — and replay determinism holds: the same payload, seed, tick and attacking hex produce an identical payload and record, and a different attacking hex deterministically changes only the origins it excludes.
- `GymHexWar` can declare the hex the player is attacking and both its control-surface tick and its rendered attack arrows honour the rule through the shipped code path (no gym-local copy of the rule), with `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` recording the surface.
- Automated tests pin: origin exclusion (frontier draw and queued attack), fallback origin, the no-exclusion regression, both `PlayScene` tick paths and the gym surface.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A hex you are attacking now defends instead of striking back, so committing to a sortie can no longer hand a neighbouring enemy hex a free hit on your held hexes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The rule lives once, in the shared pure frontier tick (`src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`), and is consumed by the game (`PlayScene`) and the gym (`GymHexWar`). The gym may not carry its own copy; a divergent harness double must record the reason in the work item and in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- **Purity and determinism.** The tick stays pure (the caller's payload is never mutated) and replayable from `(seed, tick)`. The exclusion must be derived from parameters, never from wall clock or scene state read inside the resolver, and must never consume or reorder the seeded draws in a way that breaks the "same payload ⇒ same record" property for an unchanged attacking hex.
- **No new persisted payload fields.** The attacking hex is the deployment's existing `hexId` (`HangarWarDeployment.hexId`), so nothing is added to `HangarWarPayload` and the store's field-presence migration pattern is untouched.
- **No simulated battle.** The defence stays an arithmetic comparison over stored numbers; this rule only restricts *who may launch*, never adds a battle loop.
- **Scope discipline.** Not in scope: re-balancing aggression, changing the 70 % attack chance, changing which held hex the frontier targets beyond the necessary "this target lost its only origin", or any live hex-vs-hex combat (there is none — Hex War is an algorithmic between-sortie loop).

## Existing state

- `runFrontierTick` (`src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`) runs one between-sortie tick: it redistributes aggression, resolves queued `pendingAttacks` first, then (only when nothing was queued and the seeded draw passes the 70 % attack chance) attacks **one** held, attackable hex.
- The attack origin is always derived by `attackingNeighbour(hex, hexes)` — the **most aggressive unheld neighbouring hex of the same ring**, ties settled by sorted id. `resolveAttack` uses that origin for the force (`baseAttackingForce + origin aggression × forcePerOriginAggression`) and for the attacker type (the origin's authored boss).
- `PlayScene._resolveBetweenSortieTick()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) resolves the tick from `frontierClockFor(payload)` and persists the result. It is called on the winning path from `_finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory` (before `_resolveHangarWarCapture`, deliberately, so the newly won hex cannot be attacked by the same tick) and on the losing path from the run-end handoff to `HexMapScene`. Neither path tells the tick which hex the player attacked, even though `this.hangarWarDeployment.hexId` holds exactly that.
- The tick's record is what the map renders (attack arrows plus the left-hand attack panel via `buildHexMapModel` / `renderHexMap`); `GymHexWar` renders the same shipped record and drives its `take hex → leave bot → tick` surface through the harness double `applyFakeFrontierTick` (`src/core/hangarWar/fakeFrontierClock.ts`).
- Because the winning tick resolves *before* the capture, the attacked hex is still **unheld** at tick time — i.e. exactly the kind of hex that qualifies as an attack origin today, so the reported behaviour is reproducible.

## Desired change

A new, optional input to the frontier tick: **the hex the player is currently attacking** (the deployment's target). While supplied, that hex is excluded from origin selection:

1. `attackingNeighbour` gains an optional exclusion (the attacked hex id, or a set of excluded ids) and returns the best remaining unheld neighbour, or `null` when the attacked hex was the only one.
2. `runFrontierTick` threads that exclusion through **both** launch paths — the queued (`pendingAttacks`) resolution and the frontier draw — and through the "is this hex attackable" filter used to choose the frontier's target, so a target that lost its only origin simply is not attacked this tick (the frontier may then attack a different eligible held hex, exactly as it does today when no target is attackable).
3. `FrontierTickOptions` gains a documented optional field (naming suggestion: `playerAttackingHexId?: string | null`) defaulting to `null` = today's behaviour; the record gains no new fields, because a suppressed origin produces no attack entry at all.
4. `PlayScene._resolveBetweenSortieTick()` passes `this.hangarWarDeployment?.hexId ?? null`.
5. `GymHexWar` gains a control-surface setter for the hex the player is attacking (e.g. `attackHex(hexId)` / `setPlayerAttackingHex(hexId)`), passes it to its shipped `runFrontierTick` record, and the harness double `applyFakeFrontierTick` honours the same exclusion so the gym's `tick()` surface stays consistent with the game rule.

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — add the optional exclusion to `attackingNeighbour`, thread it through `resolveAttack` / `runFrontierTick` (queued and frontier paths) and document the rule in the module header ("Who attacks, and where from").
- `src/core/hangarWar/fakeFrontierClock.ts` — mirror the exclusion in the harness tick double so the gym's control-surface tick matches the shipped rule.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_resolveBetweenSortieTick()` passes the deployment's target hex (covers both the winning and losing call sites; the doc comment on `pendingBetweenSortieTick` needs the new rationale).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — control-surface setter for the attacked hex, threaded into `shippedTickRecord()` and the harness tick; add it to the gym's documented control surface.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts` — origin exclusion, fallback origin, quiet-tick and no-exclusion regression cases.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.captureCycle.test.ts` — both tick paths pass the deployment's target hex and the recorded origins never name it.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` — the gym's attacked-hex surface and its rendered record.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2's between-sortie tick description (the "An attack is always launched from an unheld neighbouring hex" paragraph).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — `GymHexWar` row: the attacked-hex control surface and its parity status.

## Related work

- `AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88` — Pure defence resolver and frontier aggression clock (the tick and `attackingNeighbour` this changes).
- `AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP` — the between-sortie tick wired into `PlayScene`; the win-path ordering ("tick before capture") is its deliberate rule and stays.
- `AH-0MWEXI5460080WEI`, `AH-0MWEXIAEQ004IT0R`, `AH-0MWEXIHHK007H32A` — attack arrows and the left-hand attack panel that render this record.
- `AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP` — defence report rolled into the hex map (no report screen).
- `AH-0MVUXC94N008MV63`, `AH-0MWEZZDJC009FEU7` — `GymHexWar` harness and the ring-end assault surface.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — design of record for the frontier clock and the answerability rule.
- `AH-0MWEW5QCR009NX0V`, `AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG` — the hex-variety pass that recently touched the same map/tick surfaces.

## Assumptions and open questions

Applied assumptions (recommended interpretations, recorded for producer review — see the work item's comment and the Appendix):

- **A1 — Which hex.** "The hex the player is attacking" is the current deployment's target (`HangarWarDeployment.hexId`), and the rule applies to the single between-sortie tick resolved for that sortie. Hex War has no live hex-vs-hex combat for the rule to run in.
- **A2 — Both sortie endings.** The rule applies to a winning sortie (tick resolved at mini-boss defeat, before the capture) and to a losing sortie (tick resolved at run end), because the player was attacking that hex in both cases.
- **A3 — Suppress the origin, not the attack.** If another unheld neighbour exists the attack still rides from it; if none exists the target is simply not attacked this tick, consistent with the existing "unanswerable attacks are dropped" rule.
- **A4 — Queued attacks are dropped, not retried.** A `pendingAttacks` entry whose only origin is the attacked hex is consumed and dropped this tick, exactly like today's stale/unanswerable queue entries, so the queue can still never deadlock.
- **A5 — No persistence.** The exclusion is a per-tick argument; nothing is stored on the payload and no save migration is involved.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q: "Should the rule also apply to the tick resolved at the end of a **losing** sortie, or only a winning one?" — Answer: both — no producer answer available in this session. Assumption applied (recommended option): yes, both endings, because the player was attacking that hex up to the tick. Source: pending producer confirmation; ticket comment records the question.
- Q: "A queued (`pendingAttacks`) attack whose only possible origin is the attacked hex: drop it this tick, or keep it queued?" — Answer: drop it — assumption applied (recommended option): drop it, matching the shipped rule that unanswerable queue entries are consumed and never retried. Source: pending producer confirmation.
- Q: "Does the exclusion outlive the sortie (e.g. the hex stays unable to attack until the player's attack is 'spent')?" — Answer: no — assumption applied (recommended option): no, it applies to that sortie's single tick only; afterwards the hex behaves as today. Source: pending producer confirmation.
- Q: "Is Hex War a live battle in which a defending hex currently fires back?" — Answer: no — research: `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_resolveBetweenSortieTick`) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 show the frontier is an algorithmic between-sortie resolution over stored numbers, with exactly one tick per deployment. Source: repository inspection.
- Q: "Does the attacked hex currently qualify as an attack origin?" — Answer: yes — research: the winning tick resolves *before* the capture, so the attacked hex is still unheld and `attackingNeighbour` may select it (most aggressive neighbour wins). Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3864`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` (`attackingNeighbour`, `resolveAttack`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88** – Pure defence resolver and frontier aggression clock (completed)
- **AH-0MWEXI5460080WEI** – Tests: attack arrows + left-hand attack panel (model + renderer) (completed)
- **AH-0MWEXIHHK007H32A** – Renderer: draw attack arrows and the left-hand attack-details panel on the hex map (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvwzyqn8007sxig, absent, acceptance, add, added (+383 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvwzyqn8007sxig, absent, acceptance, add, added (+365 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, added, adds (+319 more)

# Strengthen a hexes defence

Problem statement: A player who owns a hex has no way to spend their banked salvage to make the bot defending it stronger. This item adds an "Upgrade Defences" flow: select a held hex on the map, open a hangar-style upgrade screen targeting that hex's bot, and spend minerals/cores on hangar-catalogue upgrades that fit the bot's ship.

## Users (with user stories)

- **Player (primary).** "When I select a hex I own, I want to send upgrades to the bot defending it, so the salvage I earned strengthens a hold I care about."
- **Player, making a purchase.** "I want to buy upgrades with minerals and/or cores from the Hangar, and only those that fit into the bot's existing ship — an upgrade to a weapon it already carries, or a new weapon in an empty slot."
- **Player, after a tick.** "I want the upgrades to stay on the bot between sorties, and to be gone for good if the hex loses its defence, so spending salvage is a real commitment."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Selecting a **held** hex on the hex map surfaces an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action; activating it opens the bot-upgrade screen for that hex's defender. An unheld hex offers no such action, and the read-only `GymHexWar` map render never offers it either.
- The bot-upgrade screen reuses the shared hangar-screen model/renderer pattern (game and `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` parity): it lists the hangar-catalogue entries (weapons, hulls and modifiers) and shows each one's fit verdict for the focused bot — **upgrade existing** (the bot already carries the weapon → raise its level), **add to empty slot** (a weapon kind the bot does not carry → offered **only** when the bot has a free permanent slot), **re-hull** (a hull entry), **train** (a modifier entry), or a disabled reason (slot pool full / unaffordable / ring-gated). No second, drifting copy of the fit rule exists.
- A purchase is paid for in minerals and/or cores from the fleet's banked salvage (the hangar wallet, `HangarState.bankedMinerals`/`bankedCores`), spends exactly the displayed price, and applies the upgrade to the bot's ship: a new weapon kind occupies one permanent slot at level 1, an already-carried weapon rises one level, a hull entry swaps the bot's `hullId` (keeping the existing carried loadout), and a modifier entry applies its effect to the bot. The fleet's owned sets, active hull/loadout and the player's deployed ship are untouched by a bot purchase.
- Weapon upgrades follow a **per-level upgrade price** (Q9 = B): a separate, authored upgrade-price rule for raising an already-carried weapon's level, distinct from the catalogue entry's purchase price for a new kind; both are documented in one pricing table.
- The bot's defence rating reflects the sent upgrades through the **one** existing rating formula (`defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / the `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` mapping); a purchase returns a fresh payload with the defender's stored `defenceRating` recomputed and re-persisted, never a second derivation.
- Upgrade state persists on the `HexDefender` across between-sortie ticks and save/load round-trips (additive optional fields, field-presence migration, same pattern as `skills`), and is destroyed with the bot when its hex falls in a defence tick (existing `applyDefence` path — a fallen hex loses its defender).
- Tests cover: the fit rule (upgrade-existing vs add-to-empty-slot vs re-hull vs train vs disabled states), purchase economics (price, per-level upgrade price, wallet deduction, refused purchases), snapshot update + rating recompute, persistence round-trip and fall-destruction, corruption tolerance of the stored upgrade state, the map action surface and the gym parity assertion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` for the new bot-upgrade control surface.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can now spend earned minerals and cores to send hangar upgrades — weapons, hulls and modifiers — to a bot defending a hex they own, and read the strengthened rating on the map; giving the hangar economy a second, defence-shaped sink.

## Constraints

- **Pure and injectable:** the fit rule, purchase application and rating recompute live in the pure core (hangar economy / a new `botUpgrade` module), no Phaser, no storage access; scenes only present and persist.
- **Same-data-model rule (producer Q2):** the bot uses the same ship data model as a player-controlled ship — the permanent slot model (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` = 6 shared weapon/power-up slots) and the victory-snapshot vocabulary from `AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ` (`DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`: permanent weapon levels, power-up levels, consumable pools). The bot is never flown; its loadout is stored data that feeds the one rating formula.
- **Hangar catalogue entries (producer Q3):** the upgrade pool is the shipped `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` — **weapons, hulls and modifiers** (producer Q10 = "everything") — no new economy, no new currency; ring gating and prices reused as authored, plus the new per-level weapon-upgrade price (Q9 = B).
- **Slot-fit rule (producer Q8 = A):** a weapon the bot does **not** already own is offered **only** when the bot has an empty permanent slot; a weapon the bot already carries is always offered as a level-upgrade. Hulls and modifiers have no slot requirement (a hull swaps `hullId`, a modifier applies its effect).
- **One interaction (producer Q4):** an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action in the hex summary section opens a version of the player-ship upgrade scene (the hangar screen) scoped to the bot — same screen pattern, different purchase target.
- **Destruction (producer Q5):** upgrades are persistent **unless** the hex loses a defence tick, which destroys the bot (today's `applyDefence` already unholds the hex and drops its defender; nothing new to build there).
- **Rating (producer Q6):** upgrades change the stored `defenceRating`, recomputed through the single shipped formula.
- **No player-ship effect (producer Q7):** a bot purchase never touches the player's deployed ship, active loadout or the fleet's owned sets.
- **No schema version bump:** new optional fields read by field presence, matching `skills` / `frontierTick`.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `HexDefender` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is a derived-rating record — `hullId`, `defenceRating`, `bankedMinerals`, optional `skills` — with no weapon slots or upgrade levels. It is never flown; every defence is arithmetic over stored numbers.
- The sibling item (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ) lands the bot ship-model vocabulary in the economy: `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`, `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` (one frozen row per `WeaponId`/`PowerUpId`), `defenderStatBuckets`, `snapshotDefenderUpgrades`, and `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` — already merged (commits `46d217b5`, `58dc8edc`). Its capture-cycle threading is being delivered through its own child items (e.g. AH-0MWHF6ZHW0058SMX); **this item depends on that snapshot existing on `HexDefender`** (dependency edge recorded).
- The player-ship slot model is the permanent six-slot pool shared by weapons and power-ups (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` in `src/core/constants.ts`, `capDropIdsToSlotPool` in `src/powerups/slots.ts`).
- The hangar economy (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) owns prices, `canBuy`/`buy`, `purchaseWeight`, ring gating and `resolvePlayerStrength`; the catalogue (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) holds hulls, starting weapons and modifiers with two-currency prices.
- The hangar screen (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) is the pure model + one renderer used by the shipped hangar scene **and** `GymHangar`; the hex map (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` + `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) renders focused-hex intel in the right-hand detail panel, with held hexes selectable but not actionable.
- Defence ticks (`runFrontierTick` → `applyDefence`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`) already destroy a fallen hex's defender (`held=false`, `defender=null`).

## Desired change

1. **Bot ship model.** `HexDefender` carries the shipped upgrade-snapshot vocabulary (permanent weapon/power-up levels, consumable pools) as additive optional fields, alongside the existing hull/rating/skills — the same-data-model rule (Q2). The bot's slot occupancy derives from the stored levels against `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
2. **Fit rule (pure).** A new pure function answers, per catalogue entry and per defender: `upgrade-existing` (bot already carries the weapon → level +1), `add-to-empty-slot` (new weapon kind, **only when a free slot exists**), `re-hull` (hull entry, no slot requirement), `train` (modifier entry, no slot requirement), or a disabled reason (slot pool full, unaffordable in either currency, ring-gated). The fit rule and the hangar's `canBuy` combine into one verdict per row.
3. **Per-level weapon-upgrade price (Q9 = B).** One authored table defines the upgrade price for raising an already-carried weapon's level (distinct from the catalogue's new-kind purchase price). Both prices appear on the row and are paid from the hangar wallet.
4. **Purchase application (pure).** Spending the displayed price applies the upgrade to the defender's ship: a new weapon kind enters at level 1 in one permanent slot, an already-carried weapon rises one level, a hull entry swaps `hullId` keeping the carried loadout, a modifier entry applies its effect; `defenceRating` recomputes through `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / the buckets mapping — one formula (Q6). A refused purchase returns the payload unchanged.
5. **Map action.** The held-hex detail panel (the "hex summary section") gains an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action; `HexMapScene` wires it to open the bot-upgrade screen for the focused defender (Q4). Unheld hexes offer nothing; the gym's read-only render (no handlers) offers nothing — parity by construction.
6. **Bot-upgrade screen.** A hangar-screen-style scene scoped to one defender: same pure model + one renderer shape as `hangarScreen`, showing the fit verdicts, both price kinds and the bot's current loadout/rating; purchases return a fresh payload that the scene persists. Game and gym (if exercised) share the model/renderer so they cannot drift.
7. **Persistence and destruction.** Purchases persist via the versioned store (additive optional fields, field-presence parse). A defence-tick fall destroys the bot including its upgrades through the existing `applyDefence` path (Q5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HexDefender` gains additive optional upgrade-snapshot fields (weapon/power-up levels, consumable pools) mirroring `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/botUpgrade.ts` (new) — the pure fit rule, the per-level upgrade-price table (Q9 = B), purchase application and per-row verdict for a defender's upgrade options (own module so the scenes never derive a fit).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — any shared helper the purchase needs (wallet spend, snapshot → rating via existing `defenderRatingFromSnapshot`).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parse/round-trip of the new optional fields (field presence).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` and `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the held-hex `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action row + activation wiring in the detail panel.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — handler wiring (`onUpgradeDefences(hexId)` → open the bot-upgrade screen) and the route back after a purchase.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/botUpgradeScreen.ts` (new) + `src/scenes/hangarWar/botUpgradeScene.ts` (or a mode of the existing hangar screen) — the pure model + one renderer for the bot-upgrade screen.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` (and `GymHangar` if it renders the upgrade screen) — parity/no handlers for the new surface.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, README — the new control surface and its parity entry.

## Related work

- **Hangar War: leave the defending bot with the run's permanent upgrades (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ)** — dependency: supplies the `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot` model, the stat-bucket mapping and the snapshot-aware rating this item's purchases consume; its capture-cycle threading first puts the snapshot on `HexDefender`.
- Hangar economy and unlock tree (AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6) — owns `canBuy`/`buy`, prices and ring gating the purchase path reuses.
- Capture cycle — hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6) — the module that creates `HexDefender`s.
- Hex-map intel / map screen (AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2) — the detail panel that gains the `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action.
- Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with special skills (AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1) — precedent for additive optional defender fields and the skills pattern (modifier `train` applies here).
- Versioned `ai_hell_hangar_war` store with migration (AH-0MVUXC0M5007LCGV) — the back-compat pattern new optional fields follow.
- Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP) — the tick path that destroys a fallen bot (Q5).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk (highest):** spendable upgrades let a player push a held hex's rating high, making well-defended hexes mathematically unretakeable — the same accepted consequence as the sibling item's Q3 = A. *Mitigation:* one rating formula and one mapping table, so a follow-up tuning item can cap or rescale prices without touching saves; measure from real runs before filing.
- **Pricing granularity risk (Q9 = B):** the per-level weapon-upgrade price is new authored data; its exact progression is a balance knob. *Mitigation:* one documented table in `botUpgrade.ts`, authorable without code changes; defaults chosen conservatively at implement time and reviewed in the effort/risk notes.
- **Dependency risk:** the brief assumes the sibling's snapshot-on-`HexDefender` threading lands first. If it slips, this item's data model cannot build. *Mitigation:* dependency edge recorded; implement after the sibling's capture threading.
- **Save-compatibility risk:** new optional fields must be omitted when empty and parsed defensively, or existing saves/fixtures drift. *Mitigation:* the `skills` pattern exactly; store round-trip + pre-change-save tests.
- **Wallet-conflict risk:** bot purchases spend the same banked minerals/cores the player uses for fleet unlocks — a bot spend can starve the hangar. *Deliberate per Q3/Q8 (A):* catalogue-priced, shared wallet; documented rather than gated in this item.
- **Modifier-fit risk (Q10 = everything):** a modifier whose effect targets run stats (e.g. `extra-lives`) has no bot meaning; only modifier effects with a stored-bot effect (e.g. `defence-skill`) can be sent. *Mitigation:* the fit rule classifies modifier effects by whether they change stored defender data; `extra-lives`-style effects are shown disabled with a reason rather than silently charged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** candidates deliberately excluded — a bot that is actually flown in combat, any new currency, new catalogue entries, and any change to player-ship progression or the frontier tuning constants. Each excluded candidate must become its own work item rather than growing this one.
- **Assumption (Q8, A):** the upgrade screen offers every catalogue entry the fleet can afford (ring + wallet gating), subject to the slot-fit rule for new weapons; a purchase spends banked salvage without granting the fleet an unlock — the bot gets the entry, the fleet does not.
- **Assumption (Q9, B):** a per-level upgrade-price table governs raising an already-carried weapon's level; a new weapon kind pays the catalogue purchase price and enters at level 1, occupying one permanent slot when one is free.
- **Assumption:** "permanent slots" for the bot mean the shared six-slot weapon/power-up pool (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`), counted by distinct permanently-carried kinds — the bot's stored data, never a live battle.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What does 'send upgrades for the ship' mean?" — **Answer (operator):** upgrade the **defending bot** (the bot left in the hex). *Source:* interactive reply.
- Q2 — "Does the bot get its own slot system?" — **Answer (operator):** the bot should be the **same as a player-controlled ship**, using the same data model so it has **slots etc.** *Research:* `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (six shared weapon/power-up slots) and the sibling item's `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot` are the vocabularies this maps onto.
- Q3 — "What counts as an upgrade the player can send?" — **Answer (operator):** **hangar catalogue entries**, purchased with minerals and/or cores from the Hangar. *Research:* `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` + `canBuy`/`buy` already implement two-currency, ring-gated purchases.
- Q4 — "What's the UI interaction?" — **Answer (operator):** add an **"upgrade defenses" button to the hex summary section**, which opens **a version of the player-ship upgrade scene (hangar)** but upgrades the bot instead of the player's ship.
- Q5 — "Persistence and limits?" — **Answer (operator):** **persistent unless it loses a defence tick, in which case it is destroyed** (matches today's `applyDefence`: a fallen hex unholds and drops its defender).
- Q6 — "How does the upgrade affect the bot's defence?" — **Answer (operator):** it **changes the defence rating** (recomputed through the one shipped formula).
- Q7 — "Does sending upgrades affect the player's ship?" — **Answer (operator):** **no**.
- Q8 — "Which catalogue entries can the player send?" — **Answer (operator):** **A** — every catalogue entry the fleet can afford, spending banked salvage without granting the fleet an unlock — **refined**: a weapon the bot does **not** already own is offered **only** when the bot has an **empty slot**. *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).
- Q9 — "How does 'upgrade to an existing weapon' price?" — **Answer (operator):** **B** — a **separate per-level upgrade price** (its own authored pricing table), distinct from the catalogue purchase price for a new kind. *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).
- Q10 — "Which catalogue kinds are in scope?" — **Answer (operator):** **everything** — weapons, hulls and modifiers are all sendable (each with its own fit rule; hulls re-hull, modifiers apply their stored effect). *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).

# Author shipped hex variety content on ring 2 (personalities, contracts, landmarks)

## Problem statement

As a player pushing into later rings, I want the **shipped** rings to actually
author hex variety, so the shipped machinery delivers the variety it was built
for instead of living only in the ring-3 verification sample. Today the shipped
table (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` + `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv`)
authors **no** variety, so no shipped hex offers a personality, a contract or a
landmark.

## Users (with example user stories)

- **The returning ring-2 player** — "I've captured hexes in every prong of ring
  1; I want at least one ring-2 hex to fight differently, one to offer a
  worthwhile optional objective, and one set-piece that asks for a real
  decision, otherwise the ring is the same chores at an angrier number."
- **The strategist** — "I want to read each hex's personality, contract and
  landmark in the map's known-ahead intel before I commit a life, so the
  variety informs my choice instead of gambling it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- `hex-r2-1` (the-siege-leviathan) authors the `nebula` personality, `hex-r2-6`
  (cobalt-siege) authors a contract (objective "Break the siege line then hold
  the hex", bonus +100 salvage / +1 core), and `hex-r2-7` (the-static-prophet)
  authors the `fortress` landmark — all in `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`,
  mirrored byte-for-value in `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv` (CSV-seed parity test
  green). Ring 1 stays the plain tutorial ring (no variety authored).
- `validateRingDefinitions(2, HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS)` stays green, and a
  shipped-data test asserts `buildHexMapModel` publishes the authored
  personality (id + projectile-drag mechanic), the contract (objective, bonus,
  `open` status) and the landmark (type + fortress progress `0/2`) before
  commitment.
- Ring 2's authored `baseAggression` values are unchanged (`2, 2, 5, 2, 5, 2, 2,
  5, 6, 2, 5, 8`); the three variety hexes stay at the aggression-2 survivable
  floor and their personalities/landmarks add no aggression step; `hex-r2-12`
  remains the ring's strict weapon/aggression maximum.
- The `nebula` personality is genuinely felt: it sits on a weapon-granting hex
  (`hex-r2-1` grants `arc`), so the boss's demonstrated volley is slowed by the
  shared drag factor (no new code path).
- The ring-timing evaluation is re-run and recorded; the ring-2 measurement and
  the authored aggression band are unchanged (variety data does not feed the
  harness).
- GDD §8.2 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` name the shipped variety hexes
  and what each authors.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players will finally meet the variety the Hangar War was built for on the ring
they actually grind: `hex-r2-1` fights differently (a drifting slow `arc`
volley), `hex-r2-6` offers an optional contract for extra banked salvage, and
`hex-r2-7` is a fortress capture that needs two passes.

## Constraints

- **Data change only.** Extend `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` and mirror it in
  `hex-ring-2.csv`. The vocabulary, loud validation, known-ahead intel,
  resolvers, persistence and docs already ship — no new code path is expected.
- **Existing economy.** Contract and cache rewards use the shipped currencies
  through `bankSalvage`; no new currency and no special-mission-style reward
  (those stay with AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55). The +100/+1 contract bonus sits below
  the 140-salvage cache payout.
- **Survivable band.** The three variety hexes are aggression-2 survivors; no
  `berserker` personality (it adds an aggression step) may be placed on one.
- **Mechanic visibility.** `nebula` only tunes the boss's demonstrated volley,
  so it must sit on a weapon-granting hex — it does (`hex-r2-1` grants `arc`).
- **One weapon hex.** `hex-r2-12` (`nova`) stays the single, strict hardest
  weapon hex; a `cache` can never be the weapon hex (already validated).
- **Leave the special mission alone.** `hex-r2-3` already authors the
  `isSpecialMission` + `hull-3` reward; do not stack a landmark/contract on it.
- **Gym↔game parity.** No scene change expected; if any is needed it must land
  in the shared core, never a per-scene copy.
- **CSV safety.** The contract objective contains no comma, so the seed stays
  unquoted and parseable.

## Existing state

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` authors rings 1 (6) and 2 (12) only, with no
  `personality`/`contract`/`landmark` on any row; `hex-ring-1.csv` and
  `hex-ring-2.csv` mirror it with empty variety columns.
- `VARIETY_RING_DEFINITIONS` in `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`
  is the authored **ring-3 sample** showing the intended shape (five
  personalities incl. both bounded mechanics, two contracts, one fortress, one
  cache) — fixture data, not shipped content.
- `validateRingDefinitions` already rejects unknown ids, malformed contracts,
  cache-on-weapon-hex and duplicate set-pieces; `buildHexMapModel` /
  `buildHexIntel` already publish personality/contract/landmark intel.
- Ring 2 aggressions `2,2,5,2,5,2,2,5,6,2,5,8` are pinned by
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC band). The
  ring-timing baseline (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`,
  `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`) does not model variety, so authoring it does
  not move the measured number.
- `hex-r2-3` is ring 2's authored special mission (`hull-3`).

## Desired change

Author variety on three distinct ring-2 hexes, all at the aggression-2
survivable floor (producer-confirmed 2026-11-15, Q1 = a, Q2 = a, Q3 = a):

| Hex | Aggression | Authored axis | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hex-r2-1` (the-siege-leviathan) | 2 | `personality` | `nebula` — shared projectile-drag mechanic; the hex grants `arc`, so its demonstrated volley drifts slow (≈61 % speed, `NEBULA_PROJECTILE_DRAG 1.65`) |
| `hex-r2-6` (cobalt-siege) | 2 | `contract` | objective "Break the siege line then hold the hex"; +100 salvage, +1 core, banked on capture via `bankSalvage` |
| `hex-r2-7` (the-static-prophet) | 2 | `landmark` | `fortress` — two capture passes (`FORTRESS_CAPTURE_PASSES = 2`), keeps its `extra-life` grant |

Ring 1 stays plain. No `baseAggression`, grant, boss or weaknesses change on any
row; only the three variety fields are added.

## Key Files

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — add the variety fields to three ring-2 rows.
- `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv` — mirror the same values in the seed columns.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — add shipped-data assertions that the
  authored variety is present and published.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — validation only; no code change expected.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — no change expected; read model already
  publishes the axes.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2 *Hex variety*) — name the shipped
  variety hexes.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — record which shipped hexes author variety.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` + `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — re-measure and
  record (expected unchanged).

## Related work

- discovered-from: AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG (hex variety epic — machinery shipped and
  verified against the ring-3 sample).
- AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7 — data vocabulary, fixtures and loud validation.
- AH-0MWEW50B10089D4W — personality axis (config-tunes + two shared mechanics).
- AH-0MWEW58WD003NFXS — contract axis.
- AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH — ring landmarks axis.
- AH-0MWEW73WS003QFV7 — epic end-to-end verification.
- AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC — ring 2 survivable aggression band.
- AH-0MWF0CTQB001XFE1 — the authored ring-2 special mission (`hex-r2-3`).
- AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55 — special missions (special rewards stay there).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk** — the personality/fortress could lengthen the three survivor
  hexes. Mitigation: all three sit at the aggression-2 floor, `nebula` slows the
  boss volley (player-friendly), no reward is removed (`fortress` keeps
  `extra-life`), and the contract bonus is modest (+100/+1).
- **Visibility risk** — a demonstrated-volley-only personality on an
  upgrade-granting hex would be invisible; `hex-r2-1` grants `arc`, so the
  mechanic is felt.
- **Scope-creep risk** — richer variety (more hexes, ring 1 variety, a `cache`,
  new mechanics) is out of scope for the minimum; record it as linked follow-up
  work, not additions here.
- **Assumption** — the ring-timing measurement is unaffected because the harness
  does not consume variety fields; verified by re-running and recording.
- **Assumption** — `hex-r2-1`/`hex-r2-6`/`hex-r2-7` are the confirmed hexes; the
  producer approved them as the recommendation's concrete examples.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: "Q1 — Content scope: one personality + one contract + one landmark on
  ring-2 hexes, ring 1 plain? (a) suggested minimum, (b) richer spread, (c) exact
  table" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-15): **(a) suggested minimum** — one of each
  on three distinct ring-2 hexes, ring 1 plain. Source: interactive reply on
  AH-0MWH4F375000X08G comment AH-C0MWHC11BN001YSIH.
- Q: "Q2 — Personality choice: (a) `nebula` shared mechanic on a weapon-granting
  survivor, (b) config-tune, (c) `berserker`, (d) implementer picks" — Answer
  (producer, 2026-11-15): **(a) `nebula`** on `hex-r2-1` (grants `arc`,
  aggression 2). Source: interactive reply, same comment.
- Q: "Q3 — Landmark choice: (a) `fortress` keeping the hex's grant, (b) `cache`
  payout, (c) either" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-15): **(a) `fortress`** on
  `hex-r2-7` (keeps `extra-life`). Source: interactive reply, same comment.

Research summary: the intended shape was read from the item's own "Suggested
minimum shape (producer to confirm)" plus the ring-3 fixture sample
(`VARIETY_RING_DEFINITIONS`); ring-2 aggressions are pinned by
`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC); `hexBoss.ts` shows
`nebula` tunes only the demonstrated volley, hence the weapon-granting-hex
constraint; the ring-timing harness (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) does not read
variety fields, so the measured baseline is expected to be unchanged.

# Hangar UI: buy to upgrade owned weapons and power-ups

## Problem statement

The hangar economy today treats every catalogue entry as **binary ownership**: `canBuy`/`buy` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) spend minerals/cores to add an entry id to the owned sets (`unlockedHulls`, `unlockedWeapons`, `ownedModifiers`), and an entry the fleet already owns is refused with `owned`. There is **no path for the player to buy an upgrade** — i.e. spend hangar currency to raise the **permanent level** of an already-owned weapon or power-up — even though permanent levels are the run's own vocabulary (`Player.getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()`, and `PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()`), and even though the capture cycle now carries exactly those permanent levels onto the defending bot (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ). The existing Hangar screen (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`, `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts`) renders unlock rows whose `HangarUnlockState` ends at `owned` (`BUY` / `OWNED` / `RING 2` / `NEED N min`) with no upgrade action.

## Goal (user story)

As a player in the hangar, I want to spend my banked minerals/cores on upgrading weapons and power-ups I already own — raising their permanent level — so the hangar is a place to grow my fleet between sorties, and so the bot I leave behind in a hex (which keeps my permanent upgrades at capture time, AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ) can be strengthened from the hangar, not only by what I happen to collect in a run.

## Impact

Players can spend banked minerals/cores in the hangar to permanently upgrade the **weapons** they already own, so the fleet grows between sorties and a captured defender inherits the upgraded permanent levels. Power-up upgrades are deferred to AH-0MWKT12BT001106T (a hangar power-up's first permanent level row has no shipped acquisition source yet), so only weapons are upgradeable in play for now.

## Design constraints (bear in mind — do NOT implement here)

This item must NOT be implemented as part of AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ; that epic only ships the **capture-side** snapshot. This item is filed so the code and UI design of the upgrade path stays compatible with what that epic introduced:

- The upgrade path should feed the **same** permanent-level model the snapshot reads: `Player.getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` (permanent components only; temporary/timed stacks must never be purchasable) and the consumable pool state (`PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()`).
- Upgrade **pricing/gating** should extend the existing economy's rule set (`canBuy` precedence `owned → gated → unaffordable`, ring gating via `minRing`, two-currency `HangarPrice`) rather than introduce a parallel purchase rule; a deliberately separate item because "buy another level" changes the `owned` refusal semantics into an upgrade-branch of the economy.
- The hangar screen's unlock rows should gain an upgrade affordance for owned rows without breaking the existing `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING 2`/`NEED N min` rendering or the attract-mode booth (cheapest-useful-unlock) decision (`decideHangarAction`).
- Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md): the upgrade rule must live in the pure economy (no Phaser, no storage), consumed by `HangarScene` and `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` alike; no divergent copy.
- A defender captured after an upgrade must persist the **already-upgraded** permanent levels (no extra storage change needed: the capture read happens at victory time; the upgrade just means the accessors return higher levels).

## Assumptions (to confirm during planning)

- The upgrade ceiling/cap (`max level` refusal) comes from the **existing** permanent-level ceiling used by the run upgrade path, not a new parallel number; the economy rule reads the same ceiling.
- The per-level price curve (e.g. a scaling multiplier per level) is left to implementation but must be deterministic and use the existing two-currency `HangarPrice` conventions.
- `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` are suggested names; the contract (pure, non-mutating, refusal on unknown/unowned/temporary/capped ids) is the requirement, not the names.
- Scope-creep guard: reward-axis purchases into a held hex (AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ) and hull upgrade bays (AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY) are **out of scope** here — this item only converts an already-owned weapon/power-up into a higher permanent level.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Economy rule.** `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` gains a pure upgrade rule (e.g. `costToUpgrade` / `buyUpgrade` beside `canBuy`/`buy`): given an owned weapon/power-up id and current permanent levels, it returns a two-currency price (using the existing `HangarPrice`/ring-gating conventions, with an explicit cap/ceiling so an already-maxed kind is refused), never mutates its inputs, and refuses unknown/unowned/temporary ids.
2. **Persistence.** Buying an upgrade raises the **permanent** level (weapon level / power-up level) in the same persisted state `getWeaponLevels()`/`getPowerUpLevels()` read, survives a save/load round-trip and a replay, and never touches temporary/timed stacks (`getTempWeaponIds()`/`getTempPowerUpIds()` stay empty after a purchase). The persisted state carries level rows for both kinds; only weapons have an in-play source of that first row in this epic (see AC3).
3. **UI affordance (weapons).** The hangar screen's owned row for a level-bearing **weapon** shows the current level and an upgrade action with its price (e.g. `UPGRADE · 25 min`), disabled visibly when the player cannot afford it or the kind is capped; the existing `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING 2`/`NEED N min` rows for non-upgradeable kinds are byte-identical to today. The renderer stays generic so a power-up level row renders identically once one exists, but this epic adds no power-up acquisition surface — power-up owned rows are deferred to AH-0MWKT12BT001106T.
4. **Capture integration.** A capture resolves against the upgraded permanent levels: a hex captured after the player buys upgrades leaves a defender whose `upgradeSnapshot`/`defenceRating` reflect the higher levels (asserted through the shared capture path, AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ).
5. **Parity and tests.** The upgrade rule is exercised by both `HangarScene` and the gym harness through the one pure economy function (no second derivation; duplicate-body guard green), and unit tests cover: price, cap refusal at max, unaffordable, unknown/unowned/temporary refusal, save/load round-trip, and the capture integration assertion.
6. **Docs.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 / the hangar section and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D record the buy-to-upgrade path as the intended upgrade source (distinct from the run-economy pickup path), and any code comment that says upgrades come only from runs is corrected.
7. **Full suite green.** Full project test suite passes with the change (via the test skill; the dev-push gate enforces it).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — the pure upgrade rule + price/gating/cap (extending the existing economy conventions).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` — economy tests.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — owned-row upgrade affordance + level display (shared renderer).
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — buy-to-upgrade handler persisting via the store.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` (or the shared hangar harness) — gym parity.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` / the permanent weapon-level store — the permanent-level grant seam a purchase writes through.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — the upgrade-source rule.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ** (this item is discovered-from) — capture-side: the defending bot keeps the run's permanent upgrades; the upgrade-buy path must feed the same permanent-level model.
- **AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6** — Hangar economy and unlock tree (completed; owns `canBuy`/`buy`, `resolvePlayerStrength`, the weights).
- **AH-0MWUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed; the hangar link A5).
- **AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ** — Strengthen a hexes defence (open; map-purchase flow for *sending* upgrades into a held hex, related but separate purchase surface).
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY** — Post-MVP hull upgrade bays as a reward axis (open; the hull-side upgrade concept — watch for overlap when hull upgrades become purchasable).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** – Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons in the loadout (default weapon only) (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1** – Hangar scene: unlock tree and deployment/loadout selector (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6** – Hangar economy and unlock tree (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mweusvj1007exjy, acceptance, accessors, action, add (+294 more)
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accessors, action, add, afford (+275 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: acceptance, accessors, action, add, agents (+240 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required — the seed context (discovered-from epic AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ, the existing economy/screen code, and completed precedent AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6 / AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1) already specified the problem, constraints and measurable acceptance criteria. Answer (Map, intake agent): proceeded without interview. Research: inspected `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` (canBuy `owned → gated → unaffordable`, `HangarPrice`, `minRing`) and `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (`HangarUnlockState`, `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING 2`/`NEED N min` rendering); find-related report at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU.md`.
- Q: "Upgrade ceiling/cap source: the item assumes the max-level refusal cap comes from an existing permanent-level ceiling in the run path. None exists (weapon levels unbounded per `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`; power-up levels unbounded above; `isPowerUpAtDiscreteCap` is a gym disable rule, false for continuous-only kinds). Where does the cap come from?" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-15): **option (a)** — introduce **one shared, documented max-permanent-level ceiling constant** (e.g. `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL`) read by both the run-path level-up offer and the hangar economy; deterministic cap refusal in the pure economy; preserves the "no parallel number" intent by single-sourcing the number. Research: `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` ("levels are unbounded but the value never exceeds a finite cap"), `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` (`isPowerUpAtDiscreteCap`, unbounded levels). Final: (a).
- Q: "Which owned kinds are upgradeable? Consumables (shield, phase_shift, teleport, force_field, mystery_ufo, thorns) never level up in the run path (charges, not levels); extra_life is field-pickup-only." — Answer (producer, 2026-11-15): **option (a)** — the upgrade rule applies to **level-bearing permanent kinds only** (weapons + non-consumable power-ups: bomb, speed_boost, magnet, mineral_scoop, smart_bomb, frenzy, chrono, salvage, strike, mining_laser); consumables/field-pickup-only kinds are refused as non-upgradeable (no permanent level to raise) and their rows stay byte-identical; charge purchases stay out of scope. Research: `src/powerups/types.ts` `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` consumable/fieldPickupOnly flags; `src/powerups/choice.ts` charge-vs-level offer dispatch. Final: (a).
- **Producer decision (2026-11-17) — re-scope: weapons only, power-ups deferred.** Asked to choose between answering the power-up ownership questions (Q1/Q2/Q3 on AH-0MWKT12BT001106T) and re-scoping this epic, the producer chose the re-scope. This epic therefore delivers the weapon half of buy-to-upgrade only: the pure rule (C2), persistence + deploy grants (C3) and capture integration (C5) are already on `dev`, and the remaining children (C4 affordance, C6 docs, C7 verification) cover weapons. The renderer/model stays generic so a power-up level row would render the same affordance, but no power-up acquisition surface (ring grants, catalogue entries, an `unlockedPowerUps` set, a power-up purchase branch) is added here. Hangar power-up ownership and its upgrade path remain open, standalone, in AH-0MWKT12BT001106T (its dependency edge from C4 was removed; its Q1/Q2/Q3 still need an answer before that item can be dispatched).

# Intake brief — Hangar Map UI: clearer overview (AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK)

## Headline

The Hangar War map's right-hand detail panel (`SELECTED HEX — FULL INTEL`) prints
the selected hex's known-ahead intel as an unlabelled monospace dump — lines such
as `S:waveLaser`, `W:waveLaser`, `→extra-life`, `bot hull-1 (2)` and
`atk 10 vs 2 · FALLS` — so the player cannot tell what each item is. Add clear
titles to every line item of the selected-hex overview so it is self-explanatory
at a glance.

## Problem statement

The overview of the selected hex in the Hangar War map is unclear: the detail
panel juxtaposes raw values and acronyms without labels, alternating cryptic
abbreviations (`S:`, `W:`, `→`, `bot`, `atk`) with bare values (the boss name is
printed with no title at all). A player reading the panel must already know the
design's abbreviations to decode the intel the map exists to show.

## Users

- **The Hangar War player** planning the next deployment from the map.
  - *As a player, I want the selected hex's overview to label each item — boss,
    strengths, weaknesses, grant, defender, pending attack — so I can read the
    intel without decoding abbreviations.*
  - *As a returning player, I want the tile labels I have learned (`AGG n`,
    ownership marker, `(q,r)` coordinates) to stay unchanged, so the map itself
    still reads the way I expect.*
  - *As a player using the `GymHexWar` parity gym, I want the titled overview to
    be the same code the game renders, so the gym remains a faithful capture of
    the shipped map.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Titles on every selected-hex line item (shared `hexLabel`).** The detail
  panel text (`hexLabel`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) labels every line of
  the selected hex's overview — hex id, state (held/unheld), aggression, boss,
  strengths, weaknesses, grant, defender, defender skills and pending attack —
  replacing the cryptic `S:`, `W:`, `→`, `bot` and `atk` prefixes with explicit
  capitalised titles (e.g. `BOSS:`, `STRENGTHS:`, `WEAKNESSES:`, `GRANT:`,
  `DEFENDER:`, `SKILL:`, `PENDING ATTACK:`). The already-headed sections
  (SPECIAL MISSION, REWARD, PERSONALITY, MECHANIC, LANDMARK, CONTRACT, BONUS)
  keep their existing titles unchanged.
- **Game/gym parity, single shared change.** The titles land in the shared
  `hexLabel`/`renderHexMap` path, so the shipped `HexMapScene` and the
  `GymHexWar` parity gym render the same titled overview; there is no
  gym-local or game-local copy of the panel text.
- **Tile labels unchanged.** The on-tile `AGG n` badge, ownership marker and
  `(q,r)` coordinates (AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U) are not modified by this item; only
  the detail-panel text changes.
- **Regression coverage updated.** Tests asserting the old abbreviations
  (`W:…`, `→…`, `bot …`, `atk …`) are updated to the titled format in
  `hexIntel.test.ts`, `HexMapScene.test.ts` and `GymHexWar.test.ts`; the panel
  still shows the focused hex's id, boss, strengths, weaknesses, grant, defender
  and pending attack, and the panel default/follow-focus behaviour is unchanged.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, the `hexIntel.ts` header narrative, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and the
  detail-panel narrative in `docs/Game Design Document.md` (CHANGELOG.md is
  excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can read the selected hex's overview and understand every item at a
glance, instead of decoding cryptic abbreviations.

## Constraints

- The panel is a 260px-wide right-hand monospace band (12px body, lineSpacing 4,
  `PANEL_X = GAME_WIDTH − 260`); titles must fit or word-wrap inside that band.
- The panel already uses the CVD-safe orange/blue pair for text colour; no
  colour changes are required (ownership is already conveyed by the held/unheld
  words and tile markers).
- The left-hand `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` panel renders the defence report model's
  own rows (`DefenceReportRow.label`) and is **out of scope** unless the producer
  opts in (see Appendix open question).
- Existing separator glyphs (·, →, ★) and the panel's title-case heading style
  (e.g. `SPECIAL MISSION`) are the convention to match.

## Existing state

The panel text is `hexLabel` (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts:887`): a raw line
dump — `<hex id>`, `HELD|UNHELD · AGG n [!force]`, `<boss-name>` (unlabelled),
`S:<strengths>`, `W:<weaknesses>`, `→<grant>`, `bot <hull> (<rating>)`,
`skill <name> +n vs <boss>`, `atk <a> vs <d> · HOLDS|FALLS`, followed by the
already-headed SPECIAL MISSION / PERSONALITY / LANDMARK / CONTRACT sections.
Both the game (`HexMapScene.renderHexMap`) and the gym (`GymHexWar`) render this
same text.

## Desired change

Only the detail-panel text changes: give every unlabelled line an explicit
capitalised title in the existing panel style (`ID:`, `STATE:`,
`AGGRESSION:`, `BOSS:`, `STRENGTHS:`, `WEAKNESSES:`, `GRANT:`, `DEFENDER:`,
`SKILL:`, `PENDING ATTACK:`), keep the already-headed variety sections as-is,
and update the consuming tests and doc narratives to the titled format. No
layout, focus, navigation or model change.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (medium risk).** The tiles, layout, focus model and the left-hand
  attack panel are all tempting polish targets, but this item is deliberately
  panel-text-only; extra opportunities (e.g. titling the attack report rows,
  reformatting the panel) belong in linked work items, not this one (see
  Appendix Q3).
- **Test/documentation churn (low risk).** Several suites assert the old
  abbreviated substrings; they must be updated in the same change or the dev
  push gate trips. The change touches only string content, so behavioural tests
  (focus, default hex, panel-follows-focus) are unaffected.
- **Width regression (low risk).** Longer titled lines could wrap inside the
  260px band; the body already has `lineSpacing` set and the panel has vertical
  room, but the implementer should eyeball `GymHexWar`'s read-only render.
- **Assumption (pending producer review):** titles apply to every
  non-self-explanatory line of the selected-hex overview; wording follows the
  existing `TITLE: value` heading style (Appendix Q1/Q2).

## Key Files:

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — `hexLabel` (+ panel-title constants) produces the detail-panel text; add explicit titles per line, keep headed sections.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — update `label` assertions (e.g. lines ~286–297, ~333, ~380–428, ~620, ~655) to the titled format.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` — update panel-text assertions (~407, ~586, ~729, ~901, ~962) that assert `W:…`/`→…` substrings.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` — update the read-only detail-panel assertions (~544–554) to the titled format.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — expected no change (titled text replaces the body string only); touch only if word-wrap needs a tweak.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update narratives that quote the detail panel's format.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U — Hangar Map UX** (completed): the map UX epic that defined the reveal, tile labels and the detail panel; this item refines the panel's text only.
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9 — Text on hex map is unreadable** (completed): created this very detail panel by moving the full intel off the tiles; this item labels its lines.
- **AH-0MWF0CXR4004C9CN — special missions** and **AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG — hex variety** (completed): added the already-headed SPECIAL MISSION / PERSONALITY / CONTRACT / LANDMARK sections the titled brief keeps.

Duplicate check performed — no overlapping completed item found (the sibling items above cover tile readability and variety sections, not line-item titles).

Automated related-work report (find-related, `AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK`):

- **AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB — Held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES map action and wiring** (blocked): will add an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action row to the *same* held-hex detail panel; coordinate ordering/format and shared test assertions when both land.
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2 — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel** (completed): the original hex-map scene whose intel this panel displays.
- **AH-0MW8F7NH1002PQE3 — Hangar War needs a restart button** (completed): a Hangar War UX sibling.
- Repo matches: `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (detail-panel narrative), `CHANGELOG.md` (excluded from doc updates this item).

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should titles be added to every line of the selected-hex overview, or only the cryptic abbreviated lines (`S:`/`W:`/`→`/`bot`/`atk`)?" — Answer (assumed, pending producer review): every line that is not already self-explanatory, keeping the already-headed variety sections. Source: item description "We need titles to tell us what each of the items are." (`wl show AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK`); no interview round held — seed context sufficed.
- Q2: "Preferred title style and format?" — Answer (assumed, pending producer review): standard `TITLE: value` per line, capitalised ASCII matching the existing `SPECIAL MISSION` / `REWARD:` heading style; exact wording is implementer's choice within the AC. Source: draft brief, pending review.
- Q3 (OPEN QUESTION, non-blocking): "Should the left-hand `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` panel's report rows also gain titles, or is the right-hand selected-hex overview the only scope?" — **Recommended: right-hand panel only** — the description names the selected hex's textual overview; the attack panel already carries its own heading and the report model's rows. If the producer wants the attack rows titled too, that becomes an additional AC (or a separate item).

# Bot oscillates too much

## Problem statement

The bot player oscillates: it turns left and right and goes back and forth,
"seemingly with no purpose", instead of always working towards a clear
objective. The live bot is the **competent framework brain**
(`createCompetentBotBrain`, flown by `PlayScene` demo/attract mode, the
bot-tuning gym and the recording/teaser tools) whose flat utility bands still
rank **minerals (4.0–4.5) and power-ups (3.0–3.75) above enemy engagement
(2.0–2.75)** — values inherited from the original "minerals > power-ups >
enemies > asteroids" order (AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L·AC1–AC4, later superseded in
the legacy ladder by the willingness model). The mere presence of a pickup in
range therefore yanks the bot away from wave-clear combat, and with the
short commitment window (`minCommitSeconds` 0.25 s) objectives churn: the
observed behaviour is exactly "switching objective too frequently".

## Users (example user stories)

- **Player watching the attract demo / teaser** — "As a player watching the
  attract demo, I want the bot to fly purposefully — holding a clear course,
  hunting the wave, and only peeling off briefly for something clearly worth
  it — so the game looks alive and competent rather than erratic."
- **Producer tuning the bot (GymBotTuning)** — "As a producer, I want to
  tune the *balance* between the bot's standing objective and opportunistic
  diversions, so the demo behaves believably without code changes."
- **Promo/teaser capture tooling** — "As the promo pipeline, I want the
  recorded bot movement to be legible in a 30-second teaser: a stable
  primary course with occasional, obvious pickups, not constant hunting."

## Acceptance Criteria

**Proposed (measurable; subject to operator review):**

- AC1 — **Two-layer objective system (hard requirement)**: the live
  competent brain runs a primary/secondary objective model. The two
  objectives are decided using the **existing band order**
  (survival > secure-life > boss > minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids
  > reposition), retuning the bands only where necessary. The primary
  objective (take an offered Extra Life while below the cap, focus the boss,
  avoid imminent danger, engage/collect per band standing, reposition to a
  key safe/attack location) is committed and sticky — it changes only when it
  is achieved, invalidated, or a genuinely higher-value primary takes over,
  never merely because a pickup appeared.
- AC2 — **Secondary interrupts are bounded and return**: a secondary goal
  (collect a high-value red mineral deposit, collect a mineral cluster,
  collect a power-up drop, destroy a collision-path asteroid) may preempt the
  primary **only** when its payoff clears the diversion threshold *and* the
  primary's urgency allows; once the secondary is complete or abandoned the
  bot returns to the primary objective.
- AC3 — **Band order decides the two objectives; collection is
  opportunistic**: the existing competent band order (minerals > power-ups >
  enemies within the combat/collection stack) determines which goals are the
  standing primary and which are interruptible secondaries; bands may be
  retuned where needed to stop churn. A lone gold mineral or ordinary
  power-up never displaces the committed primary by presence alone — a
  secondary must clear the diversion threshold (parity with the legacy
  willingness model AC11–AC14 where applicable).
- AC4 — **Red over yellow**: minerals are prioritised by value — a red
  deposit (value 10, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE`) is preferred over a gold dot
  (value 1) whenever that does not require a major divergence. This requires
  plumbing mineral `value` through `BotSnapshot` → world model → mineral goal
  weighting (currently the mineral weight is a constant `() => 1`).
- AC5 — **Oscillation measurably reduced**: a machine-checkable
  purposefulness metric (e.g. committed-goal switch rate and/or heading
  reversal count per second, sampled via `BotBrain.committedGoalId` on seeded
  runs) shows a reduction versus the current flat-band brain, and each primary
  objective is held for at least a minimum committed duration on the seeded
  demo baseline.
- AC6 — **Survival stays the hard constraint**: the never-suicide guarantee
  (no wall/enemy/bullet/hazard collision when a safe alternative exists) is
  unchanged and property-tested as today.
- AC7 — **Deterministic**: same run seed → same decision sequence (decision
  layer pure; per-press randomness stays in the governor, seed-derived).
- AC8 — **Gym↔game parity preserved**: the same brain flies `PlayScene` demo,
  the recording tools and every gym scene that exercises collection; the
  parity matrix `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and any affected gym are updated in the
  same change.
- AC9 — **Testing / validation**: unit tests per goal and per interrupt rule
  (single/minimum-threshold, cluster-vs-lone, red-vs-gold, wave-pressure
  focus) plus a deterministic simulation/integration test demonstrating a
  stable primary under a changing pickup field.
- AC10 — **Documentation**: the decision-model docs (framework module header,
  README attract/demo section, GDD) describe the two-layer objective model;
  docs-assertion tests pass.
- AC11 — **Full project test suite, typecheck and build pass** with the
  change.

## Impact

Players and producers watching the attract demo or a recorded teaser see a
bot that flies with obvious purpose — holding a clear course and only peeling
off briefly for something clearly worth it — instead of oscillating
pointlessly, and future bot tuning gets an explicit primary/secondary balance
to adjust.

## Constraints

- The **competent framework brain** is the live bot everywhere (PlayScene
  demo, GymBotTuning, recording tools). The legacy `botDecision` ladder is
  now eval-only (wrapped by `createLegacyBotPolicy`); it must not drift from
  parity tests but is not the fix surface.
- "Red over yellow" maps to the existing mineral economy: red deposit (value
  10, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_COLOR`/`VALUE` — AH-0MVJ79739008396I) vs gold dot
  (value 1); orange salvage minerals (AH-0MVJ72I8O0009T09) are cosmetic and
  worth 1 like gold.
- The operator's "two layer objective system" description (primary examples,
  "secondary does not override the primary", "secondary goals can change much
  more frequently than primary") is the design intent, **confirmed as a hard
  requirement**: the existing band order decides the two objectives, with
  retuning permitted where necessary (operator answer, 2026-11-16).
- No scope creep: recording new diversion opportunities as linked work items,
  not extra goals in this item.
- **Key risk**: interrupt/return threshold values and any band retunes are a
  tuning judgement — mitigation: expose all new thresholds as
  `CompetentBotTunables` (GymBotTuning sliders) rather than hard-coding, and
  verify with the purposefulness metric + a recorded demo before review.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — flat utility bands in the original
  operator order (minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids), survival as a
  hard-constraint band above; mineral weight is a constant `() => 1`;
  `enemyWavePressurePort` already boosts the enemy band as the wave timer
  runs down.
- `src/ai/framework/commitment.ts` — goal-commitment/hysteresis
  (min-hold, switch-margin, challenger-persistence) that prevents pure
  per-tick flip-flop but still lets a pickup band repeatedly displace combat.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` / `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — mineral
  entries carry only `x`, `y`, `type`; no value/colour, so value-aware
  scoring is not yet possible.
- `src/ai/framework/botBrain.ts` — `committedGoalId` exposed, suitable for a
  switch-rate metric.
- `src/ai/eval/policies.ts` — eval harness already runs `competent` /
  `competent-no-fallback` / `legacy` policies; a purposefulness metric can be
  added there and baselined.

## Desired change

Restructure the competent brain's goal selection into a **primary/secondary
layer** in place of the flat presence-based priority, using the **existing
band order** to decide which goals are primary and which are interruptible
secondaries (retuning bands only where necessary): a sticky primary objective
is committed and held; secondary opportunities (red deposit > mineral cluster
> power-up > collision asteroid) interrupt it only when their payoff beats
the diversion threshold and the primary is not urgent, then hand control
back. Mineral goals become value-aware (red over gold) and lone gold minerals
no longer detour the bot. The survival tier and human-like governor are
unchanged. Tunables for the layering (primary hold, interrupt threshold,
return hysteresis, band retunes) are added to `CompetentBotTunables` so
GymBotTuning can expose them.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — split flat bands into primary/
  secondary layers; value-weight mineral goals.
- `src/ai/framework/commitment.ts` — extend commitment to retain the primary
  across secondary interrupts (suspend/resume) and to rate-limit secondary
  churn.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — new layering tunables
  (primary hold, interrupt threshold, return margin/hysteresis, red-deposit
  weight).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` + `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — carry mineral
  `value` from `scene.getMinerals()` (`mineral.value`) into the world model.
- `src/ai/framework/botBrain.ts` — any primary/secondary state the brain must
  persist across ticks; `committedGoalId` already exposed for metrics.
- `src/ai/eval/` — purposefulness (switch-rate / reversal) metric and the
  seeded before/after baseline.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` / `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — wiring
  unchanged; new tunables flow through `toCompetentOverrides`.

## Related work

- AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L — "Demo bot movement goals" (completed): legacy
  willingness model (enemies default; grouped minerals/upgrades earn a
  diversion; AC11–AC14) — the behaviour this item re-creates inside the
  competent framework. Its flat AC1–AC4 order is the source of the current
  oscillation.
- AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO — "Structured competent bot" (completed): the live
  framework; AC1 flat band order and commitment/hysteresis are the surface to
  change.
- AH-0MVRMYZF5008VFV5 — "Boss-only engage targeting (hard priority)"
  (completed): precedent for a hard-priority primary (the boss band sits above
  collection); its structure informs how a primary goal outranks interrupts.
- AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — human-like input governor (unchanged; cadence).
- AH-0MVT2VYN40076JKX — wrap-aware steering + near-tie hysteresis
  (unchanged; prevents seam flip-flop).
- AH-0MVJ79739008396I — red mineral deposits (value 10) that ground the
  "red over yellow" preference.
- AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4 — Extra Life prioritisation (`secure-life` band) =
  an existing primary-goal example.
- AH-0MVJ72I8O0009T09 — orange salvage minerals (cosmetic, value 1).
- AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN — predictive dodge (survival tier; unchanged).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** – Bot prioritises extra lives in hold-full choice
  and on-screen pickups (completed) — the existing `secure-life` primary.
- **AH-0MVRMYZF5008VFV5** – Boss-only engage targeting (hard priority)
  (completed) — precedent for hard-priority primaries.
- **AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L** – Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups >
  enemies > asteroids (completed) — the flat-band order this item re-layers.

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — attract/demo bot section (decision-model docs to update).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — decision-model docs to update.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — bot behaviour docs to update.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is the two-layer primary/secondary objective system a hard architectural
  requirement, or is the underlying goal simply a bot that stops oscillating
  and always works towards shooting enemies / collecting valuables when
  convenient?" — Answer (rgardler, 2026-11-16): **"Hard requirement — use
  the existing band order to decide the two objectives (retune if
  necessary)."** Source: interactive reply on the work item. The brief now
  reflects this: the existing band order (survival > secure-life > boss >
  minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids > reposition) decides the
  primary/secondary split, with retuning permitted.
- Q: "What is the acceptable bar for 'stops oscillating'? Proposed: a
  machine-checkable purposefulness metric (committed-goal switch rate +
  heading reverses on seeded demo runs) improving over the current brain, plus
  a visual check of a recorded demo." — Answer (rgardler, 2026-11-16):
  **"Accept."** Source: interactive reply on the work item. AC5 stands as
  written.
- Q: "Fix surface: confirm the change is limited to the live competent brain
  (game demo, tuning gym, recording tools) and that the legacy `botDecision`
  ladder stays eval-only." — **Assumption made from repo evidence**: the game
  and gyms both fly `createCompetentBotBrain`; `createLegacyBotPolicy` wraps
  `decideBotIntent` only for the eval harness.

## Duplicate-work check

`wl search` over "bot movement", "bot objective", "mineral red yellow",
"goal primary secondary" and "oscillat" found no open or completed item that
already satisfies these acceptance criteria — the oscillation symptoms were
addressed ad hoc (commitment/hysteresis, near-tie hysteresis, unwillingness
model) but the two-layer primary/secondary restructure and red-over-yellow
value-aware collection are not tracked anywhere. Check performed, no
duplicate.


---

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-16 (plan session): Full plan completed for AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2. Pre-check decision `plan` (Medium/Medium); no approval pause (approval-gate `request_approval: false`). Created 7 child items in test-first dependency order:
  - AH-0MWJ7EC6T0097EWN — Purposefulness metric and seeded baseline (test-first)
  - AH-0MWJ7ECYB006S3YS — Deterministic objective and interrupt rule tests (test-first)
  - AH-0MWJ7EDTZ008FHSW — Mineral value plumbing: red over gold
  - AH-0MWJ7EELF000ALYX — Two-layer primary/secondary objective model
  - AH-0MWJ7EFAF000FWJU — Layering tunables and GymBotTuning surfacing
