# Author shipped hex variety content on ring 1 (one landmark and one contract)

## Problem statement

The shipped hex-variety machinery (epic AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG) is complete and
verified, but none of the **shipped** rings author its axes yet: ring 1
currently carries no landmark and no contract, so the opening ring does not
demonstrate the variety the machinery was built for. This item authors exactly
one landmark and one contract onto ring-1 hexes — pure content, no machinery
changes — so the opening ring exercises the shipped choices (and the follow-on
AH-0MWH4F375000X08G authors the same on ring 2).

## Users (with example user stories)

- **The new player** — "I captured the first ring's hexes as identical chores;
  I want at least one opening-ring hex to offer a real set-piece decision and
  one to offer a worthwhile optional objective, so ring 1 shows what the game
  can do before the grind sets in."
- **The strategist** — "I want to read the landmark and the contract (objective
  + bonus amounts) in the map's known-ahead intel before I commit a life, so
  the variety informs which hex I attack next."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `validateRingDefinitions` passes with no new issues; `hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` CSV-parity guard stays green (both the typed table and `hex-ring-1.csv` agree).
- AC2: the chosen landmark hex and contract hex publish known-ahead intel — tile tag and detail-panel blocks show the landmark and the contract (objective + bonus amounts) before the player commits a life.
- AC3: gameplay effects resolve through the shipped pure modules: a fortress requires two capture passes (replay-safe), or a cache pays bonus salvage instead of granting; the contract banks its bonus once (`contractFulfilled` replay guard), determinism preserved under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` field-presence migration.
- AC4: full project test suite passes with the new changes; the hex-variety epic verification (`src/core/hangarWar/hexVarietyEpic.verification.test.ts`) still passes.
- AC5: the authored content is recorded in a comment on this item (the hex ids, the landmark/contract chosen, and the balance rationale).
- AC6: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and the ring-definition/CSV header notes where relevant; no README or docs-site drift introduced.

## Impact

Ring 1 now demonstrates the shipped variety machinery — one hex with a landmark set-piece and one with an optional contract — so the opening ring offers authored strategic choices instead of identical chores.

## Constraints

- **Authoring only**: no changes to the shipped machinery (ring, resolver, deployment, capture-cycle or store modules) — those are shipped and verified. This item is pure data authoring.
- **Both sources must agree**: update `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` AND the matching `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` seed; the parity test guards drift.
- **Cache vs weapon hex**: a cache landmark can never be the ring's weapon hex (`validateRingDefinitions` rejects it). Ring 1's weapon hex is `hex-r1-6` (maw-of-ashes, `waveLaser`, `baseAggression` 6) — a cache must go on one of `hex-r1-1`..`hex-r1-5`.
- **At most one fortress and one cache per ring** (duplicate-landmark rejection).
- **Balance/band**: keep ring 1 inside its survivable aggression band; landmark/contract rewards must not distort the recommended order — in particular the weapon hex (`hex-r1-6`) stays the ring's hardest.
- **Currencies**: the contract objective/bonuses must flow through the shipped currencies (salvage/cores), fulfilling on capture via the existing banking rule.

## Existing state

- Ring 1 is 6 hexes around the hangar: `hex-r1-1` (aggression 2, hull-2), `hex-r1-2` (1, extra-life), `hex-r1-3` (3, rapid), `hex-r1-4` (2, ricochet), `hex-r1-5` (4, core-bank), `hex-r1-6` (6, waveLaser, weapon hex).
- No ring-1 row authors a `personality`, a `contract` or a `landmark` — every variety field in `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and `hex-ring-1.csv` is empty for ring 1.
- The vocabulary, validation and effects are shipped and verified against the ring-3 sample by the epic (audit-ready; all epic children in `in_review`).

## Desired change

- Author exactly **one landmark** (fortress or cache — implementer's choice, see open decision below) on a valid ring-1 hex (cache candidates `hex-r1-1..hex-r1-5`; a fortress may go on any ring-1 hex except it must not be the weapon hex).
- Author exactly **one contract** (optional per-hex objective with bonus salvage/cores banked on capture) on a ring-1 hex.
- Both changes land identically in the typed table and the CSV seed.

**Key Files:**
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — add authored `landmark` and `contract` fields to one ring-1 hex each
- `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` — mirror both in the seed rows (parity test guards drift)
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — must stay green (CSV-parity guard)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexVarietyEpic.verification.test.ts` — must stay green (epic verification)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep**: only the two authored hexes are in scope; do not start authoring personalities or the ring-2 follow-on (AH-0MWH4F375000X08G covers ring 2). Additional variety ideas raised during implementation belong in new work items, not this one.
- **Validation surprise**: a chosen landmark/contract could trip an existing validation rule not obvious from the summary (e.g. coordinate/duplicate interplay). Mitigation: run the ring-validation and parity tests locally before finishing; any rule violation means picking a different valid hex.
- **Balance drift risk**: rewards sized too generously could make a low-aggression hex out-value the recommended order. Mitigation: keep bonuses modest relative to current grants and re-check that `hex-r1-6` remains the ring's hardest/peak reward.
- **Assumption**: the epic's verification is authoritative — no re-derivation of the machinery is needed, only data.

## Open decision (for implementation)

The implementer may pick **fortress** OR **cache** for the ring-1 landmark (the
operator asked for "a landmark"). Pick the one that best demonstrates the
set-piece without unbalancing the opening ring, and document the choice + the
hex id in the final comment on this item.

## Related work

- discovered-from: AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG (hex variety epic — machinery shipped and verified against the ring-3 sample)
- related-to: AH-0MWH4F375000X08G (same content-authoring exercise on ring 2, already intake_complete)
- AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7 (data vocabulary), AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH (landmarks axis), AH-0MWEW58WD003NFXS (contracts axis), AH-0MWEW73WS003QFV7 (end-to-end verification)
- AH-0MWJ51KUS005WQK6 — related open item that also touches ring-1 data (special-mission hex); distinct axis, no overlap with this authoring
- docs: `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (hex-variety parity record), `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` header design notes

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. The seed context from the epic's
validation — scope, design constraints, acceptance criteria and the explicit
open choice for landmark kind and hex — fully specified the intake; the brief
above preserves that content rather than restating questions.

# Post-MVP Hangar War: add a special-mission hex to ring 1

## Problem statement

The special-mission mechanic (AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55) is authored for ring 2 only: `hex-r2-3` is the single `isSpecialMission: true` hex and pays the Juggernaut Hull (`hull-3`). A player in the early ring-1 phase never sees a special mission, so the "what should I take, what should I risk" decision the mechanic exists to create only appears once the frontier — and the hangar's aggression — has grown. Ring 1 should offer one special mission of its own, with a reward that fits the early ring's economy.

## Users

- **The new-ring player** — "In ring 1 I want to occasionally see a hex that pays something I cannot buy yet, so the ring surprises me from the first frontier rather than only after the midpoint."
- **The strategist** — the same known-ahead rule as ring 2: see the ring-1 special's reward before committing a life.

## Scope

- **The ring-1 special converts `hex-r1-5`** (`the-hollow-judge`, baseAggression 4, currently granting `core-bank`) to `isSpecialMission: true` in `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, mirrored in the `hex-ring-1.csv` seed column. **Ring 1 holds exactly six hexes (`6 × n` rule; `validateRingDefinitions` requires every ring coordinate covered, unique coordinates/ids, exactly one weapon hex), so the special is a conversion — the seven-hex alternative is not valid.** Converting the currency grant is the least disruptive choice: no purchasable weapon or the Bulwark hull is lost.
- The special reward is a **new ring-1-tier hull** (Q2 = a): **4 starting lives, `baseDefence` 3**, above the starter Scrap Hull (`hull-1`: 3 lives/DEF 2) and below the Bulwark (`hull-2`: 4 lives/DEF 4, itself the free `hex-r1-1` grant), so it never undercuts the Bulwark economy. Expressed through the existing `HullDefinition` / `HullRunStats` model and granted via the shipped `resolveHexGrant` path (Q2 = a shape, same as AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55).
- **The new hull is grant-only (Q3 = b): a catalogue entry under `kind: 'hull'` (so `isHullGrant` and `resolveHexGrant` accept it) with no reachable purchase path** — no shoppable `minRing`/price, so it never appears in the hangar shop and stays a special-mission reward. The catalogue comment documents that it is deliberately not purchasable.
- The special-mission offer follows the existing seeded rotation: `resolveSpecialOffer` draws only from the **current ring's** uncaptured specials, so the ring-1 special is offered during the ring-1 phase with no cross-ring interaction.
- Known-ahead intel, one payload, loud validation, gym↔game parity and docs: the existing machinery applies unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — Exactly one ring-1 hex has `isSpecialMission: true` in `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` and the `hex-ring-1.csv` mirror: `hex-r1-5`, converting its grant from `core-bank` to the new hull id. Ring 2's special (`hex-r2-3`) is unchanged, and ring 1 still holds exactly six hexes with `hex-r1-6` as its sole weapon hex.
- **AC2** — The ring validator (`validateRingDefinitions`) accepts the new definition (grant is a hull catalogue entry) and the ring-1 CSV-parity test passes; existing validation tests stay green.
- **AC3** — The reward is a new catalogue hull with **4 starting lives and `baseDefence` 3** (extra hit points over the starter Scrap Hull, below the Bulwark), expressed through the shipped model, granted through the existing `resolveHexGrant` path into `unlockedHulls` and persisting under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload (no new storage key). The hull is **grant-only**: not purchasable in the hangar (no reachable purchase path). The reward stays inside the ring-1 aggression-band budget (AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC) and does not undercut the Bulwark economy (free grant at `hex-r1-1` or purchase).
- **AC4** — The ring-1 special is published known-ahead on the hex map: `★ SPECIAL` tile tag, detail-panel reward block (hull name, `+1 LIVES`, `DEF`), and correct `offeredNow` from the seeded rotation during the ring-1 phase.
- **AC5** — Completing the ring-1 special through the shipped one-level capture (flow: adjacent-hex reveal → deploy → wave-10 mini-boss victory → `resolveHexCapture`) grants the new hull; no second run implementation (gym↔game parity).
- **AC6** — `GymHexWar` / `GymHangar` exercise the ring-1 special (reward + rotation + persistence) with the same code as the game; GDD §8.2, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` updated; full suite green.

## Impact

Players in the opening ring now meet the game's risk-vs-reward special mission from their first frontier, and their reward is a tougher hull they cannot buy — an early, memorable survivability step instead of a mid-campaign event.

## Constraints

- Ring 1 remains exactly six hexes (`6 × n`); the special is a conversion, not an addition.
- No model extension: everything through the shipped `HullDefinition` / `HullRunStats`, `resolveHexGrant`, `resolveSpecialOffer`, payload.
- No second run / new mission kind (Q1 = a) — the "special" lives in the authored hex kind plus its hull reward.
- No new storage key; the ring-1 special uses the existing seeded rotation, which draws only from the current ring's uncaptured specials.
- New hull is grant-only — deliberately not purchasable.
- Reward must not trivialise ring 1 or outclass the Bulwark / Juggernaut.

## Existing state

- Ring 1 (6 hexes): `hex-r1-1` grants `hull-2` (Bulwark, free), `hex-r1-2` grants `extra-life`, `hex-r1-3` grants `rapid`, `hex-r1-4` grants `ricochet`, `hex-r1-5` grants `core-bank`, `hex-r1-6` grants `waveLaser` (sole weapon hex, aggression 6).
- Ring 2 (12 hexes): `hex-r2-3` (`the-void-marshall`, aggression 5) is the single `isSpecialMission: true` hex, granting `hull-3` (Juggernaut, 5 lives/DEF 5, `minRing: 2`).
- Hulls: Scrap `hull-1` (3 lives/DEF 2, starter, `minRing: 1`), Bulwark `hull-2` (4 lives/DEF 4, `minRing: 1`), Juggernaut `hull-3` (5 lives/DEF 5, `minRing: 2`).
- Shared machinery: `resolveHexGrant` (captureCycle), `resolveSpecialOffer` (rng), `validateRingDefinitions` + `isHullGrant` (hexRing), `hexIntel`/`specialMission` offer publishing, `GymHexWar`/`GymHangar`.

## Desired change

One ring-1 hex (`hex-r1-5`) becomes a known-ahead special mission paying a new grant-only 4-lives/DEF-3 hull, with the same one-level capture, intel, rotation and persistence as the ring-2 special; gyms and docs updated in the same change.

## Key Files

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` + `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` — `hex-r1-5` converted to the special (grant ⇒ new hull id).
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — the new ring-1-tier grant-only hull entry (`hull-4`).
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — validation + CSV-parity tests.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`, `specialMission.ts`, `rng.ts`, `captureCycle.ts` — existing machinery; expected reuse without structural change (verify).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` (+ test) — parity coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — docs updates.

## Design considerations / risks

- **Reward choice (decided, Q2 = a):** new hull with 4 lives / DEF 3 — strictly more survivability than Scrap, clearly below Bulwark (4 lives/DEF 4), so the Bulwark keeps its value as both the `hex-r1-1` free grant and the ring-1 purchase.
- **Hex choice (decided, Q1 = a):** `hex-r1-5` — the ring's near-hardest non-weapon hex, matching the ring-2 "demanding hex" special; its lost grant is a currency bank, not a unique weapon/hull.
- **Grant-only (decided, Q3 = b):** catalogue entry under `kind: 'hull'` with no reachable purchase path; `isHullGrant` requires a catalogue hull, so the entry must exist, but `canBuy`/shop listing never surfaces it.
- **Rotation scope:** `resolveSpecialOffer` draws over the current ring's uncaptured special hexes, so the ring-1 special is offered only while the player is in ring 1 — pinned with a test so it can never leak across rings when ring 2 arrives.
- **Not a gold rush:** extra lives/defence are modest relative to the ring-2 Juggernaut.
- **Out of scope:** new special-mission kinds/objectives (Q1 = a), upgrade bays (AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY), any change beyond one converted ring-1 hex + its hull reward.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55` — the special-missions epic this extends (completed).
- `AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC` — aggression-band budget reference.
- `AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY` — hull upgrade bays (out of scope here).
- GDD §8.2, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which ring-1 hex becomes the special mission? (Ring 1 is fixed at 6 hexes, so one must be converted.) a) `hex-r1-5` (`the-hollow-judge`, aggression 4, grants `core-bank`); b) `hex-r1-4` (`ember-reaver`, aggression 2, grants `ricochet`); c) freeform." — Answer (producer): **a — `hex-r1-5`**. Source: interactive reply. Research: ring 1 definitions (hexRingDefinitions.ts) confirm its grant is `core-bank` (currency), not a unique weapon/hull; ring validator enforces the 6-hex `6 × n` coverage rule, so conversion (not addition) is the only valid shape.
- Q2: "The new reward hull's stats? a) 4 lives / DEF 3; b) 3 lives / DEF 4; c) freeform." — Answer (producer): **a — 4 lives / DEF 3**. Source: interactive reply. Research: catalogue (hangarCatalogue.ts) confirms Scrap 3 lives/DEF 2, Bulwark 4 lives/DEF 4, Juggernaut 5 lives/DEF 5; 4/DEF 3 is a clean survivability step over Scrap that stays below Bulwark.
- Q3: "Should the new hull also be purchasable in the hangar, or grant-only? a) catalogue entry with `minRing: 1` and a price (purchasable); b) grant-only." — Answer (producer): **b — grant-only**. Source: interactive reply. Research: `isHullGrant` (hexRing.ts) and `resolveHexGrant` only require a `kind: 'hull'` catalogue entry; `canBuy` (hangarEconomy.ts) gates purchase by `minRing` + price, so a catalogue entry with no reachable purchase path is grant-only while remaining a valid grant target.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWF0CX0H004OJ2Y** – Feature: Resolve special-grant on capture path (completed)
- **AH-0MWH4F375000X08G** – Author shipped hex variety content on ring 2 (personalities, contracts, landmarks) (open)
- **AH-0MWB8VDDI005WVMG** – Pin per-ring loadout resolution in tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvwzyiwx0008c55, 0mweusvj1007exjy, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+319 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvwzyiwx0008c55, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+276 more)
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — matched: 0mvwzyiwx0008c55, 0mweusvj1007exjy, accept, add, addition (+246 more)

# Two-layer primary/secondary objective model

## Summary

Restructure the competent brain's goal selection into a sticky primary / interruptible-secondary objective model using the existing band order, with bounded secondary interrupts that return to the primary, per AC1–AC3, AC6 and AC7 of AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two-layer objective system: the live competent brain runs a primary/secondary objective model; the two objectives are decided using the existing band order (survival > secure-life > boss > minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids > reposition), retuning the bands only where necessary; the primary is committed and sticky — it changes only when achieved, invalidated, or a genuinely higher-value primary takes over, never merely because a pickup appeared (Covers parent AC1).
- Secondary interrupts are bounded and return: a secondary goal (high-value red mineral, mineral cluster, power-up drop, collision-path asteroid) may preempt the primary only when its payoff clears the diversion threshold and the primary's urgency allows; once the secondary is complete or abandoned the bot returns to the primary (Covers parent AC2).
- Band order decides the two objectives; collection is opportunistic: a lone gold mineral or ordinary power-up never displaces the committed primary by presence alone — a secondary must clear the diversion threshold (parity with the legacy willingness model AC11–AC14 where applicable); bands may be retuned where needed to stop churn (Covers parent AC3).
- Survival stays the hard constraint: the never-suicide guarantee (no wall/enemy/bullet/hazard collision when a safe alternative exists) is unchanged and property-tested as today (Covers parent AC6).
- Deterministic: same run seed → same decision sequence; the decision layer is pure and per-press randomness stays in the governor (Covers parent AC7).

## Minimal Implementation

- Split the flat utility bands in `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` into primary/secondary layers: primary = committed sticky goals (secure-life, boss, enemies per band standing, reposition); secondary = interruptible collection goals (red deposit > mineral cluster > power-up > collision asteroid).
- Extend `src/ai/framework/commitment.ts` with suspend/resume so a secondary interrupt does not release the primary, and rate-limit secondary churn (return hysteresis).
- Add the diversion-threshold / primary-urgency gate for secondary interrupts.
- Keep the survival band and the human-like governor unchanged.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — primary/secondary layering
- `src/ai/framework/commitment.ts` — suspend/resume + secondary churn rate-limit
- `src/ai/framework/botBrain.ts` — any persistent primary/secondary state

## Deliverables

- Two-layer objective model in the competent brain with sticky primary, bounded interrupts and return-to-primary, satisfying the deterministic contract tests.

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2.
- Mineral value plumbing (red over gold) — value-aware secondaries.

# Layering tunables and GymBotTuning surfacing

## Summary

Expose the two-layer tuning surface (primary hold, interrupt threshold, return hysteresis/margin, red-deposit weight, band retunes) as `CompetentBotTunables` flowing through `toCompetentOverrides`, and surface them in GymBotTuning so producers can retune without code changes (tuning-risk mitigation from AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2).

## Acceptance Criteria

# Wave Laser fires from ship

## Headline

The beam weapons (Wave Laser and Mining Laser — both confirmed in scope, Q1 = A) currently render a **static polyline frozen at fire time**, so as the ship keeps flying during the beam's visible lifetime the beam's source end visibly detaches from the ship. The fix: each frame the beam's **source end tracks the ship's current position** while its **destination (the launch-resolved end point) stays fixed** — a purely visual change in the shared VFX seam.

## Problem statement

When the ship fires a beam weapon and keeps moving, the rendered beam stays anchored to the world position the ship occupied at the moment of firing rather than to the ship itself. With the ship's max speed around 175 px/s, a Wave Laser beam (visible 0.3 s) can drift up to ~50 px clear of the ship's nose while the beam is still on screen, so the beam visibly no longer "fires from the ship". The Mining Laser beam (visible 0.12 s) has the same static-polyline behaviour and is confirmed in scope (Q1 = A).

## Users

- **The player** — watches the ship fire the Wave Laser (and Mining Laser) while dodging; the beam should read as emanating from the ship's current position, never as floating in space where the ship was a moment ago.

**User stories:**

- As the player, when my ship fires a Wave Laser and I keep flying, the red beam's source end stays attached to my ship and follows it, while the beam's far end stays fixed at the point where it resolved — so the beam always visibly fires *from* my ship.
- As the player, when the Mining Laser is cutting an asteroid, its beam likewise stays connected to my ship as it drifts, not detached at the position where the shot was fired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Source follows the ship (Wave Laser).** During the Wave Laser beam's visible lifetime, its rendered source end re-anchors each frame to the ship's current position, so the beam stays visibly connected to the ship as it moves.
- AC2 — **Destination stays fixed.** The beam's far end remains at the launch-resolved destination — the first-intercept point when the ray met an entity, otherwise the full-extent endpoint — for the beam's whole visible life. The beam is never re-aimed or re-resolved: no damage is re-applied, no hit is recomputed, and the ray's damage result stays exactly as resolved at launch.
- AC3 — **Wrapped path preserved.** As the ship moves, the beam is redrawn along the **shortest wrapped path** from the ship's current position to the fixed destination (one segment per arena-edge crossing), consistent with the existing wrapped-segment geometry used by the Mining Laser beam.
- AC4 — **Duration, fade and cleanup unchanged.** The beam keeps its configured visible duration (0.3 s Wave Laser), fades and destroys identically, and never persists past its lifetime; the per-frame redraw stays cheap (a single Graphics, delta-driven, following the existing self-cleaning beam pattern).
- AC5 — **Game↔gym parity.** The re-anchoring lives in the shared VFX seam and the shared fire path (`CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam`), so `PlayScene` and every gym render the identical tracking beam; the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` still passes.
- AC6 — **Mining Laser re-anchors too.** The Mining Laser beam re-anchors its source the same way: each frame its source end tracks the ship's current position while its destination (the target asteroid's position **frozen at fire time**) stays fixed; the change must not regress the Mining Laser's damage, target selection or cadence (`CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` still damages the selected live asteroid exactly once per shot, and the beam does **not** track the asteroid as it drifts).
- AC7 — **Tests and documentation.** Unit tests cover: a moving ship re-anchors the beam source while the destination never moves; no re-hit or re-damage occurs during the beam's life; the wrapped path updates when the ship crosses an arena edge mid-beam; and game↔gym parity. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (e.g. `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` only if a divergence is retained). The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

As a player, the Wave Laser (and Mining Laser) beam now visibly emanates from your ship and stays attached as you fly, instead of floating in the space your ship occupied a moment ago.

## Constraints

- **Visual-only change.** Aim (per-shot RNG bias), cadence, damage and hit resolution are already settled at launch and must not change; the beam never re-hits or re-damages.
- **Shared seam.** The behaviour must live once in `src/scenes/core/` + `src/vfx/` so the game and every gym (GymWeapons, GymMinerals) run the same code — per the gym↔game parity convention (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **Cheap by construction.** The Mining Laser fires up to once per sixteenth note (~0.1875 s); a per-frame redraw must not accumulate Graphics objects or tweens and must clean itself up on expiry and scene shutdown.
- **Ship reference lifecycle.** The beam outlives the launch frame; it must resolve the ship's position through a safe provider that survives the ship being destroyed or the scene shutting down mid-beam.

## Existing state

- **Wave Laser** is an **instant hitscan ray** (AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ): `CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam` resolves the ray once at launch (`resolveHitscanRay` in `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts`), applies exactly 1 damage at the first intercept through the shared kill seam, and renders the static polyline with `spawnHitscanBeam` (`src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts`) — a red column with white-hot core, faded via a 0.3 s tween. The beam geometry is frozen at the launch muzzle position.
- **Mining Laser** fires an instant beam from the ship to the selected asteroid: `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` calls `spawnMiningLaserBeam` (`src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`), which draws a static wrapped polyline from the **fire-time** ship position to the **fire-time** target position and ages it over 0.12 s via a delta-driven update. This module already owns the wrapped shortest-path helper (`miningLaserBeamSegments`) that the anchored beam would share.
- Both beams are therefore disconnected from the ship for the rest of their visible life once the ship moves — exactly the reported defect.

## Desired change

- Extend the beam VFX seam with an **anchored-beam renderer**: instead of drawing a one-shot static polyline, the beam Graphics takes a **source provider** (a function returning the ship's current position, or a scene method like `getPlayer()`) plus a **fixed destination** point, and on each frame recomputes the wrapped shortest path (`miningLaserBeamSegments`-style, from `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`) between the current source and the fixed destination, clearing and redrawing the Graphics. Duration, fade, registry and shutdown cleanup stay as today.
- `CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam` passes the player as the source anchor and `resolution.end` as the fixed destination (the intercept point, or the full-extent endpoint when nothing was intercepted).
- `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` snapshots the target position at fire time (freezing the destination — the beam does **not** track the asteroid as it drifts, per "destination stays fixed") and passes the player as the source anchor.

## Key Files:

- `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts` — Wave Laser beam VFX: replace the static-polyline draw with the per-frame source-following anchored render (source provider + fixed destination), keeping duration/fade/registry semantics.
- `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts` — home of the wrapped shortest-path helper (`miningLaserBeamSegments`) the anchored beam reuses; Mining Laser beam gets the same treatment (confirmed in scope, Q1 = A).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `fireHitscanBeam`: pass the player anchor + `resolution.end` to the renderer.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onMiningLaserFire`: freeze the target position at fire time and pass the player anchor.
- `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts` — ray geometry (unchanged; supplies the fixed destination via the existing `resolution.end`).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity guard that must still pass unchanged.
- Tests (new/updated): `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.test.ts`, plus any gym test that exercises the beam while the ship moves.

## Related work

- AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ (completed, v0.1.18) — **Wave laser redesign**: built the hitscan beam seam (`src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts`, `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts`) that this item now makes ship-tracking.
- AH-0MW9QMP2P0032BWW (completed, v0.1.21) — **Shared core mining-laser fire step**: the shared `CombatCoreScene._updateMiningLaser` / `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` fire path the Mining Laser change would extend.
- AH-0MW9QMQ7B005WFH9 (completed, v0.1.21) — **Mining-laser beam VFX and audio cue**: the `spawnMiningLaserBeam` renderer and its wrapped-segment helper.
- AH-0MW9QMSI7005UU9P (completed) — **Gym coverage and parity for the mining laser** (GymMinerals), the parity gym for the Mining Laser half.
- AH-0MW10J31B0053E56 (completed) — **Wave Laser tuning**: level-resolved ray length/aim bias that fixes the level-0 length at 240 px.
- AH-0MV5DFBVW002J2XO (completed) — **Orbital Fires in direction of orb**: precedent for re-anchoring a fired effect's origin to a moving source object.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Beam pivot feel.** With a near intercept and the ship moving fast, the re-anchored beam pivots noticeably around its fixed destination, which may look unusual up close. Mitigation: source-anchor to the ship's natural firing point (the same position the ray resolved from); verify feel in the weapons gym before review.
- **R2 — Per-frame redraw cost.** The Mining Laser can fire every ~0.1875 s; a per-frame beam redraw must stay a single Graphics redraw with no object or tween accumulation. Mitigation: reuse the existing delta-driven, self-cleaning beam lifecycle and clear/redraw in place.
- **R3 — Ship destroyed mid-beam.** The beam outlives the launch frame, so the source provider must be safe if the ship is destroyed or the scene shuts down mid-life. Mitigation: provider guards against a missing player plus the existing shutdown cleanup.
- **R4 — Scope creep.** Re-aiming the beam at a moving enemy, tracking moving destinations, applying source-tracking to other weapons, or touching damage/aim/cadence are **out of scope**; any such opportunity should be recorded as a linked work item, not added to this change.

## Assumptions

- **A1 — Visual-only.** The beam's source tracking is a rendering change; the ray still resolves once at launch and damage, aim and cadence are untouched. Re-resolution or re-hits would contradict "destination stays fixed" and are out of scope.
- **A2 — Destination frozen at launch.** The beam's far end is the launch-resolved end point (first-intercept point, or full-extent endpoint) and stays there for the beam's whole visible life, even if the intercepted entity or anything else moves.
- **A3 — Mining Laser in scope** (confirmed by the producer: Q1 = A). The Mining Laser beam's destination is frozen at fire time — it does **not** follow the asteroid as it drifts; only the source re-anchors to the ship.

## Open Questions

- **RESOLVED Q1 — Is the Mining Laser in scope?** Producer answer: **A — yes, include the Mining Laser.** The Mining Laser beam has the identical static-polyline defect (0.12 s visible, ship up to ~21 px clear), and once the anchored-beam renderer exists the incremental cost is small. AC6 now mandates the same source-follows-ship treatment with the destination frozen at fire time.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-16 — Intake draft created from the seed description (auto-dispatched). Scope, ACs, key files and the single open scope question (Q1) recorded; duplicate check performed (no overlapping item found).
- 2026-11-16 — Producer answered Q1 = **A (Mining Laser in scope)**. AC6 rewritten as a firm criterion (destination frozen at fire time, no asteroid-tracking), headline/desired-change/key-files updated, the Open Question marked RESOLVED, and the Appendix records the answer.
- 2026-11-16 — Plan auto-complete (plan skill, Process step 1): the item is a bug (not an epic) whose description already carries measurable ACs (AC1–AC7) and a minimal implementation sketch (anchored-beam renderer + source provider + fixed destination, key files, constraints, risks). Effort Small / risk Medium just misses the auto-skip threshold (which requires risk Low), so the plan pre-check routed to the Process — but planning adds no value here; no decomposition into child features. AC-coverage review: `proceed` (no children, no conflicts). Decision recorded; item advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked as part of this intake): "Is the Mining Laser in scope for the source-follows-ship beam change?" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-16): **A — yes, include the Mining Laser.** Final: A (Option A — include), as recommended. Source: producer reply to the handoff comment AH-C0MWJAAJH80067EGM on the work item; research: both beams render a static polyline frozen at fire time and visibly detach from the ship (Wave Laser 0.3 s visible / ~50 px at max speed; Mining Laser 0.12 s / ~21 px), and one shared anchored-beam renderer covers both.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTV7OAJM002GGMM** – Move control buttons for gym scenes to the bottom (completed)
- **AH-0MUZMTS8J0029FSS** – Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core (completed)
- **AH-0MV1EDVNF004MTYN** – Wave laser audio fire/pickup cues and leveling-gym round-robin (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, possibly, ship, source, stays, wave
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, ship, source, stays, wave
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, ship, source, stays, wave

# Fade bullets out

## Problem statement

When an enemy bullet reaches the end of its range (its lifetime expires), it
currently **pops out of existence** — its sprite is destroyed in one frame.
Instead it should **shrink to nothing** during the last 20 % of its life, so
the expiry reads as a smooth visual dissolve rather than a snap. The bullet
remains dangerous while it shrinks.

## Users

- **Players** — as a player, I want enemy bullets to shrink away smoothly as
  they exhaust their range, so the game feel is polished and bullet expiry is
  readable at a glance instead of popping.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Shrink over the last 20 %:** an enemy bullet's view scales down
  from its full size to nothing during the final 20 % of its lifetime, and is
  destroyed when the lifetime elapses (as today).
- **AC2 — Full size before the fade window:** before the last 20 % of its
  lifetime the bullet renders at full scale (unchanged behaviour for the
  stored/lifetime bulk of its flight).
- **AC3 — Damages the player while shrinking:** the bullet's collision
  footprint keeps tracking its **visual sprite bounds** during the fade — it
  can still hit the player while visibly smaller, exactly until it fades away
  entirely.
- **AC4 — Enemy bullets only:** player bullets are **not** affected — their
  existing expiry behaviour is unchanged.
- **AC5 — Shared seam, gym↔game parity:** the change lands in the shared
  enemy-bullet lifecycle (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`), so the game
  and every gym scene that spawns enemy bullets fade identically; gyms that
  exercise enemy bullets cover the new behaviour.
- **AC6 — Testing:** automated unit tests verify the fade-window scaling
  (including a bullet destroyed exactly at expiry), no scaling outside the
  window, and that an animated (`redraw`) bullet fades too without regressing
  the per-frame animation hook.
- **AC7 — Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Enemy bullets shrink smoothly to nothing as their range runs out instead of
popping away, while staying just as dangerous while they fade.

## Constraints

- The shared lifecycle helper `advanceWrappingBullets` is the single
  ownership point for enemy-bullet advance, wrap and expiry — every scene
  (game and gyms) consumes it, so behaviour must not diverge per scene
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1, gym↔game parity).
- The bullet view is now a **sprite of a cached texture**, not a Graphics
  object (AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF); scaling must go through the sprite's
  `setScale` (no per-frame redraw of the texture).
- Fade duration is **not** proportional to bullet size — it is a fixed
  20 % of the bullet's own lifetime (producer decision, Q3).
- The existing expiry must still destroy the sprite exactly when the
  lifetime elapses (tested by the current suite).
- Collision/hitbox: enemy bullets currently use a fixed radius
  (`getEnemyBulletRadius`, ~8 px); the fade must make the effective
  footprint follow the visual sprite bounds while shrinking (producer
  decision, Q5).

## Risks & assumptions

- The bullet view contract (`BulletView`) must gain a scale capability;
  every consumer — game, gyms and the test stub — needs the new member.
  Mitigation: extend the structural interface and the `StubEnemyBullet` in
  `bulletLifecycle.test.ts` in the same change (the test already drives the
  shape of the contract).
- Scale baseline assumption: full scale (1.0) is the bullet's baked sprite
  size; the fade interpolates from 1.0 to ~0 over the window regardless of
  the baked radius — no radius-proportional formula (producer decision Q3).
- Collision-footprint change must not regress the fixed-radius path for
  bullets outside the fade window (AC2) nor the bomb/clearing paths that
  iterate `getEnemyBullets()` (PlayScene 3532, 1792).
- Scope-creep guard: fade applies to enemy bullets only; anything further
  (e.g. player-bullet fades, alpha fades, radius-proportional timing) is
  recorded as a separate work item, not part of this one.

## Existing state

In `advanceWrappingBullets` (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`), each
enemy bullet advances, wraps at the four edges, optionally animates through
its `redraw` hook, and is destroyed the moment `elapsed >= lifetime` — the
sprite vanishes in one frame. Enemy-bullet collision against the player uses
`getEnemyBulletRadius()` in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`.

## Desired change

Inside `advanceWrappingBullets`, once the bullet enters its final 20 % of
lifetime, scale its view down smoothly from full size to zero (e.g. linearly
with the remaining time fraction) before destroying it at expiry. The
shrink must be observable through the same structural view contract every
scene and test uses, and the collision footprint must shrink with the visual.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` — `advanceWrappingBullets` (+ the
  `WrappingBullet` / `BulletView` structural interfaces; likely add a
  `setScale` capability to the view contract) — owns the fade-window scaling.
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` — unit tests for the fade
  window, no-scaling-outside-window, animated-bullet fade, expiry-at-zero.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `getEnemyBulletRadius()` /
  enemy-bullet-vs-player collision — make the hit radius track the fading
  sprite bounds.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/…` — consumers of
  `advanceWrappingBullets`; verify parity (no per-scene copies to change).
- `docs/…` — GDD §4.4 (bullet range/lifetime) / any visual-feel docs, if
  the fade deserves a mention.

## Related work

- AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 — Bullets have a distance and wrap around the screen
  (lifetime/expiry model this builds on; completed).
- AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF — Cache bullet shapes as textures and batch bullet
  draw submission (sprite-of-cached-texture view; completed).
- AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA — shared bullet-lifecycle extraction parent
  (the helper this changes; completed).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention (shared seam
  requirement; completed).
- AH-0MVT2W5EL004OXNN — Eval arena wrap parity (bullet lifetime expiry
  preserved; completed).
- AH-0MUL15N63003PUDB — Animate enemies gliding to their re-anchored
  formation slots (smooth-motion/tweening precedent; completed).
- AH-0MV70Y2XY005J2HI — Hold-full overlay: fade the thruster/engine hum out
  while paused (fade precedent; completed).

### Related work (automated report)

Generated by `/skill:find-related` (imported into this brief): repository
keyword matches in `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` and
`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (bullets/damage/range/fade/shrink
terms). Full report:
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MWJ9PMYF005N588.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — Fade mechanism: reduce alpha, scale, or both? — Answer (producer):
  **scale only**. Research: cached-texture sprites support `setScale`
  directly (AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF); alpha fades are used elsewhere (pulse
  wave §7.2) but the producer chose shrink-by-scale for bullets.
- Q2 — When does the fade begin? — Answer (producer): **the last 20 % of
  the bullet's life**. Fixed fraction of lifetime, not a fixed time.
- Q3 — Fade duration proportional to initial size? — Answer (producer):
  **ignore** — stick to the last 20 % of life for every bullet regardless of
  size. Note: this supersedes the original description's "duration of the
  shrink should be proportional to their initial size". Prior
  answer/description text updated in this brief.
- Q4 — Player bullets? — Answer (producer): **enemy only**.
- Q5 — Hitbox during the fade — Answer (producer): **visual sprite bounds**;
  the bullet can still damage the player while shrinking, exactly until it
  fades to nothing.

# Hangar power-up ownership has no source

## Problem statement

The pure upgrade rule treats a power-up as **owned** only when the hangar records it, but no shipped path ever records one — the run's power-up levels are run-scoped and never reach the hangar, the hex-grant seam does not know power-up ids, and the unlock tree sells only hulls, weapons and modifiers. So the buy-to-upgrade economy can only ever upgrade weapons in real play.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want to **buy a power-up in the hangar tree** with banked minerals/cores so that my fleet permanently owns it between runs, I can then spend salvage raising its permanent level, and the ship I deploy with starts with it.

## Impact

Players can buy power-ups in the hangar and keep them between runs, so the hangar's power-up upgrade rows finally mean something — spend salvage, own a power-up, upgrade it, deploy with it.

## Users

- **The hangar player** — sees power-up rows in the unlock tree, buys one with banked salvage, and later upgrades it (`As a player I want a power-up I own in the hangar, not just a 10-second drop`).
- **The defending-bot player** — a defender left after those upgrades inherits the higher permanent level through the existing capture snapshot.
- **The gym maintainer** — `GymHangar` buys the same entry through the same pure rule and the same store write (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).

## Producer decisions (2026-11-17)

- **Q1 = (b) hangar tree/shop entry.** Power-ups become purchasable unlock-tree entries; a purchase is what creates the hangar's first permanent level row. The hex-grant route and the run-carry-over route are **not** taken (the hex boss keeps granting hulls, weapons and modifiers only).
- **Q2 = (ii) explicit owned set.** `HangarState` gains `unlockedPowerUps` as the canonical ownership record (mirroring `unlockedWeapons`), and `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` read power-up ownership from it. A persisted `hangar.powerUpLevels` row still implies ownership, so no stored row is orphaned.
- **Q3 = (1) author the shipped content here.** This item authors at least one buyable, ring-gated, level-bearing power-up entry so a fresh save can own one in normal play — a seam nobody calls would be the same bug again.

## Existing state (evidence)

- **The rule.** `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` decide ownership per kind (`ownsUpgradeableKind`): weapons via `hangar.unlockedWeapons`, power-ups via a `levels.powerUps` row. Non-level-bearing kinds are refused `non-upgradeable` (producer Q2 = (a) of AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU), and the ceiling is `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 5`.
- **Persistence exists but is unmerged.** Commit `ec62c313` on branch `wl-AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH-persist-permanent-levels-through-store-a` adds `hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels` (optional, field-presence migrated), `buyHangarUpgrade`, and the deploy-time grant in `hangarDeployment.ts`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor ec62c313 dev` is **false**, and `dev`'s `parseHangar` parses no level fields — so this item is gated by that branch landing.
- **The tree has no power-ups.** `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — `HangarEntryKind` is `'hull' | 'weapon' | 'modifier'`, `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` is documented as *six buyable entries* plus two starter entries, and `HangarEntry` has no power-up member. `HangarState` has no `unlockedPowerUps` (no such identifier exists in `src/`).
- **Purchase plumbing is generic.** `canBuy` (precedence `owned` → `gated` → `unaffordable`), `buy`, `ownsEntry` and `ownedIds` are kind-driven, so a new kind is a small, compiler-enforced change (`ownedIds` is an exhaustive switch); `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) already renders **every** purchasable catalogue entry with the existing `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING N`/`NEED N min` vocabulary, so the row is nearly free.
- **Two generic catalogue consumers would move with it.** `cheapestUsefulUnlock` (`hangarEconomy.ts`) and `cheapestSeededUnlock` (`src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts`) both scan the whole catalogue, and `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` reports unlock pace over `isPurchasableEntry` entries whose numbers are pinned in docs.
- **Run levels are run-scoped.** `Player.getPowerUpLevels()` reads the run's single `PowerUpLevelStore`; GDD §4.4 states permanence is *scoped to the run* and nothing writes those rows into the hangar.

## Desired change

Power-ups become a fourth unlock-tree kind whose ownership lives in a new persisted `hangar.unlockedPowerUps` set; buying one spends the two-currency price, records ownership **and** seeds its `hangar.powerUpLevels` row at level 1 in one payload write, so the existing upgrade rule and deploy grant work unchanged. At least one level-bearing power-up is authored for sale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. The producer decision is reflected in the design record: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.1/§8.2 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D state that a hangar power-up is **bought from the unlock tree**, owned in `hangar.unlockedPowerUps`, and upgraded by the buy-to-upgrade rule; the `hangarEconomy.ts` comment calling a `powerUpLevels` row *"the only place the hangar records a power-up level"* is corrected to separate level from ownership.
- 2. `HangarEntryKind` gains `'power-up'` with an entry type carrying the shipped `PowerUpId`, name, description, two-currency `HangarPrice`, `minRing` and `starter`, and `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` authors **at least one** level-bearing permanent power-up (from bomb, speed_boost, magnet, mineral_scoop, smart_bomb, frenzy, chrono, salvage, strike, mining_laser) for sale at a reachable ring; consumables and the field-pickup-only kind are never authored as level entries.
- 3. `HangarState` gains `unlockedPowerUps` as the canonical ownership record and the versioned store persists it: parsed defensively (non-list values, duplicates and unusable ids collapse exactly like `unlockedWeapons`), absent in a pre-change save and reading as "owns none" (field-presence migration, **no schema version bump**), and empty in `createDefaultPayload`.
- 4. Buying a power-up through `buy` spends its price, adds the id to `unlockedPowerUps` **and** seeds its `hangar.powerUpLevels` row at `level` 1 in one payload write, so `getPowerUpLevels()` and the deploy grant see it on the very next deployment; a refused purchase changes neither field and spends nothing.
- 5. `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` read power-up ownership from `unlockedPowerUps` (a persisted level row also implies ownership); an unowned power-up is still refused `unowned`, the purchased one offers and buys the next level through the store's `buyHangarUpgrade`, and the deploy path grants the raised level onto the run `Player`.
- 6. The hangar screen renders the new entries through the shared renderer as ordinary unlock rows using the **existing** `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING N`/`NEED N min` states and labels (no new row state invented); the owned-row **upgrade** affordance remains AH-0MWI5AK1E008HDDH's scope; `GymHangar` shows the same rows and buys through the same store write.
- 7. The attract/traversal bot's purchase candidates keep their current kind set (power-up entries are excluded from the bot's choice by one documented helper), so `cheapestUsefulUnlock`/`decideHangarAction` behaviour, `cheapestSeededUnlock` replays and the pinned `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` unlock-pace numbers are unchanged; if the producer prefers the bot to buy power-ups, the affected reports and docs are regenerated in the same change (see Assumptions).
- 8. Tests cover: the new catalogue entry's typing and purchase (price, `gated`, `unaffordable`, `owned` refusal), first level row created by a purchase, upgrade of the now-owned power-up end to end through the store, save/load round-trip of the owned set and the level row, a pre-change save loading with no power-ups and no rows, refusal of a consumable/field-pickup-only id, and the screen's unlock-row states for the new kind.
- 9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- 10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **One ownership record per kind.** `unlockedPowerUps` is canonical; `hangar.powerUpLevels` carries levels only. No third representation, and no parallel ownership check outside `ownedIds`/`ownsUpgradeableKind`.
- **Atomic persistence.** Ownership and the seeded level row land in one `saveHangarWarPayload` write, so a saved purchase can never own a power-up without its level (or the reverse).
- **Level-bearing kinds only.** Consumables (charge pools) and `extra_life` (`fieldPickupOnly`) are never sold as levels; the completed rule's `non-upgradeable` refusal stands and must be covered by a test.
- **Field-presence migration, no schema bump.** `unlockedPowerUps` is additive and optional in the stored payload; absence reads as "owns none".
- **Compiler-enforced kinds.** `ownedIds`/`ownsEntry` must gain the new member through the exhaustive switch — no `default:` fallback that could silently un-own a kind.
- **Loadout and grants untouched.** `resolveActiveLoadout` continues to consider only weapons and modifiers (a power-up entry never becomes a starting weapon); hex grants keep resolving to hulls/weapons/modifiers and the `GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING` sentinel pattern is unchanged.
- **Economy conventions.** Price is the existing `HangarPrice` (minerals + cores), gating is `minRing`, and `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL` stays the single ceiling — no new currency, no second cap.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The pure rule, the renderer and the store write are shared; `GymHangar` gains no divergent copy (duplicate-body guard green).
- **Scope boundary.** The owned-row upgrade affordance is AH-0MWI5AK1E008HDDH; consumable charge purchases, a full pricing pass over all ten kinds, and hex-granted power-ups are separate items.
- **Dependency.** Gated by AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH merging to `dev` (branch `wl-AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH-…`, commit `ec62c313`); without it there is no persisted level field or deploy grant to write into.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — the `'power-up'` kind, the new entry type and the authored sellable power-up(s); the "six buyable entries" comment.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarState.unlockedPowerUps` (persisted contract).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parse of the new set, `createDefaultPayload`, and the purchase write path that seeds the level row.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `ownedIds`, `ownsEntry`, `buy` (seed the level row), `ownsUpgradeableKind` (read the set); the corrected "only place" comment.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — unlock-row rendering for the new kind (shared renderer).
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — the purchase handler persisting through the store.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — gym parity for the buy row.
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` / `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — the documented bot-candidate exclusion helper.
- Tests: `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts`, `hangarWarStore.test.ts`, `hangarScreen`/`HangarScene` tests, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming` tests.

## Assumptions

- **A1 — the attract/traversal bot does not buy power-ups** (AC7): keeps demo decisions, seeded traversal replays and the pinned ring-timing unlock-pace tables stable. Override welcome; then those reports/docs are regenerated here.
- **A2 — authored set and prices**: at least one, recommended 2–3 entries across rings 1–2, priced with the existing two-currency conventions above the starter unlocks; `starter: false` (no free power-up).
- **A3 — a purchase grants level 1**, the rule's own vocabulary, leaving four purchasable steps below `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 5`.
- **A4 — deploy grant** (`applyHangarWarDeployment`) lands with AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH; this item only supplies the rows it grants.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — pinned-report drift.** GDD §8.1's "six buyable entries", `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` unlock-pace tables, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` tables and README counts all describe the tree; a new kind changes what they report. Mitigation: A1's exclusion plus updating every affected doc/report in the same change.
- **Risk — two-field consistency.** A set entry without a level row, or a level row without a set entry, would make ownership and level disagree. Mitigation: seed on purchase, union in the ownership read, round-trip test.
- **Risk — save-shape test churn.** Byte-for-byte payload round-trip tests will need the new empty field's expectation; the field must be omitted-on-empty or explicitly expected, consistently.
- **Risk — unmerged dependency.** AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH is unmerged; building against `dev` today would fork the store path. Mitigation: blocked until it lands (dependency edge recorded).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Pricing all ten kinds, consumable charge sales and hex-granted power-ups are tempting adjacent work. Mitigation: file separately, author the minimum here.
- **Risk — catalogue consumers.** `ringTiming`, `hangarWarTraversal` and `cheapestUsefulUnlock` iterate the whole catalogue; an unguarded new kind silently changes AI/eval behaviour. Mitigation: the A1 exclusion is tested.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH** (discovered-from) — persisted permanent levels + deploy grant; **blocking dependency** (branch unmerged).
- **AH-0MWI5AAVO009UROY** — the pure upgrade rule (completed; its ownership read changes to the new set here).
- **AH-0MWI5AK1E008HDHH** — hangar owned-row upgrade affordance (depends on this item for a row to upgrade).
- **AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU** — parent epic (hangar buy-to-upgrade); its AC2/AC3 power-up half is unreachable without this item.
- **AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6** — hangar economy and unlock tree (completed; owns `canBuy`/`buy` and the catalogue conventions the new kind extends).
- **AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1** — hangar scene unlock tree and deployment selector (completed; the renderer the new rows flow through).
- **AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ** — capture-side snapshot the upgraded level reaches the defender through (completed).
- **AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ**, **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY** — adjacent reward-axis purchase surfaces, explicitly out of scope.
## Plan (2026-11-17)

Effort/risk pre-check: **Medium / Medium** → planning required. Plan-approval gate:
`request_approval: false` (not Extra Large + High/Severe), so no approval pause.

### Decomposition (test-first, dependency order)

1. **Power-up ownership contract tests (red-first)** — AH-0MWKXPIWL007VB8E (task).
   The whole contract pinned before implementation: catalogue typing and purchase
   states, the seeded level-1 row, the ownership union read, store round-trip and
   pre-change-save migration, screen row states, gym parity, deploy grant.
2. **Power-up unlock-tree kind, owned set and authored entry** —
   AH-0MWKXPO5A007R5RB (feature). `HangarEntryKind` + `PowerUpUnlockDefinition` +
   the authored sellable power-up(s); `HangarState.unlockedPowerUps` and its
   field-presence persistence; the two exhaustive switches; the shared renderer's
   rows. Vertical slice: show the row → buy → own it → save/load.
3. **Purchase seeds the level-1 row and the upgrade rule reads the owned set** —
   AH-0MWKXPUGF004RACW (feature). The bug's fix: `buy` seeds
   `hangar.powerUpLevels` at level 1 in the same payload write, and
   `ownsUpgradeableKind` reads `unlockedPowerUps` ∪ a persisted row, so
   purchase → upgrade → deploy works end to end.
4. **Keep power-ups out of the bot's choice and the pinned pace reports** —
   AH-0MWKXQ073003ULDX (task). One documented exclusion helper shared by
   `cheapestUsefulUnlock` and `cheapestSeededUnlock`; pinned ring-timing numbers
   for existing entries unchanged (A1).
5. **Docs: design record, tree counts and README** — AH-0MWKXQ7HU003HIW7 (docs).
   GDD §8.1/§8.2, `OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, README and the catalogue
   doc comment; correct the "powerUpLevels row is the ownership" wording (AC1).
6. **Verification: full suite green** — AH-0MWKXQ98C0060GBM (task). Build, full

### Dependency edges

- (1) blocks (2); (2) blocks (3) and (4); (3) blocks (5); (3), (4) and (5) block (6).

### Vertical-slice check

Each phase cuts every layer: (2) data → contract type → store → pure rule → renderer
→ tests; (3) pure rule → store write → deployment grant → tests; (4) data predicate →
AI/eval consumers → pinned tests; (5) docs; (6) gate. No phase is a single horizontal
layer.

### Assumptions recorded for implementation (agent, override welcome)

- **A5 — `GymHangar` stays read-only.** AC6's "gym buys through the same store
  write" is satisfied by the shared renderer plus the shared pure rule/store write
  that `HangarScene` uses: `GymHangar`'s documented contract is an **injected,
  read-only** payload with no purchase handlers, and adding one would break that
  contract and the gym↔game parity guard. The gym shows the identical rows; the
  buy path is the same `purchaseHangarEntry` → `saveHangarWarPayload` pair, covered
  by tests rather than by a second gym-local handler.
- **A6 — the unlock-pace report keeps its per-entry numbers.** `deriveUnlockPace`
  (an eval report over *buyable* entries, not the bot's choice) gains explicit rows
  for the new power-up entries while every pre-existing row's numbers stay
  byte-identical; its tests pin both.
- **A7 — the owned-row `UPGRADE` affordance comes for free.** `buildUpgradeAffordance`
  is id-driven, so a bought power-up renders the existing `UPGRADE` state once its
  level row exists; no new affordance code is added here (that remains
  AH-0MWI5AK1E008HDDH's weapon-scoped work, already complete).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17 — Plan created: effort/risk pre-check `plan` (Medium/Medium), approval
  gate skipped by policy, six children created in test-first dependency order, AC
  coverage review `proceed` at 100 % parent-AC coverage. Predecessor verification:
  the blocking dependency AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH is now an ancestor of `dev`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **AH-0MWEWZL5B0019XSD** – Close coverage gap: **CVD-safe ownership colouring (producer Q2 = b).** Tile text uses the CVD-safe pair — orange for... (completed)

### Repository file matches

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which surface creates the hangar's first power-up level row?**
  - Q: "Which ownership source should create a hangar power-up's first permanent level row: (a) a hex-boss grant via the capture-cycle grant seam; (b) a hangar tree/shop entry so `canBuy`/`buy` sells ownership; (c) run carry-over at capture; or (d) a combination?"

Research: `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` (`HangarEntryKind`, six buyable entries), `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` (`canBuy`/`buy`/`ownsEntry`/`ownedIds` are kind-driven, `ownedIds` is an exhaustive switch), `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (`buildHangarUnlockRows` renders every purchasable entry), `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (`resolveHexGrant` would misfile a power-up id as a `modifier`), GDD §8 Candidate D vs §8.2 shipped grants.
  - Consequence recorded: the tree gains a fourth kind; the hex-grant and run-carry-over routes are explicitly not taken.

# Turn-churn metric and seeded baseline

## Summary

Add the measurement instrument for the producer's audit rejection of AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 ("still too much left/right turning ... trying to be very precise with its positioning"): a deterministic, machine-checkable **turn-churn** metric over the bot's resolved ship input (A/D turn keys and S retro keys), plus a recorded seeded baseline for the current governor so the smoothing change can be compared.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pure metric module exists in `src/ai/eval/` summarising a per-tick input trace: turn-key duty cycle, direct left-right flips, turn-direction reversals within a window (rate per second), forward-thrust toggles, reverse presses and reverse ticks.
- The metric reads the arena's recorded per-tick input (telemetry `input` field) so any seeded arena run is measurable without new instrumentation; the sample shape is generic so the closed-loop integration harness can feed it too.
- A seeded baseline for the current governor/brain is recorded in the test as a documented constant (turn duty cycle + reversals) so the after-change comparison is explicit and reproducible.
- Unit tests cover counting of flips, reversals inside/outside the window, duty cycle, toggles and rising edges; determinism (same trace -> same summary) is asserted.
- No behaviour change: the shipped bot input is bit-identical (metric only).

## Minimal Implementation

- New `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.ts` with `TurnInputSample`, `TurnChurnSummary`, `summariseTurnChurn(samples, dt, {reversalWindowSeconds})` and `turnSamplesFromTelemetry(records)`.
- Unit tests `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.test.ts`.
- Seeded baseline measurement recorded in the closed-loop governor + ship-physics harness.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.ts` — new metric module
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — telemetry record shapes (read-only)
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — resolved input shape (read-only)

## Impact

Bot tuning now has a reproducible way to prove that a steering or approach change reduces left/right twitching, instead of judging it by eye.

# Turn-control smoothing: wider deadband, flip hysteresis and press hold

## Summary

Stop the bot thrashing its A/D turn keys. The governor currently releases a turn as soon as the instantaneous (or predicted) heading error is inside a tight 0.15 rad tolerance and immediately commands the opposite turn to brake any coast, so the ship limit-cycles around its bearing and reads as constant left/right twitching (producer audit rejection, AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The turn controller uses a **wider alignment deadband** (default `alignmentToleranceRad` 0.30 rad, ~17 degrees) so small heading error no longer commands a turn.
- **Turn hysteresis**: reversing an existing turn direction requires the heading error to exceed the deadband by `turnHysteresisRad` (default 0.25 rad); inside that margin the turn is released (coast) instead of braking with the opposite key, so the ship is allowed to overshoot a little.
- **Flip hold**: once a turn direction is established, the governor may not flip to the opposite direction for `turnFlipHoldMs` (default 120 ms); releasing the key is always immediate, so safety braking is never blocked beyond that window.
- All three parameters are governor tunables surfaced in `tuningFields.ts` (human group) and reachable from GymBotTuning; no new magic numbers in the resolver.
- Legacy behaviour is preserved when the new parameters are zeroed (`turnHysteresisRad: 0`, `turnFlipHoldMs: 0`), proved by a test.
- The seeded turn-churn metric shows a material reduction in turn reversals and turn-key duty cycle versus the pre-change governor on the same seeded runs, with no survival regression (never-suicide property tests still pass).
- Unit tests for the deadband, hysteresis release-vs-brake and flip-hold behaviour.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `BotHumanInputTunables` with `turnHysteresisRad` and `turnFlipHoldMs`; retune `alignmentToleranceRad`.
- Extend `toAsteroidsInput` with an optional turn-state/hysteresis parameter object (positional defaults keep every existing call unchanged).
- Add governor turn-state tracking and flip-hold in `update`.
- Surface the fields in `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — turn controller + governor state
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` — tunable surfacing
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts` — unit tests

## Dependencies

- Turn-churn metric and seeded baseline — the measurement instrument.

## Impact

Players watching the attract demo see the bot press A/D in human-like bursts, stop micro-correcting headings, and let a small overshoot coast out instead of twitching left and right to brake it.

# Overshoot-tolerant approach: pass-through collection and reposition band stop

## Summary

Stop the bot trying to position itself precisely with its thrusters in a drifting, frictionless arena (producer audit rejection, AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2). Pickups are collected on contact, so the bot should fly through them and accept a small overshoot rather than retro-braking onto them and turning back for a pickup it has just passed; and the idle reposition goal should coast to a stop at the edge of its idle band instead of chasing the exact playfield centre and drifting back and forth.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Collection is pass-through**: by default the collect behaviour no longer reverse-brakes onto a pickup (`collectReverseBrake` defaults to `false`), and it thrusts through contact; the retro thruster stays available behind a tunable.
- **Overshoot is accepted**: a mineral/power-up the ship has just passed (behind its velocity vector) within `collectOvershootMargin` (default 60 px) is no longer chased — it drops out of the collection target set so the bot does not U-turn for it, while still being collectable later when it is ahead again.
- **Reposition stops at the band edge**: the reposition behaviour uses the idle band radius as its arrival radius in the forward model, so it coasts to a stop near `repositionRadius` instead of thrusting to the exact centre and overshooting past it.
- New tunables (`collectReverseBrake`, `collectOvershootMargin`) are `CompetentBotTunables` (no magic numbers) and are surfaced in GymBotTuning/tuningFields where a toggle or slider is appropriate.
- Deterministic tests: unit tests for the overshoot filter and the reposition band stop; the closed-loop integration harness shows fewer reverse presses and fewer forward-thrust toggles than the pre-change behaviour on the same seeded runs, with the objective score and survival not regressing.
- Docs updated (framework module headers, README attract/demo note, GDD decision-model section, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` if gym behaviour changes).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `collectReverseBrake` (boolean toggle) and `collectOvershootMargin` (px) to `CompetentBotTunables` + defaults + tuningFields.
- Add a shared overshoot filter in `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` used by the mineral/power-up target selection and the collect behaviour.
- Gate the collect behaviour's `mayReverse` on `collectReverseBrake`; keep `mayThrust` for the forward model.
- Pass `repositionRadius` as the arrival radius in `repositionBehaviour`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — new tunables + defaults
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — overshoot filter in target selection
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — collect pass-through, reposition band stop
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` — surfacing

## Dependencies

- Turn-churn metric and seeded baseline — the measurement instrument (reverse/thrust churn).

## Impact

Players watching the attract demo see a bot that flies through pickups and lets a just-passed one go instead of braking onto it or doubling back, and idles at the edge of its band rather than hunting the exact centre.
data.title: Overshoot-tolerant approach: pass-through collection and reposition band stop

# Test runner crashes with UnboundLocalError when a full-scope suite resolves to no commands

## Problem Statement

`run_tests.py` crashes with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'state_changed_flag'` when a named suite resolves to zero commands. Instead of reporting the empty resolution gracefully, the function references a variable that was never bound.

## Users

- Agent sessions that run the test skill with a named suite (e.g. `--suite node`) that happens to resolve to no commands in the current repo.
- CI / automation that invokes the test runner with varying suites across repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-scope run whose suite resolves to no commands completes without an `UnboundLocalError` — either with an actionable message naming the suite and resolution path, or a clean early return with a zero-command report.
2. The `state_changed_flag` variable is initialised before the command-execution loop (or the loop body guard handles the empty case), so the post-loop aggregation path never touches an unbound variable.
3. A regression test exercises the zero-command path (mocking `commands` to an empty list, or using a suite name that resolves to nothing) and asserts no crash.

## Impact

Users running the test runner against a suite with zero commands get a clear, actionable error message instead of an obscure Python `UnboundLocalError` crash.

## Constraints

- Fix is in a shared skill (`run_tests.py` in the `test` skill scripts); changes must not break existing callers.
- The existing `state_changed_flag` semantics (mid-run checkout movement tracking) must be preserved for the normal non-empty command path.

## Existing State

`run_tests.py` initialises `state_changed_flag` inside the `for cmd in commands:` loop body (line 3188). After the loop, the function reads `state_changed_flag` on line 3281 to populate `state_changed_during_run` in the result dict. When `commands` is empty, the loop body never executes, leaving the name unbound.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Move `state_changed_flag` initialisation before the `for cmd in commands:` loop (line ~3183, after `slot_waits`).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/tests/` — Add regression test for the zero-command path.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The fix is narrowly scoped to the `UnboundLocalError`. Do not refactor other loop-scoped variables (e.g. `command_waits`, `command_elapsed`) unless they show the same pattern.
- **Assumption:** Moving the initialisation before the loop is safe — `state_changed_flag` is reset per-command inside the loop for the normal case. We should verify whether a per-iteration reset is actually needed or whether a single pre-loop initialisation suffices.
- **Risk:** If `state_changed_flag` is intentionally per-command (reset for each iteration), a single pre-loop initialisation may lose the reset semantics. The fix should preserve per-command reset only if the logic requires it; otherwise the pre-loop init is sufficient.

## Related Work

- Discovered from AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 ("Bot oscillates too much") — the agent was running the test skill during implementation and hit this crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Does `state_changed_flag` need per-command reset, or is a single pre-loop initialisation sufficient?" — Answer (Map): A pre-loop initialisation to `None` is sufficient. The per-command reassignment on line 3224 (`state_changed_flag = run.get("state_changed_during_run")`) overwrites the value each iteration; the post-loop read (line 3281) captures the last iteration's value (or `None` if zero iterations). The bug is simply that the declaration line never runs when the loop body is skipped.
data.title: Test runner crashes with UnboundLocalError when a full-scope suite resolves to no commands
