# Intake brief — Hex Map Information UX (AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM)

## Headline

The Hex Map screen (`HexMapScene`) draws roughly fifteen separately positioned
text objects and a ring of tiles with **no sectioning at all**: war status,
transient "what just happened" news, the map itself, the selected hex's intel and
the controls legend all float over the same background, in three different
columns and two different font conventions. This item introduces named,
visually bounded **sections** — each with its own heading — so every group of
information is distinguishable at a glance.

## Problem statement

There is a lot of information on the Hex Map and too little structure holding it
apart. Measured against the shipped renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`,
960×540), the screen currently carries:

| What is drawn | Where it sits today |
|---|---|
| Screen title, and the run result line (`RUN: VICTORY · score N`) | centred, top (`y=18`, `y=46`) |
| Ring progress (`RING 2 — 3/12 HEXES HELD`) | left column (`x=24`, `y=62`) |
| Frontier strength (`FRONTIER · STR n · BEAT ≤ m (k IN REACH)`) | left column (`y=82`) |
| Hangar fleet + bank (`HANGAR · hull · n min · n cores`) | left column (`y=102`) |
| `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` panel (rolled-in defence report) | left column (`y=118`, conditional) |
| `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner (ring won / hangar falls) | left column (`y=300`, conditional) |
| `◀ HANGAR` action row | left column (`y=468`) |
| `READ THE MAP` legend, six lines of static help | right column (`y=112`–`y=182`) |
| `SELECTED HEX — FULL INTEL` detail panel | right column (`y=200`) |
| Hex tiles (`AGG n` + ownership marker + `(q,r)`), attack arrows, hangar marker | centre |
| Keyboard hint line | bottom centre (`y=530`) |

Three problems follow from that inventory:

1. **Unlike information is adjacent, like information is apart.** The three
   left-hand header lines mix ring progress, frontier combat maths and hangar
   inventory with no heading to separate them, while the two halves of "the
   selected hex" (its intel, right column; its attack row, left column) sit on
   opposite sides of the screen.
2. **Transient news has no home.** The run result is centred at the top, the
   hangar-assault outcome is a left-hand banner, and the banked win-bonus line
   (`model.winBonusLine`) is computed but **never drawn at all** — its only
   consumer is the `getWinBonusLine()` test seam. "What just happened" therefore
   arrives in up to three different places, one of which is nowhere.
3. **Help competes with content.** A six-line static legend occupies the top of
   the same right-hand column as the dynamic intel panel it explains, so the
   loudest text in that column is documentation rather than information about
   the player's war.

## Users

- **The Hangar War player** landing on the map between sorties.
  - *As a player, I want the map's status, my last sortie's outcome, the ring
    itself and the selected hex's intel each in their own labelled section, so I
    can find one thing without reading everything.*
  - *As a player, I want to know what just happened (victory/defeat, ring won or
    hangar falls, minerals banked) in one place, so I do not have to hunt three
    corners of the screen for the aftermath of my deployment.*
  - *As a player reading the selected hex, I want its intel and its attack row
    together, so one hex is one story rather than two panels apart.*
  - *As a colour-blind player, I want sections distinguished by headings and
    framing rather than by colour alone, consistent with the map's existing
    CVD-safe conventions.*
- **The maintainer** of the shared `buildHexMapModel` → `renderHexMap` pair,
  who needs the section layout to live in one renderer so the game and the
  `GymHexWar` parity gym cannot drift (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

## Producer decisions (2026-11-17)

- **Q1 = (a)** — sections are **bordered, headed panels** laid out in fixed
  columns; every section has a frame, a heading and a bounded rect.
- **Q2 = (b)** — **four content sections plus a controls footer**: WAR STATUS,
  LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX (intel **and** its attack row together), and
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
- **Q3 = (a)** — the banked win-bonus line **is rendered**, inside LAST SORTIE.

## Section model (producer-approved)

Four content sections plus a controls footer, each drawn as a **bordered,
headed panel** with a bounded rect:

| Section | Contains | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| `war-status` | ring progress, frontier strength / beatable ceiling / in-reach count, hangar hull + banked minerals/cores | always |
| `last-sortie` | run result line, banked win bonus, hangar-assault outcome (`RING WON…` / `HANGAR FALLS…`) | only when the landing carries one of those |
| `map` | the ring tiles, attack arrows and hangar marker | always |
| `selected-hex` | the focused hex's full intel **and** its `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` row | always (panel body may be empty when nothing is focused) |
| `controls` | keyboard hint line + the `READ THE MAP` legend | always |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Section registry on the shared view.** `HexMapView` publishes a `sections`
  list — `{ key, heading, rect }` per rendered section — and every rendered text
  object, tile and arrow lies inside **exactly one** section rect, with no two
  section rects overlapping and every rect inside the 960×540 frame.
- **Every section is a bordered, headed panel (Q1 = a).** Each of `war-status`,
  `last-sortie` (when shown), `map`, `selected-hex` and `controls` draws a panel
  frame and one heading from a shared exported constant (`WAR STATUS`,
  `LAST SORTIE`, `SELECTED HEX`, `CONTROLS`, and the map's own title), in one
  consistent style and position convention, so the groupings are distinguishable
  without relying on colour.
- **No information is lost.** Every string the current renderer draws still
  renders, in its new section; the tile labels (`AGG n`, ownership marker,
  `(q,r)`), arrows, hint line and legend text are unchanged in content.
- **Transient news is grouped and complete (Q2 = b, Q3 = a).** The run result
  line, the hangar-assault banner and the banked win-bonus line
  (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`, from `model.winBonusLine`) render **only**
  inside `last-sortie`; the win-bonus line is now actually drawn, not merely
  queryable. When the landing carries none of the three, the section is absent
  (no empty headed box).
- **One hex, one section.** The selected hex's intel and its attack row render
  inside the same `selected-hex` section; the attack row is hidden (not moved to
  another section) when the focused hex is in no attack.
- **Help no longer competes with content.** The `READ THE MAP` legend moves into
  the `controls` section and no longer occupies the intel column.
- **Legibility at 960×540.** No section body text overdraws a hex tile or the
  hangar marker; long strings (draw name, assault arithmetic) word-wrap inside
  their section; no rendered text is smaller than today's smallest (9px) and
  headings are at least 10px.
- **Game/gym parity, one shared layout.** All layout lives in
  `renderHexMap`/`hexMap.ts`; `GymHexWar` renders the same sections read-only
  through the same call, and no gym-local or scene-local layout exists (the
  existing `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions stay green).
- **Interaction contract unchanged.** Grid arrow navigation, Tab/Shift+Tab
  cycling, Enter/Space inspect-or-deploy, tile hover/click, the `◀ HANGAR` row
  and ESC-to-menu behave exactly as before; the attract traversal still takes
  exactly one next action and cannot stall on a section.
- **Regression coverage.** `HexMapScene.test.ts`, the renderer/`hexIntel` tests
  and `GymHexWar.test.ts` pin the section registry (keys, headings, non-overlap,
  in-frame), `last-sortie` visibility toggling, and that the selected-hex intel
  and attack row share a section; position-only pins may be updated, behaviour
  pins may not be weakened.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** — GDD §8.2 (the
  map's screen surface), the `hexMap.ts` module docblock, and
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` if its row description changes.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A Hangar War player can read the map at a glance: the war's status, the last
sortie's outcome, the ring itself, the selected hex's intel and the controls each
sit in their own labelled section instead of scattering across three columns.

## Constraints

- **Renderer-only change.** The model (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) stays
  the single source of every string; `hexMap.ts` only draws and positions. No
  gameplay rule, resolver call or persisted state is added.
- **One layout for game and gym.** The gym↔game parity contract and the existing
  `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions forbid a second layout implementation.
- **Single 960×540 viewport.** No scrolling, panning, tabs or collapsible
  sections unless the producer chooses the tabbed option in Q1.
- **Transient launch data stays transient** — run result, tick record, assault
  and win bonus are never persisted; a later entry renders no `last-sortie`.
- **Existing CVD-safe conventions hold** — section distinction must not depend on
  colour; the tile ownership encoding (blue/orange + filled/hollow marker) is
  untouched.
- **No new assets or fonts** — monospace text and Phaser Graphics panels only.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (951 lines) holds every layout constant
  (`PANEL_X`, `ATTACK_PANEL_Y`, `ASSAULT_BANNER_Y`, legend rows, hint line) and
  draws all of the inventory above. There is no section abstraction: each text
  object is positioned by a hand-tuned literal.
- `HexMapView` already exposes behavioural seams (`getRows`, `getArrows`,
  `getPanelText`, `getLeftPanelText`, `getAssaultText`, …) but nothing describing
  screen regions, so no test can currently assert grouping or non-overlap.
- `model.winBonusLine` exists (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` →
  `defenceReport.ts`) and is surfaced only by `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`;
  the renderer never draws it.
- Prior work already fixed the map's *readability* (reveal filter, CVD-safe tiles,
  coordinates, titled detail-panel lines) and its *navigation* (grid arrows), so
  this item is the remaining structural/visual-hierarchy step.

## Desired change

A sectioned Hex Map: a small number of named, bounded regions with headings, each
holding one kind of information, drawn by the shared renderer so the game and the
parity gym stay identical; transient sortie news gathered into one place; the
selected hex's intel and attack row brought together; help demoted to a controls
footer.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the whole layout: section rects, headings,
  legend relocation, last-sortie grouping; add `sections` to `HexMapView`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — shared section-heading constants and any
  model wiring for the last-sortie lines (`winBonusLine` is already published)
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — query seam for `sections`, transient launch data
  plumbing (no rule change)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — renders the same sections read-only
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — section/grouping pins; update
  position-only assertions
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — describe the
  sectioned map surface

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed): the
  scene and its intel model this item re-lays-out.
- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** — Hangar Map UX (completed, parent): reveal filter,
  CVD-safe ownership, coordinates on tiles, spatial arrows — the readability and
  navigation pass that precedes this structural one.
- **AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK** — Hangar Map UI: clearer overview (completed): titled
  every line of the selected-hex intel. Its line titles are load-bearing for
  this item's `selected-hex` section and must not be disturbed.
- **AH-0MWEWYUAS002P7P9** — Renderer: CVD-safe labels, reveal filter, owned-hex
  selection (completed); **AH-0MWEWYVD7008PPQT** — Navigation: grid columns
  (completed): both pin renderer behaviour this item must preserve.
- **AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP** — Defence report rolled into the hex map (completed):
  source of the attack arrows and the left-hand attack panel now moved into
  `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEZZA4E0081NJ5** — Assault defence report and reset announcement
  (completed): source of the `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner now grouped under
  `last-sortie`.
- **AH-0MWF0CWB7002MG2F** — Special-mission intel (completed): the `★ SPECIAL`
  tile tag whose detail-panel block lives in `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** — Win path: bank a fixed post-win bonus (open): owns the
  `winBonusLine` whose presentation Q3 decides.
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** — Text on hex map is unreadable (completed): the
  legibility baseline this item must not regress.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** – Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed)
- **AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU** – Player has no audio (completed)
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** – Text on hex map is unreadable (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: clearly, create, easily, group, hex, hexmap, identify, information, logical, lot, make, map, much, page, presented, sections, sense, there
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: clearly, create, distinguishable, group, hex, hexmap, lot, make, map, much, page, sections, there
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: create, group, hex, hexmap, logical, lot, make, map, much, page, presented, there

Keyword false positive: `AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU` (audio) matched on generic words
(`make`, `there`) and is not related to this item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Clutter inversion.** More framing can add more visual noise than it removes;
  mitigation: a small fixed section count (4 + footer by default), one heading
  style, and the non-overlap/fit assertions as the guard.
- **Text reflow collisions.** Wrapped draw names and long assault arithmetic are
  the strings that collide at 960×540; mitigation: wrap widths inside each
  section rect plus the "no body text overdraws a tile" assertion.
- **Parity drift.** A scene-local tweak would break gym↔game parity; mitigation:
  all layout in `hexMap.ts`, with the existing equivalence assertions kept.
- **Test churn on positions.** Several suites assert coordinates indirectly;
  mitigation: pin sections structurally (`sections` registry) rather than by
  literal pixel offsets, and update only position-only assertions.
- **Scope creep** into a full visual redesign, new fonts, or tabbed navigation;
  such opportunities are recorded as new linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** headings are monospace text in the existing style (no new
  assets); **assumption:** the attract/demo traversal gains no new state, because
  every section is read-only like today's panels.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — How should the sections be delineated?**
  (a) Bordered, headed panels in fixed columns — every section has a frame, a
  heading and a bounded rect (recommended).
  (b) Headed bands with separator rules only — headings plus horizontal rules,
  no boxes, more breathing space over the map background.
  (c) Collapsible/tabbed sections — only one section expanded at a time, cutting
  on-screen text but adding interaction state and hidden information.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a frame per section is the most unambiguous
  distinction, needs no new interaction, and is directly assertable (rect +
  heading + non-overlap) by the existing scene/renderer tests.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** bordered, headed panels in fixed
  columns. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q2 (ANSWERED, producer chose (b)) — Which grouping taxonomy should the map use?**
  (a) Six sections: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX, ATTACK,
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
  (b) Four sections plus a footer: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX
  (intel **and** its attack row together), CONTROLS/LEGEND (recommended).
  (c) Keep today's regions and only add headings/separators to each.
  **Recommended:** (b) — it separates the three genuinely unlike kinds of
  information (war state, transient news, focused-hex detail) while keeping one
  hex's intel and attack row together, and it avoids the extra section that
  option (a) spends on material that is about the same focused hex.
  Research: the inventory in *Problem statement* comes from
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`; the attack panel and the detail panel are both
  keyed by the focused hex (`model.attackDetails` / `displayedHexKey`), which is
  what makes (b) coherent.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (b)** four sections plus a controls footer,
  with the focused hex's intel and its attack row in one `selected-hex` section.
  Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q3 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — Should the banked win-bonus line be
  rendered as part of this item?**
  (a) Yes — render `model.winBonusLine` (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`) inside
  LAST SORTIE (recommended).
  (b) No — leave it query-only and record it as deliberately out of scope.
  (c) Remove the unused line/model field entirely.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the line already exists and is tested through the query
  seam; without it the "what just happened" section silently omits a reward the
  player just earned, and it is a one-line addition to a section this item is
  already building.
  Research: `winBonusLine` is produced by `defenceReport.ts` and republished by
  `hexIntel.ts`; `hexMap.ts` never draws it and `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`
  is its only reader.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** render `model.winBonusLine` inside
  `last-sortie`. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q4 (recorded, not blocking) — Is a repo/gym search needed for the selected-hex
  line titles?** Answered by inspection of AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK: the titles
  (`ID:`, `STATE:`, `BOSS:`, `STRENGTHS:`, …) are shipped and are treated as a
  fixed input here. Source: work item description + `hexIntel.ts` constants.

# Procedurally generated Hex Map

## Problem statement

The hex ring's **shape** is already generated at runtime from the shared `6 × n`
geometry, but its **content** — boss identity, strengths/weaknesses, the granted
weapon or upgrade, base aggression and the optional variety axes — is
hand-authored data for rings 1 and 2 only, so the war stops where that table
ends. The producer has decided that **every ring should be procedurally
generated from the war's seeded RNG**: the same `(seed, ringIndex)` always yields
the same ring, and the frontier has no authored ceiling.

## Users

- **Player** — "Every war's map is generated from its seed, the frontier never
  stops at ring 2, and the same seed replays the same map."
- **Designer** — "I no longer author a table per ring, and the generator honours
  the shipped ring rules so procedural rings stay balanced and readable."
- **Test/agent** — "The generated ring is a pure function of `(seed, ringIndex)`,
  so I can assert determinism and run it headlessly in the gym with game
  parity."

## Producer decisions (recorded this intake)

- **Q1 = B — all rings procedural.** Rings 1 and 2 are generated from the seed
  like every other ring; `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the CSV seeds are retired as
  the runtime content source.
- **Q2 = A — pure function of `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on
  demand.** Only the existing `HexState` is persisted; stored rings are never
  regenerated.
- **Q3 = A — cycle real catalogue grants with level scaling.** Larger rings
  repeat catalogue entries and each repeat raises an upgrade/weapon level
  (capped).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated ring content is a **pure, deterministic function of
  `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`**: the same seed/ring yields identical hexes (ids,
  coordinates, boss, strengths/weaknesses, grant, base aggression and variety
  axes), and at least two distinct seeds yield materially different rings.
- The authored runtime table `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the `hex-ring-1.csv` /
  `hex-ring-2.csv` seeds are **retired as the runtime content source** (no scene
  or runtime path imports authored ring content; the CSV parity test is removed
  or replaced), and rings 1 and 2 generate from the seed like every other ring.
- Every generated ring satisfies the shipped design invariants, validated
  loudly rather than repaired: exactly one weapon hex and it is the ring's
  hardest, one special-mission hex granting a hull, at least one beatable hex,
  unique ids and coordinates, and the aggression band/budget rules.
- **Grant economy:** the generator prefers unowned catalogue entries; when a
  ring exhausts them it cycles level-capable entries and each repeat raises the
  weapon/power-up level (capped at `MAX_LEVEL`), while unlevellable repeats
  (hull/modifier) bank a mineral payout; every granted hex resolves to a real
  effect (never a silent no-op).
- **Existing saves remain playable and unchanged**: a stored ring (full or
  partial) is never regenerated or discarded; a fresh/empty ring generates from
  the seed; defensive parse and migration behaviour is covered by tests.
- Unit, property and integration tests cover determinism, distinct-seed
  variety, invariant enforcement across many seeds and large ring indices, the
  grant-economy rule, and the save/load round-trip; `GymHexWar` renders the same
  generated model as the game.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can push the frontier indefinitely: every war's hex map is generated
from its seed rather than stopping where hand-authored content ends.

## Constraints

- **One seeded stream.** Generation draws from the shipped seeded RNG
  (`createSeededRng` / `createHangarWarRng`, `normaliseSeed`) — no `Math.random`
  in content decisions. Draws must be derived per `(seed, ringIndex)` (and per
  hex) so a change in one ring cannot shift another ring's map.
- **Pure and headless.** The generator lives in the pure core
  (`src/core/hangarWar/`) with no Phaser, storage or scene dependency, so the
  map scene and `GymHexWar` share exactly one code path (gym↔game parity).
- **Preserve the published map.** The known-ahead intel promise (boss,
  strengths/weaknesses, aggression, grant) and the `6 × n` shape are unchanged;
  only *where content comes from* changes.
- **Finite grant vocabulary.** The hangar catalogue holds roughly 12–14 entries
  (hulls, weapons, modifiers, defence-skill), while ring 3 needs 18 distinct
  grants and ring *n* needs `6 × n` — so the level-scaling repeat rule (Q3 = A)
  is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
- **Deterministic identity.** Generated boss identities and hex ids must be
  stable for a seed and traceable in telemetry; hex ids must stay unique within
  the ring and stable across reloads.
- **No new combat implementations.** Personalities resolve through the existing
  bounded vocabularies (`HEX_PERSONALITY_IDS`, `HEX_LANDMARK_IDS`) and shared
  mechanics; generation only assigns them (at most one weapon hex and one
  special mission per ring).
- Aggression stays a whole number in `[0, 9]`; the frontier budget and
  beatable-hex invariants are preserved.

## Existing state

- **Shape generated, content authored.** `ringCoordinates` / `ringSize` compute
  the `6 × n` geometry; `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`)
  authors rings 1 (6 hexes) and 2 (12 hexes). `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv`
  mirror that table and a parity test fails if they drift.
- **No shipped ring 3.** The only ring-3 content is test fixture data
  (`VARIETY_RING_DEFINITIONS` in
  `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`); `aggressionScenarios.ts`
  already synthesises a deterministic placeholder shape for "ring 3+" in the
  harness — precedent, not shipping code.
- **Materialisation** goes through `materialiseRing` / `openNextRing`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`), which call `createRingState` and leave
  the ring unchanged when an authored successor is missing, so a war stalls at
  the last authored ring.
- **Seeded RNG and seed plumbing exist.** The payload carries a normalised
  `seed` (set from the run seed when a war starts); `createHangarWarRng` exposes
  `next`/`nextInt`/`pick` over the shipped mulberry32 stream, and
  `specialRotationSeed` demonstrates per-index stream mixing.
- **Precedent for generation modes.** AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT shipped per-wave
  `curve` / `fixed` / `dynamic` modes (`dynamic` = regenerated at runtime, seeded
  from the run RNG, reproducible per seed) — the project already has the
  vocabulary for seeded content.
- **The original intake premise was half right:** geometry is runtime-generated,
  content was build-time authored data.

## Desired change

Replace the authored ring-content source with a seeded generator used by **all**
rings. The generator produces a complete, valid `HexRingDefinition`-shaped ring
for any ring index from `(seed, ringIndex)` using the shared RNG and the shipped
catalogues/vocabularies, and flows through the existing materialisation, intel,
map and capture seams. Definition lookup by hex id must be derivable from the
same seed, and repeated catalogue grants must level up rather than no-op.

## **Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — add the seeded ring-content generator; keep
  `validateRingDefinitions` / `generateRing` pure and reuse them.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` — add a per-ring/per-hex derived stream (mirroring
  `specialRotationSeed`); do not add a second generator.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — retire the authored runtime table; keep only
  catalogue/vocabulary exports the generator draws from.
- `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`,
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — retire the seed/parity pair.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing` / `openNextRing` and
  grant application (`withGrantedEntry`) generate on demand and apply the
  level-scaling repeat rule.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/specialMission.ts` —
  definition lookup by id and the default definitions source consult the
  generator.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts`, `hexDifficulty.ts`, `hexDefence.ts` — the
  profile, aggression band and budget rules the generator must satisfy.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts` — the grant pool and the
  level caps (`MAX_LEVEL`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — remove the
  authored default and verify one rendered code path.
- Fixtures/tests: `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`,
  `aggressionScenarios.ts`, `hexVarietyDocs.test.ts`, gym/doc parity tests.
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and module comments.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** — Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions
  (completed). Origin of `hexRing.ts`, `validateRingDefinitions` and the authored
  rings; its producer decision chose authored content, which this item now
  reverses by producer decision (Q1 = B).
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed,
  hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration (completed). Closest
  precedent: a `dynamic` mode regenerated at runtime from the run RNG,
  reproducible per seed.
- **AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7** — Hex variety data vocabulary, fixtures and loud
  validation (completed). Defines the personality/contract/landmark vocabularies
  the generator assigns.
- **AH-0MWB9V9Q3004HD2P** — HexMap aggression increases too quickly (completed).
  The aggression budget/band rules procedural rings must honour.
- **AH-0MWJ51KUS005WQK6**, **AH-0MWF0CTQB001XFE1** — special-mission hexes;
  **AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH** — ring landmarks. The invariants the generator must
  preserve.
- **AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB** — Held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES map action (blocked,
  tangential): consumes the map read model; generated rings must not regress it.
- **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5** — Rebalance ring 2's grind budget (open, tangential):
  generated aggression must not reintroduce the grind problem it tracks.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Blast radius (main risk).** Retiring the authored table and CSV seeds reaches
  many tests, fixtures, scenes and docs that import `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`.
  Planning should decompose this as an epic into: generator, retirement/migration,
  definition-lookup wiring, grant level-scaling, save compatibility, and
  tests/docs.
- **Determinism contract.** Adding a field or changing a draw order changes every
  seed's map. Treat the draw sequence as a versioned contract and pin it with
  golden tests; scope generation to the pure `(seed, ringIndex)` inputs.
- **Tutorial variance.** Ring 1 is now seed-dependent: every war opens on a
  different ring. If the first war must stay a fixed tutorial, that is a separate
  decision; this brief assumes the producer's all-procedural choice stands.
- **Grant-economy detail.** Q3 = A did not specify repeats of entries with no
  level dimension (hull/modifier). Assumption: prefer unowned entries, level up
  level-capable repeats to `MAX_LEVEL`, and bank a mineral payout for
  unlevellable repeats (reusing the shipped banking rule). Confirm or correct.
- **Validation cost.** Decide whether generated rings are validated on every
  materialisation, only in tests/CI, or once per ring open.
- **Save compatibility.** A stored ring must never be regenerated or lost; an
  old/absent payload must parse defensively. Add a migration test.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Turning this into a new-boss / new-mechanic content suite
  would balloon it. Extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items, not
  folded into this one.

## Open questions

None outstanding — Q1–Q3 are answered. The documented assumptions above (grant
repeats for hulls/modifiers, tutorial variance, validation cadence) are recorded
so the producer can correct them without blocking the plan.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Which rings become procedural, and does the authored content stay?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B — all rings procedural**, including
  rings 1–2; retire `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the CSV seeds and regenerate
  rings 1–2 from a seed too. Evidence: options recorded in comment
  `AH-C0MWLAGDNN006KLTX`; research inspected
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, `src/data/hex-ring-*.csv` and
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`.
- **Q2 — How is a generated ring reproduced and stored?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — pure function of
  `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on demand**; persist only the existing
  `HexState`, no schema migration. Evidence: comment `AH-C0MWLAGECE008CFOM`;
  research inspected `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (`materialiseRing`),
  `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` (`HangarWarPayload.seed`) and
  `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`.
- **Q3 — How should generated rings source grants once the catalogue runs out?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — cycle real catalogue grants with
  level scaling**; repeats raise an upgrade/weapon level (capped). Evidence:
  comment `AH-C0MWLAGEWP002U2ZA`; research counted ~12–14 catalogue entries in
  `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` against ring 3's 18 required grants, and
  confirmed `withGrantedEntry` currently only adds an owned id (no level raise).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** – Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions (completed)
- **AH-0MWJ4ZDXO007VDJS** – Author shipped hex variety content on ring 1 (one landmark and one contract) (completed)
- **AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0** – Rush push into the next ring is playable (AC8 gap) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, 0mwfdqcfv007bze5, 0mwj51kus005wqk6, absent, acceptance (+453 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, 0mwfdqcfv007bze5, 0mwj51kus005wqk6, absent, acceptance (+428 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, absent, acceptance, action, add (+357 more)

# Completing a hex battle means the equipped hulls/weapons/plugins are reset

## Problem statement

The hangar currently treats the **whole fleet as permanent**: a deployed ship is not consumed when a battle ends, and buying an upgrade does not arm it. The producer wants each deployed ship to be a **one-battle consumable** — the flown hull, its equipped starting weapons and modifiers, and their bought permanent levels are spent on **win or loss** — while owned items the player did not fly, and the free starter kit, survive. Re-fitting a new ship must be quick, so **buying an upgrade should enable it immediately**, and a follow-on item will add saved ship configurations for one-action re-purchase.

## Users

- **Primary — the player** building and flying ships through the hex war.
- **Secondary — the balance/progression owner**, because the salvage economy must now fund re-fitting after every sortie.

Example user stories:

- As a player, after a battle I want the ship I flew to be spent, so each sortie is a real commitment and losing one costs me the ship, not my whole collection.
- As a player, I want buying an upgrade to arm it immediately, so re-fitting a new ship takes one action per part instead of buy-then-hunt-for-equip.
- As a player, I want the owned items I did not fly to survive, so a bad run never erases my progress.
- As a player, I want to keep the free starter hull and starter weapon, so I can always deploy after a wipe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On completion of a hex deployment — **win or loss** — the deployed ship is removed from the hangar payload: the deployed hull (unless it is the free starter hull), every starting weapon in the hangar's active loadout (unless it is the free starter weapon), every modifier in that loadout, and the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows for those consumed ids are deleted. Every owned item the player did not deploy, and the free starter kit, remain owned.
- After the consumption the hangar is reset to the free starter kit: `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty, so the next deployment uses only the free starter kit until the player re-purchases. The player's `bankedMinerals` and `bankedCores` are unchanged by consumption (the existing win bonus still applies on a win).
- A successful hangar purchase **auto-enables** the entry: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, and a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers`; a refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership nor the loadout. This deliberately supersedes the economy's current "buying never equips" rule for the hangar screen, while other callers can keep the old behaviour through an explicit option.
- Automated tests cover both outcome paths and the purchase paths through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity): win and loss consumption, starter-kit survival, un-flown owned items surviving, consumed items' level rows removed, no soft-lock with an empty loadout, demo mode not overwriting the player's war, and auto-enable plus refusal for hull/weapon/modifier.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

After every hex battle the ship you flew is spent and you rebuild from the salvage you earned — and because buying an upgrade now arms it immediately, re-fitting a new ship takes fewer steps and each sortie feels like a real commitment.

## Constraints

- **No soft-lock.** The free starter hull (`hull-1`) and starter weapon (`spread`) are always owned; an empty loadout is legal (deploy with the ship's permanent cannon only, AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D).
- **One payload write per battle** through the existing `saveHangarWarPayload`; defensive parsing stays the authority; no schema-version bump expected because the shape is unchanged.
- **Demo/attract runs never overwrite the player's war** — the existing `_saveHangarWarPayload` demo guard must keep holding for the consumed payload.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The consumption rule lives in the pure core and is exercised by the headless harness; no scene-only logic.
- **Supersedes a prior decision.** `hangarEconomy.buy()` currently documents that "buying only grants ownership — equipping stays the deployment selector's job" (A5/A6). This item overrides that for the hangar screen only.
- **Separate concern left alone.** The ring-end hangar-falls reset (`resetCampaign`, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J) already wipes both axes and is unchanged.
- **No new balance tuning.** The existing win bonus (`bankWinBonus` / `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS`) already provides the "wins pay more" difference the producer described.

## Existing state

- `buy()` in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` spends the price and adds the entry to the owned set, but deliberately does **not** equip it.
- `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` in `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` clone the payload and currently **preserve** `hangar.activeHull` and `hangar.activeLoadout`.
- `HangarWarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) already carries the deployed `hullId`, `startingWeapons`, `modifiers` and the carried war `payload`, so the scene has the ship identity at battle end.
- `parseHangar` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) restores `activeHull` / `activeLoadout`; `createDefaultPayload` seeds the starter hull and starter weapon as owned, not equipped.
- Permanent levels live in `hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels`.
- Precedent: `resolveHexCapture` already derives the hex's defending bot from the deployed hull (`leaveDefender`), so "the flown hull is spent" fits the existing capture model.

## Desired change

- Add a **pure consumption reducer** (for example `consumeDeployedShip(hangar, ship, catalogue)`) that removes the flown hull, equipped starting weapons and modifiers plus their level rows, resets `activeHull` to the starter hull and clears `activeLoadout`, and preserves the starter kit and every un-flown owned item.
- Apply it on **both** the win path (`resolveHexCapture`) and the loss path (`resolveDeploymentDefeat`), driven by the deployment's hull and the hangar's active loadout.
- Add **auto-enable on purchase** to the hangar purchase path (`purchaseHangarEntry` / `buy` with an explicit `equipOnPurchase` option), keeping `buy`'s default non-equipping behaviour for other callers.
- Update the hangar screen so a purchase reads as equipped immediately, and update the affected unit/integration tests and docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — add the pure `consumeDeployedShip` reducer and an `equipOnPurchase` option on `buy`; keep the default non-equipping for other callers.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — consume on the `resolveHexCapture` win path and the `resolveDeploymentDefeat` loss path; thread the deployed ship into both.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — expose the exact equipped set (hull + active loadout) that consumption applies to.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the deployment's hull/loadout into the capture and defeat resolvers.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `purchaseHangarEntry` uses `equipOnPurchase` and renders the auto-equipped state immediately.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — persist the auto-equipped purchase through the same payload write.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — confirm the consumed/auto-equipped payload round-trips; no schema bump expected.
- Tests beside each module plus the `hangarWarFlow` integration test.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Economy treadmill.** Consuming the flown ship every battle could feel punitive, especially after a loss. Mitigation: wins pay more salvage (existing bonus), and the saved-configuration follow-on (AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7) makes re-fitting one action; validate against the ring-timing budgets before advancing.
- **Soft-lock.** Consumption must never remove the starter kit or leave no deployable ship. Mitigation: always retain `hull-1` and `spread`, and keep the empty-loadout rule (AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D); test it.
- **Silent loss of un-flown levels.** Removing level rows must target only the deployed ids. Mitigation: consume the resolved deployed ids only, and assert un-flown `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` rows survive.
- **Split writes.** Consumption, banking and the win bonus must land in one `saveHangarWarPayload` write. Mitigation: pure reducer plus a single persist, with a test that the balance and ownership cannot diverge.
- **Demo leakage.** An attract/demo run must never consume the player's war. Mitigation: the existing demo guard on `_saveHangarWarPayload`; test it.
- **Scope creep.** Auto-enable could grow into a full loadout-preset system; that is deliberately split into AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7. Price, win-bonus and ring-economy tuning stay out of scope.
- **Stale loadout references.** A save whose active loadout names items no longer owned is already filtered by `resolveActiveLoadout`; consumption must operate on resolved ids, not raw stored ids.

**Assumptions:** both outcomes consume the ship (Q2 = B); only deployed items are consumed (Q4 = B); the ring-end hangar-falls reset is unchanged; and "the ship" is the hangar's active loadout as shown, not the six-slot post-cap run set.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6** — Capture cycle: hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (the win path this item extends).
- **AH-0MVUXC2DD003HN0I** — Hangar War menu entry, mode separation and deployment (the deployment payload this item consumes).
- **AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J** — Capture-cycle assault gate (the ring-end hangar-falls reset; deliberately unchanged).
- **AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ** — Strengthen a hex's defence (a nearby economy change to co-ordinate with).
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons in the loadout (empty-loadout legality this item must preserve).
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7** — Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action (the follow-on created from this intake; depends on this item).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D persistence rules), `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 (capture cycle), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWB8VFBC003743Y** – Requote docs and reconcile ring-timing guards (completed)
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7** – Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action (blocked)
- **AH-0MWB8VDDI005WVMG** – Pin per-ring loadout resolution in tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: battle, build, cases, cores, defend (+28 more)
- `README.md` — matched: battle, build, cases, cores, defend (+27 more)
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — matched: battle, build, cores, defend, earned (+25 more)

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What should the hangar show after a hex battle (win or loss)?** — Answer (producer): **C, refined** — the deployed ship is genuinely consumed on both outcomes and **all its upgrades must be re-purchased**; when an upgrade is purchased it is **automatically enabled**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q1 follow-on — add saved ship configurations?** — Answer (producer): **yes** — save ship configurations and select them from a drop-down to quickly purchase the needed upgrades. Created as **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Should winning and losing differ?** — Answer (producer): **B** — winning also consumes the deployed hull (it is left as the hex's defender); losing destroys it. The difference is economic: a win pays more salvage to equip a new ship. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Bug or design change?** — Answer (producer): **B** — this is a design-change request, not a defect report. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — After a hex battle, how much of the fleet must be re-purchased?** — Answer (producer): **B** — only the deployed ship is consumed: its equipped hull, equipped weapons, equipped modifiers and their levels are removed; owned items the player did not fly, and the free starter kit, survive. Source: interactive reply.

**Assumptions carried:** the free starter hull and starter weapon are always owned (no soft-lock); un-equip toggles remain available after an auto-equip; and the existing win bonus already supplies the "wins pay more" difference, so no new balance tuning is in scope.

## Traceability

- Duplicate check performed — no open or completed item covers ship consumption on battle completion; the closest items are the capture-cycle, assault-gate and defender items listed above, which this item extends rather than duplicates.

# Graze and Danger Multiplier

Discovered from: the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 10 of 10 — highest expected enjoyment; direction: create, **High** priority).

## Goal (user story)

As a player threading a dense bullet pattern, I want a near miss to be worth
points and to build a visible multiplier, so that the most skilful thing I do —
flying close to danger — is rewarded rather than merely survived.

## Problem statement

Dodging is currently un-rewarded. Score (GDD §4.5) is a flat per-kill sum plus a
per-level time bonus; there is no multiplier, combo, graze or grade anywhere in
`src/` (verified: no `graze` / `nearMiss` / scoring-`combo` identifiers — the
only `multiplier` hits are bot-tuning and hull speed multipliers). The genre's
strongest retention lever, turning near misses into score, is absent, so a
skilled player and a cautious player are separated only by survival time.

Evidence of the gap:

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_handleCollisions` resolves the player /
  enemy-bullet overlap against a fixed radius with no proximity branch, so the
  band between "hit" and "near miss" is invisible and unpaid.
- The player's collision footprint (≈14 px, `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`
  `PLAYER_HIT_RADIUS`) is already smaller than the 20 px hull art, so a natural
  graze band exists that the player can neither see nor be paid for.

## The mechanic (full proposal)

1. **Graze band.** A graze is recorded when a live enemy bullet or a live enemy
   body passes within `grazeRadius` of the ship's collision centre and outside
   the hit radius, where `grazeRadius = playerHitRadius + GRAZE_BAND` (initial
   `GRAZE_BAND = 12 px`). Judged on the shared collision centre and radius
   helpers, never on sprite bounds. Asteroids and other contact hazards graze
   too — they can kill on contact.
2. **Credit once per pass.** Each hostile object can be grazed once per pass.
   Credit is keyed by a stable per-object id and clears when the object is
   destroyed, when its lifetime expires, or when it leaves the band by more
   than a hysteresis margin (`GRAZE_HYSTERESIS = 4 px`) — so a bullet hovering
   at the band edge cannot farm score.
3. **Danger multiplier.** Five tiers: `×1 → ×1.5 → ×2 → ×3 → ×5`. Each graze
   contributes a fixed amount of tier progress (`GRAZE_TIER_PROGRESS = 1`, so
   the top tier is reached at a tunable count), and inactivity decays the
   multiplier one tier every `GRAZE_DECAY_SECONDS = 2.0`. Kill score is
   multiplied by the current tier, rounded half up, at the existing score seam.
4. **A player hit ends the chain** — the multiplier resets to `×1`, so the risk
   is real and the reward is for *staying* clean.
5. **Legibility.** A spark arc at the nearest point of the grazed object, a
   rising pitch cue per tier, a HUD `DANGER ×N` tacho that drains as the decay
   timer runs, and a distinct flash on tier loss. The signal is never carried
   by colour alone (a shape/pulse difference accompanies each tier).
6. **Purity and parity.** The whole rule lives in one pure module
   (`src/core/graze.ts`) with an explicit tunables record, consumed by the
   shared combat core, so the game and every gym resolve identical values; the
   scene only renders and plays cues.

## Why this improves player enjoyment

- It rewards the exact behaviour the game is about, so the inner loop gains a
  second, skill-shaped objective beside survival.
- Close flying becomes a **choice** ("hold the line for a higher tier") rather
  than an accident.
- It gives the leaderboard a skill gap that grinding cannot close, and it is the
  natural scoring substrate for any future run-grade feature.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A pure `src/core/graze.ts` resolves band detection, once-per-object credit,
   hysteresis, tier growth, decay and the score multiplier from an explicit
   tunables record; no scene-local copy exists, and the duplicate-body guard in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` covers the new seam.
2. A live enemy bullet or enemy body entering the band outside the hit radius
   records exactly one graze for that object; leaving and re-entering by less
   than `GRAZE_HYSTERESIS` records none.
3. Kill score is multiplied by the current tier (rounded half up) and the run's
   final score reflects it; grazes award no score beyond tier progress.
4. The multiplier falls one tier per `GRAZE_DECAY_SECONDS` without a graze and
   resets to `×1` on a player hit and at run start.
5. Feedback is present and accessible: tier change reads through shape or pulse
   as well as colour, the HUD shows the tier and its remaining decay, every cue
   respects the shared SFX volume/mute settings and degrades to a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext`.
6. Gym↔game parity: a formation gym exercises detection and tier growth through
   the same shared code path, with a row recorded in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
7. Determinism: the same seed and input trace produce the same graze count and
   score; the rule consumes no RNG of its own.
8. Balance evidence: a same-seed bot batch before/after shows survival,
   `mineralsCollected`, `upgradesSelected` and `avoidableHits` still inside the
   `src/data/experience-targets.json` bands — the expected outcome is **no
   change**, because graze is score-only.
9. Documentation: the normative GDD §4.5 scoring table is amended **when this
   item lands** (the proposal itself is already recorded in GDD §8.3), and
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` gains the new surface.
10. The full project test suite passes (run through the test skill, never an
    ad-hoc invocation).

## Impact

A player who threads a bullet pattern now watches a DANGER multiplier climb and
banks real score for it, so flying dangerously becomes the point rather than a
risk taken only to survive.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **Score-only.** Graze never affects damage, movement, lives or drops, so ring
  timing, the power-up economy and every balance baseline stay put.
- **No new persistent state.** Graze is run-scoped: nothing is written to
  `ai_hell_settings`, the checkpoint or the hangar-war payload.
- **One tunables record** so the feel is retuned without code changes; the
  values are designer-owned, not scene-owned.
- **No new input.** The mechanic reads collisions only, so no key binding,
  control-scheme or Settings change is required.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/core/graze.ts` (new) and `src/core/graze.test.ts` — the pure rule.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — one graze pass in the collision pipeline
  and the multiplier at the shared kill/score seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts`, `src/vfx/` — the spark and tier cue.
- `src/ui/` HUD — the `DANGER ×N` tacho.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — the shared formation-gym base
  (extends `CombatScene`, so the graze pass is inherited by every formation
  gym); `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` is the concrete gym to audit.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.3 (already records the proposal).

## Related work

- GDD §4.5 scoring (the table this multiplies) and §2.3 (hit model).
- Shared collision pipeline and the gym↔game parity rule
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — a graze-heavy session is a good capture
  fixture; `docs/TELEMETRY.md` for the score trace the tests read.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MW3KP1R90030QY9** – Re-measure the mobile tier on hardware WebGL and close parent AC5 (4x CPU throttle, quiet host) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR** – Data-driven enemy health config (completed)
- **AH-0MUDY2GH3003NYY3** – Player-death juice parameter model and constants (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, absent, acceptance, accident, alone (+368 more)
- `README.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, alone, already, amount (+325 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, absent, acceptance, alone, already (+289 more)

## Plan (plan_complete — single vertical slice, no child items)

Effort/risk pre-check returned `skip` (Small / Low, ≈13.5 h expected), so this
is planned as one end-to-end increment rather than a decomposition. Ordering is
**test-first**; each step lands code + tests + docs together.

1. **Pure rule (tests first).** `src/core/graze.ts` + `src/core/graze.test.ts`:
   band resolution (`grazeRadius = playerHitRadius + GRAZE_BAND`), once-per-object
   credit keyed by a stable id with `GRAZE_HYSTERESIS` re-entry, tier growth
   `×1 → ×1.5 → ×2 → ×3 → ×5`, `GRAZE_DECAY_SECONDS` decay, reset on player hit
   and at run start, and the rounded-half-up score multiplier — all from one
   explicit tunables record. No RNG. Covers AC1–AC4 and AC7.
2. **Shared seam wiring.** One graze pass in the shared
   `CombatScene._handleCollisions` pipeline and the multiplier applied at the
   existing `gameState.addScore` kill seam (asteroids/boss phases included) so
   game, gyms and the sim all read the same code. Completes AC1, AC3.
3. **Legibility.** Spark arc at the nearest band point, per-tier pitch cue
   through the shared SFX settings (no-op without an `AudioContext`), HUD
   `DANGER ×N` tacho draining with the decay timer, and a shape/pulse change on
   each tier loss — never colour alone. Covers AC5.
4. **Parity + documentation.** Gym evidence through the same path
   (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` extends `CombatScene`, so
   `GymFodderEnemies` inherits the pass), a `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` row, and the
   normative GDD §4.5 scoring table amendment. Covers AC6 and AC9.
5. **Evidence.** Same-seed bot batch before/after (expectation: no change, since
   graze is score-only) plus a determinism check of graze count and final score
   from a fixed seed and input trace. Covers AC7 and AC8; AC10 is the full suite
   through the test skill.

Vertical-slice decision: a single slice is correct here — the mechanic has no
user-visible value until the rule, the score seam and the HUD cue all exist, so
splitting would ship horizontal layers with nothing playable between them.
Between-step guidance: after step 2, re-read step 3–5 details against the landed
seam (the nearest-band-point API is what the spark arc consumes).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17 — plan skill review pass (auto-plan, Small/Low): verified ACs
  1–10 against the description and the current tree; corrected the predicted
  gym key-file path from the non-existent `src/scenes/gym/GymFormationScene.ts`
  to `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`; confirmed no child items are
  needed; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the item reached `intake_complete` with
  a complete problem statement, ten measurable ACs, explicit constraints
  (score-only, no new persistent state, one tunables record, no new input) and
  key files, and the effort/risk pre-check placed it below the planning
  threshold.
- OPEN QUESTION (none) — no requirement was ambiguous enough to need producer
  input; the single change made (the gym path correction) is a factual
  correction against the current tree, not a requirement change.

# Weapon evolutions: fuse two active weapon kinds into an evolved weapon

Discovered from the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 8 of 10;
direction: create, **Medium** priority).

## Problem statement

The sixteen catalogue weapons are independent: nothing in
`src/utils/weapons.ts`, the shared fire path or the catalogue data reads a
*combination* of two active kinds. A run takes about **two** upgrades (GDD §2.7
target `upgradesSelected 2.00 ± 0.50`), each timed weapon lasts 10 s
(`WEAPON_EFFECT_DURATION`), and the hold-full choice offers level-ups of a
single kind — so a run's build rarely reads as more than "Cannon plus Spread",
and mixing two weapons pays no premium over stacking one.

## Users

A player building a loadout during a run, and — secondarily — the designer
authoring pairings and the gym that must demonstrate them.

- As a player mid-run, I want the second weapon I collect to sometimes **fuse**
  with my first into a visibly different weapon, so my pickups add up to an
  identity I chose rather than a longer list of guns.
- As a player, I want to learn the recipes from play, so I can plan ("I need one
  more `arc` for Chain Ricochet") instead of reading a wiki.
- As a designer, I want pairings to be declarative data with a validating test,
  so a new pairing is a content unit and a typo fails loudly.
- As a gym user, I want a gym row that fires every shipped pairing through the
  same code the game runs, so parity is demonstrable and not asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **One pure resolver.** A pure pairing resolver (new module beside
   `src/utils/weapons.ts`) answers, for the active/owned weapon set, which
   evolved weapon (if any) is live and why (field overlap vs owned pair). No
   scene, gym or bot-decision module derives its own answer.
2. **Pairings are catalogue data with a validating test.** An unknown weapon id
   in a pairing fails loudly at load/validation time; a catalogue without
   pairing data reproduces today's behaviour byte-for-byte (no pairing ⇒ no
   evolved weapon, identical firing trace).
3. **Field tier (timed overlap).** While both kinds of a pairing are active
   simultaneously the evolved pattern fires; when either half expires the
   evolved weapon stops on the next bar downbeat and each half reverts to its
   own pattern.
4. **Owned tier (permanent).** Once both kinds are permanently owned at level
   ≥ 2 — through the shipped hold-full grants, the hangar buy-to-upgrade levels
   (`MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 5`, base 1), or both — the evolved weapon persists for
   the rest of the run and survives the expiry of a timed overlap; `reset`/
   run restart clears it exactly as it clears other owned weapons.
5. **Damage parity.** An automated comparison shows an evolved weapon produces
   no more damage instances per cadence tick than the two halves it replaces,
   and the boss still requires 200 hits at every weapon level.
6. **Grid conformance.** Every evolved cadence resolves to whole 16th-note
   onsets at `beatBpm` on the shared lattice, and pattern morphs occur only on
   bar downbeats.
7. **Legibility.** Fusion and expiry each read through a distinct cue, a HUD
   badge naming the evolved weapon plus its icon, with a shape/text difference
   that does not rely on colour alone; cues respect the shared SFX settings.
8. **Gym ↔ game parity.** `GymWeapons` (or a dedicated row) fires every shipped
   pairing through the shared code path, with a row in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
9. **Determinism.** Same seed and input trace produce the same firing trace.
10. **Balance evidence.** A same-seed bot batch shows `survivalSeconds`,
    `levelReached` and `avoidableHits` inside the experience-target bands, and
    the ring-timing harness is re-measured (a fusion that shortens ring 1 below
    its window is a tuning input, not a blocker). The level-0 output budget
    (non-cannon weapons ≤ 60 % of pre-change level-0 output, GDD §4.4.2) still
    holds.
11. **Hex matchup classification.** An evolved weapon resolves to its **base**
    weapon id(s) for hex matchup purposes, so a fusion can never bypass a hex's
    authored `strengths` / `weaknesses` (cross-item requirement from
    AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ); the resolver publishes both ids and a test pins the
    classification.
12. **Documentation.** GDD §4.4 gains the pairing table (and §8.3's "proposed,
    not shipped" entry is updated to shipped), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` gains the gym
    row, and a `src/weaponBalanceDocs.test.ts`-style docs test covers the
    pairing table so the document and the data cannot drift. Code comments are
    updated to reflect the changes, including README and any relevant wiki or
    docs-site entries.
13. **Test gate.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
    (run through the test skill).

## Impact

A player who collects a second weapon that pairs with their first now sees the
two fuse into a named, visibly different weapon, so a run's pickups add up to a
build the player chose rather than a longer list of guns.

## Proposed mechanic (retained from the seed item)

1. **Pairings are catalogue data.** A declarative entry names, for a **pair** of
   weapon ids, the evolved weapon id. Pilot table (three authored pairings):
   - `ricochet` + `arc` → **Chain Ricochet** — bolts bank off walls *and* hop to
     a second nearby target on each bounce.
   - `cluster` + `mortar` → **Cluster Barrage** — MIRV warheads leave short
     lingering blasts at their burst points.
   - `spread` + `options` → **Fan Escort** — the orbiting pods fire along the
     ship's heading instead of radially, forming a wide fan.
2. **Two tiers, both earned in play (no new economy).** Field evolution fires
   for the overlap window of two active halves; permanent evolution persists
   once both halves are owned at level ≥ 2.
3. **Pattern, coverage and behaviour only** — never damage instances per shot.
4. **Cadence stays on the shared lattice** as its own `(k, n, rotation)` ladder,
   so an evolved weapon morphs only on a bar downbeat and stays phase-locked.
5. **Legibility**: a distinct fusion cue, a HUD badge with the evolved name and
   icon, and a matching downbeat cue on expiry.
6. **One pure module** consumed by the shared fire path, so the game and every
   weapon gym run identical code.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **No new economy and no new slot.** Evolutions consume the existing six
  shared slots and the existing hold-full / hangar level paths; nothing is
  purchasable.
- **Pattern, not power.** An evolution must not raise damage per tick or the
  number of damage instances; the balance risk is coverage, and AC5 pins it.
- **Authored, not combinatorial.** Three pairings ship; the mechanism supports
  more, but each pairing is a balance-tested content unit.
- **One resolver.** Pairing logic never appears in a scene, a gym or a
  bot-decision module — bot decisions read the resolved active set.
- **Permanent levels are one snapshot.** Both ownership sources (run hold-full
  grants, hangar buy-to-upgrade) already converge on `Player.getWeaponLevels()`;
  the owned tier reads that snapshot rather than adding persisted state.
- **No dependency on AH-0MWKT12BT001106T** (hangar power-up ownership) — that
  sibling gap is about power-ups' first permanent row, not weapons.
- **Assumption:** the evolved ids are resolved *output*, not new catalogue rows,
  so `src/data/weapons.csv` and `weaponCatalogueParity.test.ts` stay untouched
  (see Risks for the fallback if this proves wrong).

## Existing state (verified in the repo, 2026-11-17)

- **Catalogue ids**: the 16 ids are declared in `src/utils/weapons.ts:100`
  (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova,
  mortar, arc, rear_guard, broadside, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug`).
  `WeaponDefinition` is at `src/utils/weapons.ts:810`; subdivision-based
  fire-rate constants (`WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE`) derive cadence from the beat
  lattice, so an evolved weapon slots into the same shape.
- **`resolveWeaponDefinition`** is the one level-resolving catalogue read,
  consumed by `src/entities/Player.ts:1226`, `src/ai/eval/arena.ts:983` (bot
  arena) and `src/utils/weaponStrength.ts`. Any second resolution path would be
  a duplicate.
- **Catalogue data is CSV-authored**: `src/data/weapons.csv` (one row per
  weapon, header documents `id, name, description, subdivisions, bulletColor,
  bulletShape, bulletSize, …`), patterns in `src/data/weapon-patterns.csv`,
  ladder rungs in `src/data/weapon-levels.json` (`{k, n, rotation}` per level
  per weapon). Parsed by `parseWeaponCatalogue` (`src/core/csv.ts`), guarded at
  runtime by `src/utils/weaponCatalogue.ts`, written by
  `src/core/weaponCatalogueStore.ts`, and pinned by
  `src/data/weaponCatalogueParity.test.ts`.
- **The pairing relation is cross-row**, so it cannot live as a column in
  `weapons.csv` — it needs its own table wherever it is authored.
- **Shared fire path and active set**: `src/entities/Player.ts`
  (`getActiveWeapons()` `:896`, `_permanentWeapons` `:315`,
  `_permanentWeaponGrants` `:324`, `getWeaponLevels()` permanent-level
  snapshot), plus the region registry in `src/powerups/effects.ts`
  (`EffectsRegistry` `:361`, `WEAPON_EFFECT_DURATION = 10`,
  `src/powerups/effects.ts:159`).
- **Permanent level ladder already exists**: `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 5` with
  `BASE_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 1` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:583`), so
  "owned at level ≥ 2" is reachable both in-run (two hold-full grants) and from
  the hangar (buy-to-upgrade, AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU, completed).
- **Ownership display** already reads the permanent-only snapshot:
  `buildOwnedLoadout` (`src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts:97`) — the same snapshot the
  owned tier should read, so no new persistence is needed.
- **Drop feedback surfaces**: `src/powerups/icons.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`
  and `src/ui/HUD.ts`.
- **Gyms**: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `GymWeaponLeveling`,
  `GymWeaponTuning`; the parity ledger `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` already documents
  the weapon rows (`:115`, `:116`).
- **Docs**: GDD §4.4 carries a "proposed, not shipped (backlog §8.3)" pointer to
  weapon evolutions (`docs/Game Design Document.md:1203`); §8.3 holds the
  backlog entry. The `*Docs.test.ts` convention (e.g.
  `src/weaponBalanceDocs.test.ts`) is how a document is pinned to its data.
- **Hex matchup does not exist yet**: no `resolveHexMatchup` symbol exists in
  `src/`; hex `strengths`/`weaknesses` live in
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` / `hexRing.ts` and the matchup resolver is
  still open work (AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ, `open`/`plan_complete`) — see Q3.

## Desired change

1. New pure module `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts` holding the authored pairing
   table and the resolver: input = active ids + permanent levels, output = the
   live evolved id (or none), its base ids, and the reason
   (`field` | `owned` | none).
2. Evolved definitions added beside the catalogue (id, name, icon, colour,
   pattern/ladder, cadence subdivision) resolving through the existing
   `Subdivisions`/`WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` shape so cadence stays on the lattice.
3. Exactly one call site in the shared fire path (`Player`/`CombatCoreScene`)
   reads the resolved set instead of enumerating weapons itself; the bot arena
   reads the same resolution.
4. Fusion/expiry feedback: cue + HUD badge (name, icon, shape/text, not
   colour-only) through the shared SFX settings.
5. Gym demonstration of every shipped pairing through the shared path, plus the
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` row.
6. Docs: pairing table in GDD §4.4, §8.3 entry promoted, docs test pinning the
   table, code comments updated.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts` *(new)* — pairing table, evolved definitions,
  the pure resolver, and its unit tests (`weaponEvolutions.test.ts`).
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `WeaponId` union extension for evolved ids (if the
  evolved ids join the union) and the shared `WeaponDefinition` shape.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — the single resolved-active-weapon read
  (`getActiveWeapons`, `_permanentWeaponGrants`, `getWeaponLevels`).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — the shared region/auto-fire path the evolved
  pattern fires through.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts` — evolved icon and fusion badge.
- `src/data/weapon-levels.json` (or a sibling file) — evolved cadence rungs, if
  cadence is authored as data rather than constants.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (+ tests) — the pairing parity row.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4, §8.3),
  `src/weaponBalanceDocs.test.ts`-style docs test.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Power creep through coverage.** Fusions widen coverage even at equal damage
  per tick. Mitigation: AC5's automated damage-instance comparison plus AC10's
  bot-batch bands; evolved cadence is a tuning input, not a free upgrade.
- **A second resolution path.** The obvious failure is a gym or scene deriving
  its own answer. Mitigation: AC1 forbids it and AC8's gym row fires the shared
  path, so a divergence shows up as a gym failure.
- **Phase drift on the lattice.** A bespoke timer would break the shared beat
  lattice. Mitigation: AC6 resolves evolved cadence to whole 16th-note onsets
  and morphs only on bar downbeats.
- **Owned-tier confusion.** Two ownership sources (run hold-full grants vs
  hangar permanent levels) could disagree. Mitigation: both are already one
  permanent snapshot (`Player.getWeaponLevels()`), which is what
  `buildOwnedLoadout` reads — reuse it rather than adding state.
- **Scope creep.** The mechanism invites more than three pairings, a fusion
  economy, or researched-weapon pairings from
  `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`. Those are follow-up work items, not
  scope here.
- **Assumption (verify at implementation).** Evolved ids can stay outside the
  `WeaponId` union (resolved output only) — this avoids touching the CSV parity
  test and the bot arena's `WeaponId` handling. If they must join the union, the
  CSV and parity tests need rows too.

## Related work

- GDD §2.3 (shared beat lattice), §4.4 (catalogue + level-0 output budget),
  §4.4.2 (weapon strength budget), §4.3 (boss 200-hit pool), §8.3 (backlog
  entry), §2.7 (`upgradesSelected` target).
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** — Make weapons both cumulative and time out
  (completed): the timed-cumulative active set the field tier observes.
- **AH-0MUQOTSFE00462EJ** — Feature: per-weapon level state on Player
  (completed): `getWeaponLevels()` / `_permanentWeaponGrants`.
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** — Feature: permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling
  (completed): the hold-full path that raises the owned tier's level.
- **AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU** — Hangar UI: buy to upgrade owned weapons and power-ups
  (completed): the hangar permanent levels the owned tier reads.
- **AH-0MWKT12BT001106T** — Hangar power-up ownership: no path creates a
  power-up's first permanent level row (`open`): sibling work on the ownership
  model; this item must not depend on it.
- **AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ** — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat
  (`open`/`plan_complete`): source of the AC11 base-id requirement.
- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` — the pairing layer is the natural
  home for future researched weapons.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

Answers pending — the three decisions below materially change scope,
authoring surface and sequencing, so they are recorded as producer questions.
They are **idempotent entries**: on re-run, update in place, never duplicate.

- **Q1 (scope / issue type).** Keep this as one `feature`, or re-type it to an
  `epic` and decompose into children at planning? The thirteen ACs span five
  independently testable subsystems (pairing resolver + data; field tier firing;
  owned tier persistence; fusion feedback/HUD; gym parity + docs + balance
  evidence).
  Options: (a) `epic` + children; (b) stay one `feature`; (c) split into two
  items (resolver + tiers, then feedback/parity/docs).
  **Recommended:** (a) `epic` — each subsystem has its own test gate and a
  single worktree session should not carry all five.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer).

- **Q2 (where pairing data lives).** Author the pairing table in a new
  TypeScript module beside the catalogue (`src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts`), or
  in designer-editable CSV/data (a new `src/data/weapon-pairings.csv` routed
  through `parseWeaponCatalogue`-style parsing, `src/utils/weaponCatalogue.ts`
  runtime guard and `src/core/weaponCatalogueStore.ts`)? AC2 says "catalogue
  data with a validating test" but the existing CSV is one row per weapon, so a
  pairing relation cannot be a column there.
  Options: (a) TS table in `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts`; (b) new CSV +
  parser + runtime guard; (c) TS now, CSV authoring as a follow-up item.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a cross-row relation read by one pure resolver, with
  compile-time id validation and no new CSV/parser/guard surface; designer
  authoring can follow as its own item once the three pairings prove out.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer).

- **Q3 (hex matchup sequencing).** AC11 requires evolved weapons to classify as
  their base ids, but `resolveHexMatchup` does not exist yet (AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ
  is `open`/`plan_complete`). Options: (a) declare this item blocked by
  AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ; (b) publish the base ids from the resolver now and pin the
  classification test when that resolver lands (two-way cross-reference, no
  dependency); (c) implement matchup classification here.
  **Recommended:** (b) — base-id exposure is cheap and costs nothing now;
  blocking the whole evolution feature on a larger open item would stall it,
  while (c) would duplicate that item's work.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer).
