data.description:
Add the frozen transition knobs to `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` and the pure junction arithmetic that every later slice reads: resolved per-junction fades (clamped to a quarter of the shorter neighbour cut), chained `xfade` offsets, and each deliverable's expected duration.

Part of **AH-0MWLYWYGK004JR2A** (capture:promo should cross fade highlights). Producer answers are already recorded: **promo and showreel cross-fade** (Q1 = B), **400 ms video dissolve clamped to ≤ 25 % of the shorter neighbouring cut** (Q2 = B), **audio cross-fades slightly slower at 500 ms** (Q3 = A with 500 ms).

## Scope

- `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` gains a frozen `transitions` block — `{ videoFadeMs: 400, audioFadeMs: 500, maxFadeRatio: 0.25 }` — with a doc comment explaining the clamp and the `videoFadeMs: 0` opt-out to hard cuts.
- Derived exports alongside the existing ones (`DEFAULT_TARGETS`, `PACE_BAND`, `CUT_CADENCE`, …) so tests, the argv builder and the docs read one definition.
- New pure helpers in `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`: a junction planner that takes clamped segments + the transition config and returns, per junction, the resolved video/audio fade (clamped by `maxFadeRatio` against both neighbours) and the cumulative video `xfade` offset, plus `expectedDurationMs = Σ cuts − Σ resolved video fades`.
- Unit tests in `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` (TDD: write them first, then make them green).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EDITORIAL_CONFIG.transitions` is frozen, equals `{ videoFadeMs: 400, audioFadeMs: 500, maxFadeRatio: 0.25 }`, and is read through a derived export asserted against the config by a derivation test in the style of the existing ones.
- The junction planner is pure and returns `n − 1` junction records for `n` cuts, each carrying the resolved `videoFadeMs`/`audioFadeMs` clamped to `maxFadeRatio × min(previous cut, next cut)` and a cumulative `videoOffsetMs` of `Σ cuts so far − Σ video fades so far`.
- Offsets chain correctly for 2, 3 and 40 cuts: each offset is asserted against an independent reference computation in the test and is strictly increasing.
- A 1 s cut adjacent to a 6 s cut resolves a 250 ms video fade (the 25 % clamp) and an audio fade clamped to the same 250 ms; two 6 s cuts resolve the full 400/500 ms.
- `expectedDurationMs` equals `Σ cutMs − Σ resolvedVideoFadeMs` for every fixture.
- With `videoFadeMs: 0` the planner reports zero transitions and `expectedDurationMs === Σ cutMs` (hard-cut arithmetic opt-out).
- No behaviour changes in the argv yet: the existing suite and the C0 goldens stay green.

- **Parent criterion (verbatim):** The transition durations are frozen editorial knobs in `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` — video dissolve **400 ms**, audio cross-fade **500 ms**, both clamped to at most a quarter of the shorter neighbouring cut — read through shared derived exports, and setting the video duration to `0` restores the current hard-cut `concat` graph byte-for-byte so the change is opt-outable. — satisfied by this slice's frozen `transitions` block and derived export; the byte-identical `concat` graph at `videoFadeMs: 0` is proven by the following graph slice against the C0 golden.

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` (~L109), derived exports (~L200), new junction planner near `secondsOf`/`buildDeliverableArgv` (~L1550).
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — config derivation, clamp, offset-chain and expected-duration specs.

**Dependencies:** blocked by the golden-baseline child (its argv must not move).

## Impact

No user-visible change yet: the dissolve timings become one frozen, tested editorial knob (400 ms picture / 500 ms sound, clamped on short cuts) instead of a magic number, so the compiler can prove how long the finished promo will be before it encodes anything.

data.description:
Rewrite the multi-cut junction in `buildDeliverableArgv` from a single `concat` into a chained `xfade` (video) + `acrossfade` (audio) graph, keeping the single-segment path and the zero-duration opt-out byte-identical to today.

Part of **AH-0MWLYWYGK004JR2A** (capture:promo should cross fade highlights). This is the slice a producer sees: the promo and showreel stop hard-cutting and dissolve instead. Everything it needs (knobs, clamp, offsets) comes from the config/arithmetic child.

## Scope

- `buildDeliverableArgv`: for `segments.length > 1` and `resolved videoFadeMs > 0`, fold the normalised `[v0..vn]` through successive `xfade=transition=fade:duration=<s>:offset=<s>` steps and `[a0..an]` through successive `acrossfade=d=<s>` steps, using the chained offsets from the planner. No extra `-filter_complex` pass and no extra encode: the dissolve lives in the existing single pass.
- Per-input normalisation (`trim`/`setpts`/`scale`/`pad`/`fps`/`format=yuv420p`/`setsar` and `atrim`/`asetpts`/`aformat`) stays ahead of the fade chain, because `xfade` requires matching timebase/format/fps.
- Single segment and `videoFadeMs = 0` keep the current code paths verbatim.
- Unit tests in `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A multi-cut promo argv contains exactly `segments.length − 1` `xfade=transition=fade:duration=<seconds>:offset=<seconds>` occurrences and exactly `segments.length − 1` `acrossfade=d=<seconds>` occurrences, with each `offset` equal to the planner's cumulative offset.
- The video chain threads a labelled intermediate per junction (`[v0][v1]xfade…[vx1];[vx1][v2]xfade…`) and the audio chain does the same, ending in `[v]`/`[a]`; no `concat=` filter remains on the multi-cut path when transitions are enabled.
- The showreel takes the same cross-faded path (asserted by building a multi-cut deliverable of both kinds), while a single-cut highlight still maps `[v0]`/`[a0]` directly with no transition filter.
- With `videoFadeMs: 0` the multi-cut graph equals the C0 golden `concat=n=N:v=1:a=1[v][a]` graph byte-for-byte, and the single-segment argv equals its C0 golden byte-for-byte.
- Determinism holds: the same plan + segments produce byte-identical argv across repeated builds, and the existing `ffmpeg driver — deterministic command building` test still passes.
- Normalisation filters still appear before the first `xfade`/`acrossfade` in the graph.

- **Parent criterion (verbatim):** Multi-cut deliverables join their cuts with a **dissolve**, not a hard cut: the `-filter_complex` graph built by `buildDeliverableArgv` uses `xfade` (video) and `acrossfade` (audio) between consecutive streams, with no `concat` filter remaining on the multi-cut path. Promo **and** showreel both cross-fade; single-cut highlights are unchanged. — satisfied here: multi-cut promo and showreel chain `xfade`/`acrossfade` with no `concat`, single-cut highlights unchanged.

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — `buildDeliverableArgv` (~L1579) and its doc comment.
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — graph-shape, opt-out and determinism specs.

**Dependencies:** blocked by the config/arithmetic child.

## Impact

The compiled promo and showreel dissolve from cut to cut instead of hard-cutting, so the published footage reads as an edited trailer rather than a splice of separate recordings.

data.description:
Keep the audio timeline aligned with the picture now that audio overlaps 100 ms more per junction than video: extend each outgoing cut's audio tail from its probed source headroom, and clamp that junction's audio fade back to the video duration when the headroom is not there.

Part of **AH-0MWLYWYGK004JR2A** (capture:promo should cross fade highlights). This is the item's main technical risk: an uncompensated 500 ms audio cross-fade against a 400 ms video dissolve removes 100 ms more audio per junction — roughly 3.9 s short of the picture across a ~40-cut promo, which is unusable.

## Scope

- `buildDeliverableCommands` already probes each source and clamps segments to it; pass the per-segment headroom (`min(probed source duration − videoOutMs, …)`) into the graph builder.
- Per junction: extend the outgoing cut's `atrim` end by `audioFadeMs − videoFadeMs` when the source has that much tail, so the audio chain loses only the video fade; otherwise clamp that junction's `acrossfade d` to `videoFadeMs + availableHeadroom` and emit no extension.
- Deterministic only: inputs are `videoInMs`/`videoOutMs` and the probed source duration — never wall-clock or encoder state.
- Unit tests in `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With ≥ 300 ms headroom at every junction, the outgoing cut's `atrim` end equals `videoOutMs + (audioFadeMs − videoFadeMs)` in seconds and each junction's `acrossfade d` stays at the full audio fade; the accumulated audio timeline equals the video timeline (`Σ cuts − Σ resolved video fades`) for 2, 5 and 40 cuts.
- With zero headroom at a junction, no `atrim` extension is emitted there, that junction's `acrossfade d` equals `videoFadeMs`, and every other junction keeps its full compensation — the same fixture still yields audio and video totals within one frame of each other.
- A mixed fixture (some junctions with ample headroom, some short) accumulates **no** drift: the difference between the accumulated audio and video durations is 0 or at most one frame at 60 fps, and it does not grow with cut count.
- Repeated builds of the same plan produce identical `atrim`/`acrossfade` values (no clock, no encoder state); the determinism test still passes.
- The clamp rule and its one documented fallback are stated in code comments, not inferred from behaviour.

- **Parent criterion (verbatim):** **Audio and video stay aligned across the whole deliverable** with no cumulative drift: because the audio cross-fade overlaps 100 ms more than the picture at every junction, the audio chain is compensated per junction (the outgoing cut's audio is extended by the extra overlap from its source headroom, or the junction's audio fade is deterministically clamped back to the video duration when that headroom does not exist), so the delivered audio and video streams end within one frame of each other rather than the audio running short by `100 ms × (junctions − 1)`. — satisfied here: the per-junction extension/clamp rule and the no-drift specs.

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — `buildDeliverableCommands` (headroom from the existing probe, ~L1641), `buildDeliverableArgv` audio chain (~L1579), planner audio fields.
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — no-drift, mixed-headroom and no-headroom-fallback specs.

**Dependencies:** blocked by the cross-faded graph child.

## Impact

The promo sounds in sync with the picture at every cut: the audio blend at each dissolve no longer shortens the track, so a long promo cannot drift progressively out of sync.

data.description:
Account for the screen time a dissolve removes: size the promo against `Σ cuts − Σ fades` before filling, and record each deliverable's expected duration and the configured transition settings next to the measured ones in the report, summary and `--help`.

Part of **AH-0MWLYWYGK004JR2A** (capture:promo should cross fade highlights). Every junction removes 400 ms from the delivered length, so a heavily cut promo loses 10–20 s; without fixing the fill budget it drops under the 45 s floor and `assessTargets` legitimately fails.

## Scope

- `buildEditPlan`: the promo fill budget becomes "expected duration net of the fades implied by the cuts selected so far", still `targets.promo.maxMs − targets.promo.safetyMs`, so the delivered promo lands inside the 45–60 s band (§7.6).
- `DeliverableCommand` gains `expectedDurationMs` and the resolved `transitions` it was built with; `buildDeliverableCommands` fills them from the same arithmetic.
- `compileDeliverables` adds a per-deliverable `expectedDurationMs` next to the measured `durationSec`, plus a top-level `transitions` settings block in `compile-promo-report.json` (expected-vs-measured stays auditable).
- `formatCompileSummary` prints expected vs measured duration and states the transition settings once; `USAGE_TEXT` documents the dissolve, the timings, the clamp, the A/V compensation and the hard-cut opt-out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The promo fill budget reserves the fades implied by the chosen cuts: for a representative fixture the sum of nominal cut lengths may exceed `maxMs − safetyMs` by the fade total, but `Σ cuts − Σ fades` stays within `[promo.minMs, promo.maxMs − safetyMs]` — and a test fails if the budget is computed from raw cut lengths again.
- Each `DeliverableCommand` exposes `expectedDurationMs` equal to `Σ cuts − Σ resolved video fades` and the `transitions` block it used; the promo, showreel and every highlight command carry them.
- `compile-promo-report.json` records the per-deliverable expected duration alongside the measured probe duration and a top-level `transitions` block; a unit test asserts both are present and consistent with the plan.
- `formatCompileSummary` states the transition settings once and prints expected vs measured duration per deliverable.
- `--help` (`USAGE_TEXT`) documents the 400 ms dissolve / 500 ms audio blend, the 25 % clamp, `videoFadeMs: 0` restoring hard cuts, and that the audio timeline is compensated per junction.
- The existing determinism, `assessTargets` and pace-band tests still pass unchanged.

- **Parent criterion (verbatim):** Each deliverable's expected duration — `Σ cut durations − Σ video transitions` — is computed in the plan/command layer, uses the same arithmetic to size the promo fill budget so a delivered promo still measures inside the 45–60 s band (§7.6), and is recorded in the compile report alongside the configured transition settings (so expected-vs-measured is auditable). — satisfied here: net-of-fade fill budget, `expectedDurationMs` and the report's transition block.
- **Parent criterion (verbatim):** Unit tests cover: cross-faded graph shape for a multi-cut deliverable, chained offset arithmetic, per-junction clamping on short cuts, the 500/400 ms audio-video alignment compensation (including the no-headroom fallback) with no accumulating drift, the `0`-duration hard-cut regression, single-segment output unchanged, and byte-identical argv for an identical plan (the existing determinism test must keep passing). — satisfied across the cross-fade slices; this slice asserts the full matrix exists and passes before it completes.
- **Parent criterion (verbatim):** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. — satisfied here (this is the last production-code slice).

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — `buildEditPlan` (~L673, budget at ~L757), `buildDeliverableCommands` (~L1641), `compileDeliverables` (~L1883), `formatCompileSummary` (~L2054), `USAGE_TEXT` (~L782).
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — budget arithmetic, report fields, summary and help-text specs.

**Dependencies:** blocked by the audio-alignment child.

## Impact

A recompiled promo still measures inside the 45–60 s band despite the time the dissolves remove, and the compile report states the expected and measured length plus the transition settings, so a reviewer can see the package was sized deliberately.

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts` — per-deliverable assertions (~L167), promo probe block (~L288).

data.description:
# Intake brief — Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results

## Problem statement

Returning to the hex map after a hex deployment currently reduces the whole
sortie to a single thin line (`RUN: VICTORY · score 1200`) plus a banked
win-bonus line, and on defeat it shows only `RUN: DEFEAT` with no explanation of
why the hex was not taken. The player cannot see, in one place, what the battle
outcome was, which rewards (salvage, granted weapon/upgrade, special reward,
contract/cache bonus) were actually paid, or — on a loss — what the defending
boss was strong and weak against. This brief adds a **post-battle results
dialog** on the hex map that presents that detail.

## Users

The **player** finishing a hex deployment in the Hangar War outer loop, and the
**attract/demo traversal** that must not stall on the new surface.

- As a player who won a hex, I want a dialog that tells me the outcome, my
  score and every reward I received, so I know exactly what the sortie earned me.
- As a player who lost a hex, I want a dialog that summarises the enemy boss's
  strengths and weaknesses (and the reward I missed), so I can plan the retake.
- As a player or watcher, I want to dismiss the dialog with one input (and have
  the attract demo auto-dismiss it) so the map stays playable and never stalls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a hex deployment ends, landing on `HexMapScene` presents a modal dialog over the paused map stating the battle outcome (`VICTORY`/`DEFEAT`) and the run's final score.
- On victory the dialog itemises every reward that was actually paid — salvage banked (minerals/cores), any granted weapon/upgrade, any special-mission reward, any contract and/or cache bonus, and the banked win bonus — and shows no line for a reward that was not paid.
- On defeat the dialog summarises the target hex boss's authored strengths and weaknesses (from `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`) and states the grant the player did not claim; it also states the unbanked salvage that was forfeited.
- The dialog is dismissible by a single confirm input (keyboard or pointer); dismissal resumes the map, and in demo/attract mode the dialog auto-dismisses after the shared dwell so the traversal cannot stall on it.
- The dialog's contents are produced by a shared, pure "result for view" builder over the game's own capture/defeat record and the authored hex definition (the dialog derives no reward or weakness itself), covered by unit tests plus a landing integration test that boots `HexMapScene` with a sortie result and asserts the dialog text and dismissal.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

After every hex battle the player gets one clear results dialog that names the
outcome, the rewards actually earned and, on a loss, the enemy's strengths and
weaknesses — so no sortie ends on a bare `RUN: DEFEAT` line with no explanation.

## Constraints

- **Reuse the shipped overlay pattern.** The map already pauses itself at the
  `SceneManager` level and launches `MiniBossWheelScene` / `MineralChoiceScene`
  over the paused map. The results dialog follows the same single-overlay
  contract (launch → pause → optional `onResult` callback → resume), including
  the demo auto-resolve rule (`HexMapScene.presentReward`).
- **One rule, no re-derivation.** Reward figures come from the capture cycle's
  own `HexCaptureResult` (`resolveHexCapture`) and the defeat path's
  `resolveDeploymentDefeat`; the boss strengths/weaknesses come from the authored
  hex definition. The dialog/view model must never re-derive a number.
- **Transient launch data only.** Like the existing run line, win bonus and
  assault banner, the sortie result is never persisted; a later menu/hangar
  re-entry shows no dialog.
- **Gym parity note.** `GymHexWar` is a read-only ring harness that runs no
  deployment and no combat, so it cannot show a post-battle dialog; this is a
  landing-surface presentation of the game's finished deployment, not a gameplay
  object, and needs no divergent gym copy.

## Risks

- **Handoff drift.** The reward detail lives in `HexCaptureResult`, not in the
  map today; if the handoff copies fields by hand, a new reward kind could be
  silently dropped from the dialog. Mitigation: pass the shipped record and let
  the pure builder read it, so a new reward field surfaces without a second edit.
- **Duplicated presentation.** If the dialog is added but the thin run line and
  win-bonus line are left in place, the landing shows the same facts twice.
  Mitigation: assumption A1 folds them in; a test asserts the dialog carries the
  outcome/score/win bonus.
- **Demo stall.** A modal that waits for input would freeze the attract
  traversal. Mitigation: reuse the existing demo auto-resolve rule so the dialog
  auto-dismisses after the shared dwell (asserted in a test).
- **Scope creep.** Related opportunities (e.g. surfacing the defeating bot's
  skills, or a full sortie history) are recorded as separate linked items rather
  than folded into this brief.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene` ends a hex deployment by starting `HexMapScene` with
  `{ payload, record, won, score, reward, assault, winBonusMinerals, demo,
  demoDwellMs }` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, the `_endRun` hangar-war branch).
- `HexMapScene` renders the map and a thin `runLine()`
  (`RUN: VICTORY|DEFEAT · score N`) plus the model's `winBonusLine` and, when a
  ring-end assault fired, the `RING WON` / `HANGAR FALLS` banner. It presents the
  mini-boss reward over the paused map via `presentReward()`.
- `HexCaptureResult` (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`) already carries every
  reward number a victory paid: `bankedDelta`, `grant`, `specialReward`,
  `contractBonus`, `cachePayout`, `defender`, `ringSecured`, `ringAdvanced`,
  `assault`. The defeat path `resolveDeploymentDefeat` yields the `forfeited`
  salvage. **None of this is currently handed to the map** — only `assault`,
  `won`, `score` and `winBonusMinerals` are.
- Boss intel is authored per hex in `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`
  (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`): `boss`, `strengths`, `weaknesses`,
  `grants`, and is already surfaced in the map's detail panel.

## Desired change

1. Extend the deployment→map handoff so `HexMapScene` receives a compact
   **sortie result** for the finished deployment: the target hex id, the
   capture result's reward fields (`bankedDelta`, `grant`, `specialReward`,
   `contractBonus`, `cachePayout`, `ringSecured`, `ringAdvanced`) on a win, and
   `forfeited` on a loss (plus `won`/`score`/`winBonusMinerals`, already there).
2. Add a pure **results-for-view builder** (e.g.
   `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts`) that turns that record plus the authored
   hex definition into ordered dialog rows: outcome + score, every paid reward,
   and — only on defeat — the boss's strengths/weaknesses and the unclaimed
   grant. No rule lives in the scene.
3. Add the **results dialog overlay** (a new scene mirroring
   `MineralChoiceScene`'s pause/launch contract, or a modal section of the
   shared `hexMap` renderer) and present it on `HexMapScene.create()` when a
   sortie result is carried, before the demo dwell starts. A single confirm
   input dismisses it; demo auto-dismisses after the shared dwell.
4. Fold the now-redundant thin `runLine()` / win-bonus announcement into the
   dialog on a deployment landing (assumption A1), leaving the distinct
   hangar-assault banner in place.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — add the sortie result (capture/defeat record + target hex id) to the `scene.start(HEX_MAP_SCENE_KEY, …)` handoff at run end.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — accept, hold and present the sortie result; fold the thin run line into the dialog; resume the map on dismissal (and demo dwell).
- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts` (new, or extend `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) — pure results-for-view builder consuming the record + `HexRingDefinition`; the single source of dialog text.
- `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.ts` (new, or a modal section in `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`) — the pause/launch overlay with a single confirm dismissal, mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` / `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — types already carried (`HexCaptureResult`, `DeploymentDefeatResult`, `SalvageAmounts`); no rule change expected.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — authored `strengths`/`weaknesses`/`grants` read by the builder (no change expected).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.test.ts` (new) — coverage for the builder and the landing dialog.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D § UI / scene surface) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — record the new landing surface and the gym-parity note.

## Related work

- `AH-0MWEXIOZZ009UX14` — Scene: `HexMapScene` accepts record/run-line/reward and presents the reward over the paused map.
- `AH-0MWEZZA4E0081NJ5` — Assault defence report and reset announcement.
- `AH-0MWF2Q2JC008MAJE` — DefenceReportScene: announce the banked win bonus before the map.
- `AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP` — Between-sortie frontier tick and the deployment→map landing handoff.

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, § *UI / scene surface* and § *Known-ahead intel and anti-checklist mitigations*.

## Appendix: Assumptions and questions for producer confirmation

These are repo-grounded assumptions made to keep intake moving; the producer
may override any of them at review. No question was answered interactively
during this intake pass.

- **A1 — Dialog replaces the thin map lines.** The results dialog carries the
  outcome, score and win bonus that the current `runLine()` and `winBonusLine`
  show, so those two are folded into the dialog on a deployment landing to
  avoid duplication. The `RING WON` / `HANGAR FALLS` hangar-assault banner stays
  as a separate, distinct announcement. *If the producer prefers the dialog to
  appear alongside the existing lines, this is a presentation-only change and
  does not affect the ACs.*
- **A2 — "Enemy strengths and weaknesses" means the target hex boss.** The
  summary uses the target hex's authored `strengths` / `weaknesses` in
  `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`, plus the `grant` the player did not claim. The
  defending-bot `skills` are not summarised unless the producer asks.
- **A3 — Blocking modal, one confirm to dismiss, demo auto-dismiss.** The
  dialog pauses the map (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`) and is dismissed by a
  single keyboard/pointer confirm; in demo/attract mode it auto-dismisses after
  the shared dwell so the traversal cannot stall.
- **A4 — Both outcomes show the dialog.** A victory shows outcome + rewards; a
  defeat shows outcome + the boss strengths/weaknesses + the unclaimed grant and
  the forfeited unbanked salvage.
- **A5 — Data must be extended, not re-derived.** The map currently receives no

  cycle's own record rather than the map recomputing rewards.

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan skill, 2026-11-18)

Decomposed into **7 children** in test-first dependency order. Each child is a
minimal end-to-end slice (code + tests + the docs/observability its layer owns);
the contract is pinned by tests before the implementation items land, in the
repo's red-before/green-after convention.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|------------|
| 1 | TEST-FIRST: pin the sortie results dialog contract (`AH-0MWMGPPIR009DOKR`) | task | — |
| 2 | Pure sortie result view builder (`AH-0MWMGPQUE0064AFH`) | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Deployment handoff carries the sortie result (`AH-0MWMGPS9R008SMEG`) | feature | 2 |
| 4 | Hex combat result dialog overlay scene (`AH-0MWMGPTNF004EX3T`) | feature | 2 |

| 7 | Sortie results dialog end-to-end verification (`AH-0MWMGPY2U009XMBD`) | task | 5, 6 |

### Vertical-slice phasing

This is one landing-surface slice, not a multi-phase epic, so there are no
phase gates. Where the plan does split work it splits on **module boundaries**
that are independently shippable — the pure builder (2) and the overlay scene
(4) both run in isolation, and 3 and 4 can land in either order before the map
wiring (5) joins them. Every child still cuts through its own layers: a pure
model plus unit tests (2), a scene plus its registry and capture entries (4), a
handoff plus its launch-data test (3), a landing plus its stepped-frame
integration test (5), and the documentation of record (6).

**Between children:** re-read the next child's description before starting it
and update it if the shipped shape has moved (for example the exact
`SortieResultRecord` field names fixed by child 2, which children 3–5 quote from
the intake rather than from code).

  and the read-only `GymHexWar`. A blocking modal inside the shared renderer
  would force every gym render to make a modal/parity decision, while the
  intake records that `GymHexWar` runs no deployment and can never land. A
  separate `HexCombatResultScene` (child 4) mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s
  launch/pause/callback contract keeps the shared renderer untouched and the
  gym divergence-free, and matches the shipped overlay pattern the constraint
  section names.
- **Carry the shipped records, not a copied subset.** Child 3 hands the map the
  capture cycle's own `HexCaptureResult` and the defeat path's `forfeited`
  salvage, so the parent's "handoff drift" risk is closed by design: a reward

  copy edit.

# Pure sortie result view builder

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

The results dialog must present the sortie's outcome, its paid rewards and — on
a defeat — the target boss's strengths/weaknesses, without the scene deriving
any of it. Today the reward detail lives only in `HexCaptureResult`
(`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`) and the defeat detail in
`DeploymentDefeatResult`; the boss intel is authored per hex in
`HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`. This item adds the single pure module that turns those
records into ordered dialog rows, so the scene renders text it was handed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The dialog's contents are produced by a shared, pure "result for view" builder over the game's own capture/defeat record and the authored hex definition (the dialog derives no reward or weakness itself), covered by unit tests in this item plus the landing integration test in the `HexMapScene` child that boots `HexMapScene` with a sortie result and asserts the dialog text and dismissal.
- A new pure module `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts` defines the compact `SortieResultRecord` the map receives (won, score, target hex id, banked win bonus, the carried `HexCaptureResult` on a victory, the forfeited `SalvageAmounts` on a defeat) and `buildSortieResultView(record, definition)` returning ordered rows for the dialog.
- On a victory the rows are: outcome + score first, then salvage banked (minerals/cores), any granted weapon/upgrade, any special-mission reward, any contract bonus, any cache payout and the banked win bonus — each only when it was actually paid, never a zero line.
- On a defeat the rows are: outcome + score, the target hex's authored `strengths` and `weaknesses`, the grant the player did not claim, and the forfeited unbanked salvage.
- The builder **re-derives nothing**: every reward figure and every strength/weakness string is copied from the carried record or the authored `HexRingDefinition`; the module imports no Phaser, reads no store and mutates no input (a frozen input is not thrown on).
- A sortie result whose target hex is absent from the supplied definitions degrades to the outcome + score rows (and, on a victory, the carried reward rows) instead of throwing or inventing boss intel.
- Unit tests cover every reward kind present and absent for both outcomes, the forfeited-salvage line, the unknown-hex fallback and input immutability.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts` (new)
- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (types read only — `HexCaptureResult`, `DeploymentDefeatResult`; no rule change)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` (the `HexRingDefinition` shape)
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` (`SalvageAmounts`)

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN
- Contract pinned first: TEST-FIRST sortie results dialog contract
- Consumed by: the results dialog overlay and the `HexMapScene` landing child
- Reward source: AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6 (capture cycle)

# Deployment handoff carries the sortie result

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

At run end `PlayScene._finishRun` starts `HexMapScene` with
`{ payload, record, won, score, reward, assault, winBonusMinerals, demo,
demoDwellMs }`. The reward detail a victory paid (`HexCaptureResult`) and the
salvage a defeat forfeited (`DeploymentDefeatResult.forfeited`) never leave
`PlayScene`, so the map cannot show them. This item extends that handoff to
carry the compact sortie result the new builder consumes — passing the shipped
records, never a hand-copied subset of their numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PlayScene` resolves a `SortieResultRecord` at the end of a hex deployment (win: the target hex id from the hangar deployment plus the capture cycle's own `HexCaptureResult` from `resolveHexCapture`; loss: the target hex id plus the `forfeited` salvage `resolveDeploymentDefeat` settled) and adds it to the `scene.start(HEX_MAP_SCENE_KEY, …)` launch data.
- The handoff carries the shipped record objects rather than individually copied reward fields, so a reward kind added to `HexCaptureResult` later reaches the map without a second copy edit; no figure is recomputed on either side.
- `HexMapSceneData` gains the optional `sortie` field and `HexMapScene` holds it, exposes it through a `getSortieResult()` query seam returning a detached copy, and never persists it — no payload field, no store migration, and a later menu/hangar re-entry (which carries no `sortie`) shows no result.
- A defeat landing carries the forfeited unbanked salvage; a victory landing carries no `forfeited` value (nothing is forfeited on a win).
- Tests cover the victory handoff (capture record fields survive to the map), the defeat handoff (forfeited salvage survives), the detached-copy seam and the "launch data only" rule.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (the `_finishRun` hangar-war branch and `_forfeitUnbankedSalvage`)
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` (`HexMapSceneData`, `init`, `getSortieResult()`)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.captureCycle.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`

- Existing handoff: AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP, AH-0MWEXIOZZ009UX14

# Hex combat result dialog overlay scene

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

The map already presents the shipped mini-boss reward over a paused map through
`MiniBossWheelScene`/`MineralChoiceScene` (launch → pause → optional callback →
resume). The results dialog needs the same single-overlay contract but a
different body: read-only rows and one confirm to dismiss. This item adds that
overlay scene and registers it, so the landing child only has to launch it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new scene `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.ts` (key `HEX_COMBAT_RESULT_SCENE_KEY`) renders the ordered rows it is handed — a heading plus labelled lines — and derives no reward, score, weakness or rule of its own (no import of the capture cycle, the hex definitions or the store).
- It mirrors the shipped overlay contract: `init({ origin, title, rows, onDismiss, autoConfirmMs })`, a single confirm input (Enter, Space or a pointer click) dismisses it, `onDismiss` fires **exactly once**, and with `onDismiss` omitted it simply closes (isolated tests).
- In demo mode (`autoConfirmMs > 0`) it auto-confirms after that delay so the attract traversal cannot stall on it; normal play omits the delay and waits for the player.
- The scene is registered in the boot scene list (`src/core/gameConfig.ts`) and its capturability is decided explicitly in `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` with `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` updated to match, so the scene registry and the capture registry cannot drift.
- Tests cover: rows rendered verbatim, one confirm per dismissal (a second confirm cannot fire `onDismiss` twice), the keyboard and pointer paths, the demo auto-confirm delay, and the no-callback close.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.ts` (new)
- `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.test.ts` (new)
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts`
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`, `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (the overlay contract being mirrored, pattern only)

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN
- Depends on: pure sortie result view builder (the row shape it renders)

# HexMapScene presents the results dialog on landing

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

`HexMapScene.create()` builds the map and either presents a carried mini-boss
reward or schedules the demo dwell; the finished sortie is reduced to a thin
`runLine()` (`RUN: VICTORY|DEFEAT · score N`) plus the model's `winBonusLine`.
This item presents the carried sortie result as the results dialog over the
paused map before the demo dwell starts, and folds the two now-redundant lines
into it (parent assumption A1), leaving the distinct `RING WON` / `HANGAR FALLS`
assault banner in place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a hex deployment ends, landing on `HexMapScene` presents a modal dialog over the paused map stating the battle outcome (`VICTORY`/`DEFEAT`) and the run's final score.
- A landing that carries a sortie result presents the results dialog over the **paused** map, before the demo dwell is scheduled; the dialog text is the carried builder's rows (no scene-side derivation) and names the outcome (`VICTORY`/`DEFEAT`), the run's final score and every reward actually paid.
- A single confirm input dismisses the dialog, resumes the map and — in demo mode — restarts the shared dwell, so the attract traversal cannot stall on the dialog (a stepped-frame test advances from the landing through the dismissal to the next deployment).
- A landing with no sortie result (a plain menu/hangar re-entry) shows no dialog, and the sortie result is consumed exactly once so a second presentation path cannot re-show it.
- If the dialog overlay is not registered (headless test or misconfiguration) the map stays live and the demo dwell still starts, mirroring `presentReward()`'s no-stall rule.
- On a deployment landing the thin `runLine()` and the banked `winBonusLine` are no longer drawn — the dialog carries the outcome, score and win bonus — while the `assault` banner renders unchanged; the ordering with a carried mini-boss reward is deterministic and documented (sortie dialog first, then any reward).
- Tests cover both outcomes, the paused-map presentation, one-confirm dismissal and resume, the demo auto-dismiss without stall, the plain re-entry, the unregistered-overlay fallback and the folded-line assertions.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (the `runLine` render option and the last-sortie section)
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` (asserted unchanged — read-only harness, no divergent copy)

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN
- Depends on: deployment handoff carries the sortie result; hex combat result dialog overlay scene
- Folds: AH-0MWEXIOZZ009UX14 (run line), AH-0MWF2Q2JC008MAJE (win-bonus line)
- Keeps: AH-0MWEZZA4E0081NJ5 (assault banner)

# Docs: record the hex combat results dialog

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

The hex map's landing surface is described in the README, the Game Design
Document, the outer-loop design of record, the gym-parity record and the
gameplay-capture guide — each still describing the landing as a thin run line
plus a banked win-bonus line with no results dialog. This item brings the
documentation of record back in line with the shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — code comments in the touched source files, the README, the Game Design Document, and any relevant docs site or wiki entry — so no relevant entry still claims the landing shows only a run line and a win-bonus line.
- The README `HexMapScene` entry describes the post-battle results dialog: outcome, final score, the rewards actually paid and, on a defeat, the boss's authored strengths/weaknesses, the unclaimed grant and the forfeited unbanked salvage — replacing the claim that a landing shows only the run line and win-bonus line.
- GDD §8.2 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D, § *UI / scene surface*) record the new landing surface and name the pure builder (`src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts`) and the overlay scene as the single source of the dialog text.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records the parity position: `GymHexWar` stays a read-only ring harness that runs no deployment and no combat, the dialog is a landing-surface presentation rather than a gameplay object, and there is no divergent gym copy (with the reason, per the gym↔game parity convention).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` records the new launch-data field(s) and any capture-registry change so a capture config can drive the dialog.
- Every claim is accurate against the shipped code and written in UK English; the module/header comments in the touched source files describe the new landing presentation; any repo docs assertion test passes.

**Key Files:**

- `./README.md`
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2)
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D § UI / scene surface)
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`

# Sortie results dialog end-to-end verification

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

The dialog spans four layers — the pure builder, the deployment handoff, the
overlay scene and the map landing — plus the docs and the scene registries. This
item verifies the integrated slice end to end and closes the parent's "full
project test suite must pass" criterion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- The suite is run through the test skill (`/skill:test`, never an ad-hoc suite invocation), and any failure is triaged into a critical `test-failure` item per the triage policy.
- End-to-end assertions cover both outcomes: a hex deployment win lands on the map, presents the dialog with the paid rewards, dismisses with one confirm and leaves an interactive map; a hex deployment loss presents the boss strengths/weaknesses, the unclaimed grant and the forfeited salvage.
- The attract traversal is verified end to end: a demo landing presents the dialog, auto-dismisses after the shared dwell and reaches the next deployment without stalling or skipping a screen.
- Gym↔game parity holds: `GymHexWar` is unchanged and still renders the same shared model/renderer pair, and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (the duplicate-body guard) plus the gym-parity docs assertion pass.
- The scene registries agree — the boot scene list, `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` and `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` — and the docs assertions in the suite pass.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.hangarWar.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (unchanged guard)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` (unchanged guard)

- Parent: AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN

- Gate that enforces the suite on push: dev-push gate (test skill)

# When starting a Hex War battle, show the ship config screen

## Problem statement

A Hex War (Hangar War) battle can currently be started **without ever seeing
the ship-configuration screen**: activating an unheld hex on the hex map calls
`HexMapScene.deploy()`, which starts `PlayScene` directly (`src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`,
`deploy()`). The player therefore commits a life with whatever loadout is
already equipped, and the boss's authored **strengths / weaknesses** — the
strategic intel the design promises ("the weapon that is strong against the
boss", `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *Known-ahead intel*) — are not visible
where the loadout is actually chosen.

This item makes the **hangar screen the pre-battle config screen on the way
into a hex** (the design of record calls it "a deployment / hull-and-loadout
selector on the way into a hex", `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md:1058`), and
makes that screen **target-aware**: it names the boss of the hex being attacked,
prints its strengths and weaknesses, and marks the player's weapons **green when
they counter that boss** and **red when the boss resists them**.

## Users

- **The strategist** — "I read that this boss is weak to `waveLaser`; when I
  pick the hex I want the config screen to tell me to bring it, and to warn me
  off the weapons the boss resists."
- **The grinder** — "I want the pre-battle screen to make a wrong loadout
  legible *before* I spend a life, not after three boss phases."
- **The accessibility-minded player** — "I must be able to read weapon
  effectiveness without relying on colour alone." (Repo CVD policy: never
  colour-only.)
- **The producer/maintainer** — "One shared model and renderer, so the game and
  `GymHangar` show the same screen and no scene owns a second matchup rule."

Example user stories:

- As a player, I select a hex on the map and land on the hangar/config screen
  for **that** hex before the fight starts.
- As a player, I see the target boss and its strengths and weaknesses on the
  config screen.
- As a player, I see which of my weapons are strong (green) and weak (red)
  against this boss, with a non-colour marker too.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The ship config screen comes before a hex battle.** Activating an unheld
   hex on the hex map opens the ship-config (hangar) screen pre-targeted at that
   hex and does **not** start `PlayScene` directly. That screen's `▶ DEPLOY`
   row names the target hex and launches the deployment at it. Entering the
   hangar from the menu (no chosen hex) targets the existing default (the
   weakest unheld hex via `selectDeploymentHex`), so no hex battle begins
   without the config screen first.
2. **The target boss's intel is shown.** The config screen publishes the target
   hex's boss name and its authored `strengths` and `weaknesses` lists in a
   clearly labelled section, resolved from the shared ring definitions
   (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`) — never a scene-local copy. An
   unauthored/unknown hex renders an explicit "unknown" fallback instead of
   throwing.
3. **Weapons are marked for the matchup.** Every weapon row the screen presents
   for the target — the `LOADOUT` starting-weapon selector **and** the unlock
   tree's weapon entries — carries its matchup against that boss's lists: a
   weapon in the boss's `weaknesses` (it counters the boss) is **strong** →
   green; a weapon in the boss's `strengths` (the boss resists it) is **weak**
   → red; every other weapon is **neutral**. Matchup resolution normalises the
   ring-data alias (`waveLaser` ↔ catalogue `wave_laser`) through the shared
   mapping the capture cycle already owns, so a catalogue weapon and an
   authored list can never disagree.
4. **Accessible and unambiguous, not colour-only.** Each strong/weak state also
   carries a non-colour marker (a glyph plus text tag, e.g. `▲ EFFECTIVE` /
   `▼ RESISTED`) so the matchup is readable without colour, per the repo's CVD
   policy; the highlight is visually distinguishable from the existing
   actionable (green) and disabled (muted) row colours.
5. **One shared code path (gym↔game parity).** The intel and the matchup live
   in the pure model (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) so `GymHangar`
   renders the identical screen read-only. The attract/demo traversal traverses
   the new config step (`map → config → deployment`) without stalling and
   within its existing action bound.
6. **Automated tests cover the feature.** A pure matchup resolver
   (`strong`/`weak`/`neutral`, including the `waveLaser`↔`wave_laser` alias);
   the model's boss-intel and per-row matchup fields; the map→config routing
   and target carry-through; `▶ DEPLOY` launching at the target hex; the
   unknown-hex fallback; and `GymHangar` parity of the shared model.
7. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Before every hex battle the player configures the ship on the hangar screen with
the target boss's strengths and weaknesses in view and their weapons marked
green or red for whether they counter or bounce off that boss — so a loadout is
a deliberate counter-pick, not a blind guess.

## Assumptions (documented; producer may override at review)

- **A1 — "ship config screen" means the existing hangar screen.** Reuse
  `HangarScene` / `buildHangarScreenModel` / `renderHangarScreen`; do not build
  a second config screen or a forked model.
- **A2 — "strong / weak" is player-centric.** A weapon the boss is **weak
  against** is strong (green); a weapon the boss is **strong against** is weak
  (red). This follows the design's "the weapon that is strong against the boss"
  language.
- **A3 — Highlight scope.** The highlight applies to every weapon row the
  screen presents for the target (the `LOADOUT` selector and the unlock tree's
  weapon entries); non-weapon rows keep their existing rendering.
- **A4 — Default target.** With no explicitly chosen hex (menu entry), the
  screen shows the intel of the deployment it would actually launch, i.e. the
  weakest unheld hex.
- **A5 — Transient target.** The target hex is launch data only; nothing new is
  persisted and the payload schema is unchanged.
- **A6 — CVD.** Green/red is always paired with a non-colour marker.
- **A7 — Display/flow only.** This item does **not** make the lists change the
  fight; that is AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ.

## Constraints

- **Pure model, shared renderer.** Intel and matchup are computed in the pure
  screen model from shared data; the scene only presents and persists. Both the
  game and `GymHangar` consume the same model/renderer (AGENTS.md gym↔game
  parity, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **Reuse the shared weapon-id alias.** Ring data spells the laser
  `waveLaser`; the catalogue spells it `wave_laser`. Match through the existing
  `GRANT_ALIASES` / `resolveHexGrant` mapping (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`),
  never a second ad-hoc table.
- **Never colour-only** (CVD policy precedent in `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`).
- **No arcade-path change.** `PlayScene`, the arcade checkpoint, the leaderboard
  and the feature-flag entry surface are untouched; a hex deployment stays a
  separate session (no checkpoint write/clear).
- **No purchase/combat-rule change.** Prices, ownership, gating and the run's
  hit model are unchanged; this item changes what the config screen **shows**
  and when it is reached.
- **No stall in attract/demo.** The bot must traverse the added config step and
  remain bounded by `HANGAR_WAR_TRAVERSAL_MAX_ACTIONS`.
- **Layout safety.** The new intel section must not collide with the existing
  rows; keep the shared layout constants single-sourced.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A counter-weapon auto-pick, damage-type combat effects,
  in-combat effectiveness glyphs, or reshaping the unlock-tree economy are out
  of scope; record them as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Existing state

- **The map deploys directly.** `HexMapScene.deploy(hexId)`
  (`src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`) builds the deployment and `scene.start`s
  `PlayScene`; the map's hex activation calls it. The map's own detail panel
  already publishes `STRENGTHS:` / `WEAKNESSES:` (via `buildHexMapModel`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) but has no loadout control.
- **The hangar already is a config screen, but not target-aware.** `HangarScene`
  renders the unlock tree plus the hull / starting-weapon / modifier selectors
  and the `▶ DEPLOY` row through `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`. Its
  `deploy()` targets whatever `buildHangarDeployment` selects (explicit `hexId`
  or the weakest unheld hex); it accepts no target from launch data and shows
  no boss intel.
- **Boss strengths/weaknesses are authored data.** `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`
  authors `boss`, `strengths` (weapons the boss resists, e.g. `['cannon','dual']`)
  and `weaknesses` (weapons that counter it, e.g. `['nova','arc']`) per hex.
  `resolveHexGrant` + `GRANT_ALIASES` normalise the ring/grant spelling to
  catalogue ids.
- **The catalogue's weapons** are `spread`, `wave_laser`, `ricochet`, `cluster`
  (plus grant-only/other entries), keyed by `id`; a hangar weapon option's `id`
  is a catalogue id, while boss lists carry shipped `WeaponId` spellings.
- **Parity gym.** `GymHangar` renders `buildHangarScreenModel` /
  `renderHangarScreen` read-only; any new model field automatically reaches it
  but must also be asserted there.

## Desired change

- **Route the map into the config screen.** `HexMapScene`'s hex activation opens
  `HangarScene` carrying `{ payload, storage, demo, demoDwellMs, targetHexId }`
  instead of starting `PlayScene`.
- **Make the hangar target-aware.** `HangarScene` accepts an optional
  `targetHexId` in launch data, threads it into `buildHangarScreenModel` and
  into `deploy()` so `▶ DEPLOY` launches at the chosen hex (default: weakest
  unheld hex).
- **Add the boss-intel section to the pure model.** Extend
  `buildHangarScreenModel` with the target hex's boss, strengths and weaknesses
  (resolved from the shared definitions), plus a per-weapon-row `matchup`
  verdict (`strong` | `weak` | `neutral`) for the `LOADOUT` selector and the
  unlock tree's weapon entries.
- **Add one pure matchup resolver** beside the ring/capture helpers: given a
  weapon id (catalogue or shipped spelling) and a hex definition, return
  `strong` / `weak` / `neutral`, normalising through the shared alias map.
- **Render it.** Extend `renderHangarScreen` to draw the intel section and to
  colour/mark weapon rows (green `▲ EFFECTIVE`, red `▼ RESISTED`, neutral
  unchanged), without colliding with the existing rows.
- **Traverse it in the demo.** Keep the attract traversal total: the map's
  "deploy at hex" step now lands on the config screen, whose own decision
  buys or deploys at the carried target.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — boss-intel section, per-row matchup
  verdict, coloured/glyphed rendering, target-aware DEPLOY.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — accept `targetHexId`, thread into the model and
  `deploy()`.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — route hex activation to the config screen with
  the target hex.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` / `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — shared
  definitions source (read-only).
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — reuse `GRANT_ALIASES` /
  `resolveHexGrant` for spelling normalisation (or extract the alias lookup).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — target-hex resolution
  (`selectDeploymentHex`) reuse.
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` — demo routing through the config step.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — parity of the new model/render.
- Tests: `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`, plus new pure-model/matchup tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat**
  (open): the mechanical effect of the same lists. This item is the
  **display/flow** half; they share the `strong`/`weak` vocabulary and the
  alias normalisation, but neither duplicates the other's rules.
- **AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE — Build Candidate D — Hangar War (outer loop)**
  (completed): the design of record, including "a deployment / hull-and-loadout
  selector on the way into a hex".
- **AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1 — Hangar scene: unlock tree and deployment/loadout
  selector** (completed): the screen and model this item extends.
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2 — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel** (completed):
  the map that already publishes boss strengths/weaknesses and the target rule.
- **AH-0MVUXC2DD003HN0I — Hangar War menu entry, mode separation and deployment**
  (completed): the `▶ DEPLOY` / deployment-payload path.
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7 — Saved ship configurations** (open): adjacent loadout
  UX; no overlap with this item's intel/highlight goal.
- Automated find-related report also surfaced: AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9 (CSV seed
  data), AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (deployments start with the default weapon only),
  AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB (held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES, blocked).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**No producer interview was required.** The seed context plus the design of
record (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *UI / scene surface* and §
*Known-ahead intel*, GDD §8.2) were sufficient to draft a clear brief. The
interpretive decisions below are recorded as **documented assumptions** (see
*Assumptions* above); the producer may override any of them at review without
gating the brief.

- **Q1 — Which screen is the "ship config screen"?**
  Answer (agent, documented assumption A1): the existing hangar screen
  (`HangarScene` + `buildHangarScreenModel`/`renderHangarScreen`). Evidence:
  `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md:1058` names "a deployment / hull-and-loadout
  selector on the way into a hex", and `hangarScreen.ts`'s own header calls it
  the deployment/hull-and-loadout selector.
- **Q2 — "Strong/weak" from whose perspective?**
  Answer (agent, documented assumption A2): player-centric — boss `weaknesses`
  = weapons that counter it → green; boss `strengths` = weapons it resists →
  red. Evidence: the design's "the weapon that is strong against the boss"
  (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *Known-ahead intel*; GDD §8.2 "Boss and
  weapon strength are known ahead").
- **Q3 — Which weapon rows are highlighted?**
  Answer (agent, documented assumption A3): every weapon row shown for the
  target — the `LOADOUT` starting-weapon selector and the unlock tree's weapon
  entries. Non-weapon rows unchanged.
- **Q4 — Normalisation of ring vs catalogue weapon ids?**
  Answer: reuse the shared `GRANT_ALIASES` / `resolveHexGrant` mapping
  (`waveLaser` ↔ `wave_laser`); no second alias table. Evidence: the related
  item AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ Q5 fixed this same normalisation.
- **Q5 — Colour-only signalling?**
  Answer: no — pair green/red with a non-colour glyph/tag, per the repo CVD
  policy (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`).

# When completing first battle no minerals rewarded

## Problem statement

Today, a winning hangar battle that targets **no hex** — which is the first
battle of a fresh war, and the first battle after a war restart — shows
`WIN BONUS BANKED: +100 MINERALS` on the hex map, but nothing is banked: the
hangar still shows the same salvage balance, so the player is promised a reward
that never arrives.

## Root cause (evidence-backed)

The win-path bonus is banked by `PlayScene._resolveHangarWarCapture()`, which
**returns early** when the deployment has no hex:

```ts
// src/scenes/PlayScene.ts (≈4226)
const deployment = this.hangarWarDeployment;
if (!deployment || !deployment.hexId) return;   // ← no hex ⇒ no capture, no bonus
```

A fresh war stores an **empty ring** — `createDefaultPayload()` writes
`ring: { ringIndex: DEFAULT_RING_INDEX, hexes: [] }`
(`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`), and `restartHangarWar()` rebuilds that
same fresh payload (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`).

Only the **hex map** materialises the ring (`materialiseRing()` in
`src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`, persisted on first entry). The **hangar screen does
not**: `HangarScene.deploy()` builds the deployment from the raw stored payload,
so `selectDeploymentHex()` returns `null` for the empty ring and
`buildHangarDeployment()` records `hexId: null`
(`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`). The hangar's own DEPLOY row even
reads `▶ DEPLOY — no hex · aggression 0 · level 1`
(`formatRingLine` → `Ring 1 — 0/0 hexes held`).

The run itself is still a hangar-war run (`isHangarWarRun()` is true whenever a
deployment exists), so the mini-boss defeat ends on `_finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory`
→ `_resolveHangarWarCapture()` (no-op) → `_finishRun()` starts `HexMapScene`
with:

```ts
winBonusMinerals: won ? WIN_BONUS_MINERALS : 0,   // unconditional on `won`
```

The map renders `winBonusLine` from that value
(`src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` →
`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` → `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`), so the
announcement is decoupled from what was actually banked. The announcement is
**not** derived from the capture result — it is passed as a constant.

Consequence: the first hexless win banks **no bonus and no capture salvage**
(the capture cycle never runs), while the win screen claims +100 minerals.

Path evidence:
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_resolveHangarWarCapture()` early return (≈4228),
  `winBonusMinerals: won ? WIN_BONUS_MINERALS : 0` (≈5687).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — `hexId: hex?.id ?? null` from
  `selectDeploymentHex()` (returns `null` for an empty ring).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `createDefaultPayload()` empty ring.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — `deploy()` builds from the raw payload (no ring
  materialisation).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — the map materialises + persists the ring.

## Users

- **New player**: finishes the first battle after opening Hangar War, is told
  100 minerals were banked, then finds the hangar's salvage unchanged — the
  first reward of the outer loop appears broken.
- **Returning player who restarts the war**: sees the same mismatch on the new
  war's first battle.
- **Producer / balance owner**: needs the announced reward and the banked
  balance to agree in every path, because the win-bonus amount is a balance knob
  (`WIN_BONUS_MINERALS`).

User stories:

- As a new player, when I win my first battle, the minerals the win screen says
  I was awarded are in my hangar.
- As a player, I am never told a reward was banked unless it was actually banked.
- As a player, my first deployment targets a real hex (like every later
  deployment from the map), so my first win captures ground and grants the hex's
  authored entry.
- As a player on a save where the ring cannot be materialised, a winning battle
  still pays the fixed bonus — the run is a hangar deployment either way.

## Acceptance Criteria

Producer decisions recorded 2026-11-19 (Q1 = (a), Q2 = (a), Q3 = (a)) — see
Appendix. The first battle of a fresh war (and of a restarted war) now targets a
real hex and pays through the normal capture; the bonus-banking fallback exists
for a winning deployment that still has no target hex; and the announcement is
derived from what was actually banked.

- **Announcement ⇔ banking (Q3 = a).** A winning hangar battle never announces
  `WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS` unless that exact number was added to
  `hangar.bankedMinerals` in the same run resolution; the value the map renders
  is read from the win resolution's own record, not from
  `won ? WIN_BONUS_MINERALS : 0`.
- **Hexless win still pays (Q1 = a).** A winning hangar deployment with
  `hexId: null` banks exactly `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` (minerals only, capture
  watermark untouched, no hex state change), so the announced line and the
  hangar's salvage balance agree.
- **First deployment targets a real hex (Q2 = a).** A fresh war's ring is
  materialised from the authored definitions and persisted when the hangar
  screen loads its payload, so `▶ DEPLOY` names a real hex and the first battle
  banks its salvage + bonus through the normal capture cycle. The same holds
  after a war restart.
- **Exactly once.** A winning deployment pays the bonus once — the capture path
  when it ran, the fallback only when it did not; no path can pay both.
- **Regression tests.** A winning deployment with `hexId: null` asserts the
  announced bonus equals the actual `bankedMinerals` delta; a fresh-war hangar
  load asserts the ring is materialised, persisted and deployed at a real hex; a
  real-hex win asserts the captured balance is not topped up a second time.
- All existing hangar-war, capture-cycle, hex-map and win-bonus tests keep
  passing; the full project test suite passes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Impact

The first battle's reward is real: the minerals the win screen says were banked
are in the hangar, and the screen never claims a reward it did not pay.

## Constraints

- The win-bonus **amount** (`WIN_BONUS_MINERALS = CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT = 100`)
  is a provisional balance value baselined by `AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA`; this item
  must not change the number, only whether/what is announced.
- The win-path decisions recorded in `AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2` (producer Q1 = (c),
  Q2 = (a), Q3 = (b), 2026-11-13) stay authoritative: no mini-boss wheel, no
  bonus cores, minerals only, announced on the landing.
- The capture cycle remains the single authority for banking; a fix must not
  introduce a second write path or a new storage key.
- Demo/attract runs never persist — a demo hexless win must not write.
- Materialising the ring on hangar load is a **persisted** state change: it must
  go through `saveHangarWarPayload()`, respect the demo/storage guards already
  used by `HexMapScene.persist()`, and never pad or discard a partial ring.

## Interpretation of the producer's answers

Q1 = (a) and Q2 = (a) are complementary, not alternatives: the normal first
battle now targets a materialised hex, so it pays through the capture cycle;
Q1 = (a)'s "bank anyway" is the **fallback** for a winning deployment that still
has no target hex (an unauthored ring, or a save whose ring cannot be
generated). Payment is mutually exclusive: a capture that ran pays the bonus
itself, and the fallback pays only when no capture ran.

## Existing state

- Win bonus: `bankWinBonus()` (`src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts`), applied
  in `PlayScene._resolveHangarWarCapture()` only when a hex capture runs.
- Announcement: `winBonusMinerals` passed as run launch data to `HexMapScene`,
  rendered as `winBonusLine` in the `last-sortie` section.
- Ring materialisation exists (`materialiseRing()`) but is only used by
  `HexMapScene` (which persists it) and `resolveHexCapture()`;
  `HangarScene.loadPayload()` does not materialise, so a fresh war's DEPLOY is
  built from an empty ring.
- No test covers a winning deployment with `hexId: null`; every existing
  win-bonus test deploys at a real hex.

## Desired change

Per the producer's answers (Q1 = a, Q2 = a, Q3 = a):

1. **Ring materialisation at the hangar entry (Q2 = a)** — `HangarScene` loads
   its payload through `materialiseRing()` and persists the materialised ring
   (the `HexMapScene.init()` behaviour), so a fresh war's `▶ DEPLOY` targets a
   real hex and the first battle runs the normal capture cycle. Ring progress
   (`Ring 1 — 0/6 hexes held`) then reads correctly from the start.
2. **Bonus banking on a hexless win (Q1 = a)** — `_resolveHangarWarCapture()`
   gains a hexless winning branch that banks `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` through
   `bankWinBonus()` and persists it through the existing payload write, without
   touching the capture watermark and without inventing a hex capture.
3. **Announcement derived from the resolution (Q3 = a)** — the bonus the map
   announces comes from the win resolution's own record (the amount it banked),
   so an unbanked bonus can never be rendered and a double pay is impossible.
4. **Tests** for the three behaviours plus the existing suites, and the
   in-code notes beside `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` / `bankWinBonus()` updated to
   describe the hexless fallback.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — hexless winning branch in
  `_resolveHangarWarCapture()`; pass the banked amount (not the constant) to
  `HexMapScene` from `_finishRun()`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — materialise the ring on payload load and persist
  it; deploy from the materialised payload.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — reuse `materialiseRing()`; the capture
  rules themselves are unchanged.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — unaffected if the payload is
  already materialised; verify `hexId` resolves non-null.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — unchanged unless the launch-data field is
  renamed; the map keeps materialising for direct entries.
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` / `hangarEconomy.ts` — comment-only
  updates for the hexless fallback; `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` value unchanged.
- Tests: `src/scenes/PlayScene.hexMiniBossVictory.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.captureCycle.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` is unaffected (no gameplay object changes); the
  win-path notes live beside `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` and in
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** — Win path: suppress the mini-boss wheel and bank a
  fixed post-win bonus on hex wins (open, `plan_complete`; all children done).
  The originating design decision for the bonus this item exposes as mis-paid.
- **AH-0MWF2Q0O0008NGKL** — PlayScene: suppress win-path wheel and bank the
  bonus on win resolution (completed). Introduced the `won ? … : 0` announcement.
- **AH-0MWF2Q2JC008MAJE** — announce the banked win bonus before the map
  (completed). The surface that now over-claims.
- **AH-0MWL8CDGN005878A** — Owned hexes provide minerals (open). A separate
  income mechanic; not this bug.
- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** — Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward
  value per hex deployment (completed). Owns the bonus amount.
- **AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6 / AH-0MWCOW4IQ003XST5** — capture cycle and mini-boss
  victory paths this bug runs through.
- **AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP** — a deployment ends on the hex map (the surface that
  shows the announcement).
- **AH-0MVUXC118004B4OX** — salvage banking at checkpoints (adjacent but not the
  same banking path).
- Duplicate check: no item already covers this defect; the automated
  related-work report below is complementary, not overlapping.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a hexless winning deployment is a defect, not a mode — once
  the hangar materialises the ring it should be unreachable in normal play and
  exists only for an unauthored/ungeneratable ring.
- **Risk — double pay:** the capture path and the new hexless fallback both pay
  the bonus; the implementation must make them mutually exclusive (a
  `banked`/`captured` flag on the win resolution), covered by the "exactly once"
  AC and a dedicated test.
- **Risk — scope creep:** "make the first battle pay", "capture a hex" and
  "fix the hangar's `0/0 hexes held` line" are three related changes; extra
  ring/UI polish belongs in linked items, not here.
- **Risk — double-counting:** any bonus banking added on the hexless path must
  stay outside the capture watermark (the reason `bankWinBonus()` is
  watermark-free) so a later checkpoint cannot re-bank.
- **Risk — demo writes:** an attract/demo run must still never persist a bonus
  (`_saveHangarWarPayload` demo guard).
- **Risk — test gaps:** the repo's scene tests fabricate deployments, so a
  `hexId: null` fixture must be added deliberately; otherwise the regression is
  invisible again.
- **Risk — stale balance display:** if the fix banks on the hexless path, the
  hangar must show the new balance when the map hands back (`openHangar` passes
  the map's payload, so no reload is expected).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Asked in a downtime-dispatched (non-interactive) intake session: the questions
were recorded on the work item with `needsProducerReview=true`, and the producer
answered in the follow-up session on 2026-11-19. The agent's recommendation is
recorded alongside each accepted answer for auditability.

### Q1 — What should a winning deployment with no target hex do? — Answer: **(a)**

Path context: a hangar `▶ DEPLOY` on a fresh war, or the first battle after a
war restart.

Options as asked: (a) bank the fixed bonus anyway on any winning deployment;
(b) bank nothing and show no bonus line; (c) materialise the ring so the first
battle always targets a real hex and pays through the capture cycle.

- Answer (producer, session reply 2026-11-19): **(a)**.
- Agent recommendation was (c) with (b) as a defensive guarantee; the producer
  chose the fallback-payment option instead. Q2 = (a) supplies the ring
  materialisation separately, so both effects land — see *Interpretation of the
  producer's answers*.

### Q2 — Where should a fresh war's ring be materialised? — Answer: **(a)**

Options as asked: (a) on hangar payload load, persisted (the hex map's
behaviour); (b) at deploy time only; (c) never.

- Answer (producer, session reply 2026-11-19): **(a)** — matches the agent
  recommendation.

### Q3 — Should the announcement be derived from the amount actually banked? — Answer: **(a)**

Options as asked: (a) yes, pass the banked delta; (b) keep the constant.

- Answer (producer, session reply 2026-11-19): **(a)** — matches the agent
  recommendation.

### Research recorded during intake

- The win-path decisions (`AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2`, producer 2026-11-13: Q1 = c,
  Q2 = a, Q3 = b) remain the governing design: no wheel, minerals only, bonus
  announced on the landing. This item changes **when** the bonus is banked and
  **what** is announced, not the amount.
- `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` (= `CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT` = 100) is a provisional
  balance value owned by `AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA`; it is not re-tuned here.
- No existing test exercises a winning deployment with `hexId: null`, which is
  why the regression was invisible.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWHTZRQJ008O9CE** – [test-failure] src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts — run upgrade snapshot (AH-0MWHF6X9N0082BRO, red-first guard) — persists the snapshot on the stored defender through resolveHexCapture — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MWHTZMEW005DDM3** – [test-failure] src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts — run upgrade snapshot (AH-0MWHF6X9N0082BRO, red-first guard) — records the snapshot on the defender and rates it through the one derivation — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MWMT4S5U001EGDF** – Hex map routes into the config screen (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: available, awarded, battle, first, hangar (+6 more)
- `README.md` — matched: available, battle, first, hangar, minerals (+5 more)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: available, battle, first, hangar, minerals (+5 more)
