# Chime whenever a mineral is collected

## Problem statement

Collecting minerals — the game's core economy loop — is completely silent
today: `_collectMineral` credits the hold and updates the HUD bar, but the
player gets no audio confirmation at all. A successful mineral run therefore
feels flat, and the only confirmation is a small HUD bar the player is not
looking at during combat.

## Users

- **Player (game):** wants collecting minerals to feel rewarding and immediate
  without looking away from the ship.
  - *As a player, when my ship picks up a mineral I hear a quiet, satisfying
    chime so the pickup registers without me checking the HUD.*
  - *As a player, when I sweep up a scatter of minerals in quick succession
    the chime steps upward so a good run reads as rising musical momentum —
    and it settles back to its base note once I stop collecting.*
- **Maintainer / gym author:** needs the feedback to run the same code in the
  game and every gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity), with the pitch/level tuning
  in one place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every **player** mineral pickup plays a quiet chime: one chime per collected
  mineral, on every path that credits the mineral hold (`PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene` and its subclasses, `GymLevel`, `GymPowerUpsUtility` and
  the leveling gyms' mineral supply), through **one shared implementation** —
  no per-scene copy of the pitch/escalation logic.
- The chime **rises in pitch** with each successive pickup while the player
  keeps collecting, and **resets to its base pitch** after a gap of
  `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` (1.5 s) with no pickup; the rise is capped at a
  documented ceiling (A-minor ladder `[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]` semitones, i.e.
  up to one octave) so a long streak never becomes shrill.
- The chime is **subtle and quiet**: the baked asset peaks at ≤ 0.2 (the
  documented player-cue ceiling in GDD §7.3) with a stated target level in the
  recipe header, and it never masks enemy-fire telegraphs. It obeys the global
  SFX volume/mute settings and the shared per-cue voice limiter, and degrades
  to a silent no-op with no `AudioContext` (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
  browsers).
- **Enemy absorption plays no chime** — the feedback is player-only (an enemy
  hoovering up a mineral must not read as a player reward).
- New cue is delivered through the existing **ToneForge baked pipeline**: a new
  `aihell-mineral-chime` recipe (next free seed **32292**), a manifest entry, a
  deterministic baked WAV plus committed checksum, and `npm run
  build-audio:verify` passes unchanged for every pre-existing asset.
- The pitch-escalation state machine is **pure and unit-tested** with an
  injected clock: rise per pickup, cap, reset after the gap, and reset on
  run restart / scene teardown. A dense burst (several minerals in one frame,
  a 100-mineral gym field, Mineral Scoop sweep) is bounded — it may not
  shotgun-stack chimes beyond the shared voice limiter.
- Tests cover the cue (export + manifest + resolvable baked asset), the
  escalation state machine, and the shared wiring in the game and in the gyms.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (specifically
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` both tables and GDD §7.3 /
  §4.5).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Collecting minerals now rewards the ear as well as the HUD: each pickup gives a
quiet chime that steps upward through a quick scatter, so a mineral run feels
satisfying and audibly productive without the player ever glancing at the
mineral bar.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** the escalation rule and the cue dispatch live
  once; the game and every gym consume the same implementation. Divergence, if
  any (e.g. the leveling gyms' bespoke collection loops), must be justified in
  the work item and in a code comment.
- **Baked audio only:** no runtime synthesis. The cue must be a ToneForge
  recipe rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`, with SHA-256 checksums committed
  to `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`; renders are deterministic (the pipeline
  renders twice and compares).
- **Enemy-balance guards are untouched:** the new recipe is a *player* cue, so it
  is tagged `player`/`mineral`/`pickup` with no enemy tag and no
  `AMPLITUDE_TIERS` key (the guard only analyses the enemy family). The A-minor
  conformance guard likewise applies to enemy cues only, but the pitch ladder is
  musical anyway so the cue sits inside the game's tonal language.
- **Player-cue ceiling** ≤ 0.2 peak (GDD §7.3), and every existing player cue
  degrades to a silent no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- **No second throttle:** the shared per-cue voice limiter (4 voices / 150 ms,
  `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts`) already bounds overlap through the one
  `playCue` funnel; add no parallel rate limiter.
- **Reset gap is game time, not wall time**, so a paused scene cannot expire a
  streak mid-run and the streak does not depend on frame rate.
- **Purely audio:** no change to mineral economy, drop rules, collection
  geometry, scoring, telemetry or the hold model.
- No new persisted `rules.ts` tunable — pitch/level/length are fixed named
  constants beside the cue (precedent: `COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES`,
  `WAVE_LASER_VOLUME_SCALE`), so retuning is a one-line change with no re-bake.
- Scope-creep guard: extra opportunities found on the way (e.g. a pitch ladder
  for power-up pickups, a streak HUD indicator) are recorded as separate linked
  work items, not folded into this one.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "slightly" means small steps — one A-minor scale degree per
  pickup, capped at an octave. If the producer prefers a chromatic ladder or a
  smaller cap, only `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES` changes.
- **Assumption:** the reset window is 1.5 s (`MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS`), the
  "short period" in the brief; one constant to retune.
- **Assumption:** a red 10-value deposit and a scattered pair each chime once
  per collected mineral, not once per mineral *unit*, so a deposit does not fire
  ten chimes.
- **Risk — aliasing:** reusing `aihell-mineral-tinkle` (the Mystery UFO spill
  cue) would make a pickup indistinguishable from a spill; mitigated by a
  dedicated `aihell-mineral-chime` recipe.
- **Risk — audio clutter:** mineral fields are dense (gyms seed 100 minerals,
  Mineral Scoop sweeps, doubled drops). Mitigated by the voice limiter, a quiet
  baked level and the cap on the pitch ladder; verified by a dense-burst test.
- **Risk — pitch/duration coupling:** raising pitch via `playbackRate` also
  shortens the cue (0.2 s → 0.1 s at the octave). Accepted (the countdown tick
  precedent) and documented in the recipe comment.
- **Risk — render environment:** baking needs the local ToneForge CLI
  (`../ToneForge`); if it is unavailable the implementer must not hand-write a
  WAV — stop and report the blocker.

## Existing state

- Collection seam: `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` (`collectMinerals`) is
  shared by `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility`; each scene supplies an `onPlayerCollected` callback
  (`_collectMineral` / `_collectGymMineral`) that credits the hold and syncs the
  HUD. `GymWeaponLeveling` / `GymPowerUpLeveling` run their own bespoke
  overlap loops over a seeded mineral supply.
- No pickup sound exists anywhere on those paths.
- `playMineralTinkleSound()` (`aihell-mineral-tinkle`, seed 32290) exists but is
  the Mystery UFO **spill** cue, fired once per spill with the scattered drops.
- Pitch escalation by playback rate already ships for the countdown tick:
  `playCountdownTickSound(step)` + `COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES` +
  `countdownTickRate(step)` (`src/audio/effects.ts`).
- One cue funnel: `playCue()` applies the per-cue voice limiter, seed variant
  pick and the shared master gain; `SfxPlayOptions` supports `rate`, `volume`,
  `delay`, `loop`.
- The seed block 32100–32299 is reserved for game recipes; the highest shipped
  seed is 32291, so **32292** is the next free seed.
- Contract tests (`src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`,
  `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`) fail if an `effects.ts` cue has no
  manifest entry or no baked asset — a new cue cannot ship half-wired.

## Desired change

1. **New baked cue** `aihell-mineral-chime` — a short (~0.2 s, ≤ 0.2 peak)
   bright chime: one triangle/sine partial with a gentle decay and a quiet
   shimmer, deliberately distinct from `aihell-mineral-tinkle` (no falling
   E7 → A6 sweep, no noise tick) so a pickup never reads as a spill. Recipe,
   manifest entry (seed 32292), baked WAV, checksum.
2. **`playMineralCollectChimeSound()`** in `src/audio/effects.ts` — plays the
   cue at the current streak step's rate, with the semitone ladder, cap and gap
   as named constants.
3. **Shared escalation state machine** — a small Phaser-free module (e.g.
   `src/audio/mineralChime.ts`) owning the streak counter, the game-clock gap
   check and the reset, with an injectable clock for deterministic tests. One
   exported `noteMineralCollected(nowMs)` that advances the step and returns the
   playback rate, plus a reset seam for run restart / scene teardown.
4. **Wiring** — every player-collection path calls the shared seam exactly once
   per collected mineral (preferably from the shared collection layer or one
   shared core hook rather than five copies).
5. **Docs** — recipe header, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (mapping
   table + new-recipes table), GDD §7.3 cue table and the §4.5 collection
   bullet, plus the code comments recording the pitch-ladder and gap rationale.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` — New shared escalation state machine
  (streak step, cap, 1.5 s game-clock gap, reset seam; injectable clock).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — New `playMineralCollectChimeSound()` plus the
  semitone-ladder/gap constants beside the cue.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — Shared collection seam; preferred single
  dispatch point for the player-pickup chime.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_collectMineral` (game path; must not duplicate
  the escalation logic).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_collectMineral` (every
  formation gym).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  — Remaining player-collection paths / bespoke mineral loops.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Candidate shared hook if the dispatch
  belongs on the scene core instead of the collection layer.
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-mineral-chime.yaml` — New recipe (seed
  32292; document the level target and the rate/aliasing rationale).
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — New cue entry.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-mineral-chime.32292.wav`,
  `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — Baked asset + checksum
  (`npm run build-audio`).
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`
  (§7.3 cue table, §4.5 collection bullet) — Documentation rows/rationale.
- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` (new), `src/audio/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`, `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Coverage for the state
  machine, cue wiring and the defined-once/parity guards.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-19)

Decomposed into six child items, **test-first and dependency-ordered**. Each
child carries its own acceptance criteria, minimal implementation slice and
key files; this block is the traceability index only.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|-----------|
| 1 | Mineral chime escalation spec tests (AH-0MWNMRBO4000T5F8) | task | — |
| 2 | Pure mineral chime escalation state machine (AH-0MWNMRCEW006N0EH) | task | 1 |
| 3 | Baked aihell-mineral-chime cue (AH-0MWNMRD6I002CCVT) | task | 2 |
| 4 | One shared chime dispatch on every player pickup (AH-0MWNMRDY60005Z4K) | feature | 2, 3 |
| 5 | Document the mineral pickup chime (AH-0MWNMRER0009385Y) | docs | 4 |
| 6 | Verify the mineral chime end to end (AH-0MWNMRFJ9004F66R) | task | 4, 5 |

**Phase plan — each phase is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs/infra):**

1. **Pitch rule** (items 1→2): the pure state machine and the spec that drives
   it — behaviour, unit tests and documented constants land together.
2. **Audible cue** (item 3): recipe → deterministic bake → committed WAV +
   checksum → manifest entry → `effects.ts` export → contract and peak tests.
3. **Gameplay wiring** (item 4): the single shared core dispatch plus the six
   collection paths and the run-reset/teardown resets, with the parity,
   absorption-silence, defined-once and dense-burst tests.
4. **Docs** (item 5): cue-mapping tables, GDD §7.3/§4.5, README, code comments,
   pinned by a docs assertion test.
5. **Verification gate** (item 6): `build-audio:verify`, the full suite via the
   test skill, the production build and the ear check.

**Between phases:** re-read the next child's description and update it with
anything the previous slice learned (final constant names, cue name, test seams
to extend) before starting it. The children are the implementable
specification; this item's ACs are the coverage map.

**Architecture decision (recorded, no producer input needed):** the single
dispatch point is a shared `CombatCoreScene` hook, **not** the Phaser-free
`mineralLayer.collectMinerals`. Rationale, consequences and the parity argument
are in the wiring child's "Architecture decision" section.

**Plan changelog:** 2026-11-19 — first decomposition: 6 children created (issue
types task/task/task/feature/docs/task), 7 dependency edges wired, six automated
review stages run, AC coverage review = `proceed`. No prior plan block existed.

## Related work

- **Mystery UFO feel layer** (AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6) and its cue bake
  (AH-0MVSAJMLL00835T8) — shipped `aihell-mineral-tinkle` for the UFO **spill**,
  the closest existing mineral audio and the reason a pickup cue must not alias
  it.
- **Countdown count SFX cue via the ToneForge pipeline** (AH-0MV55OA93008OUL1)
  — the precedent for rising pitch through playback `rate` (`COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES`,
  `countdownTickRate`) and for adding a recipe/manifest/checksum/docs in one
  change.
- **Wire non-combat pickup audio into `GymPowerUps._collectDrop()`**
  (AH-0MTGS94T9007TAAC), **PlayScene: add per-type power-up pickup activation
  audio** (AH-0MU8QVX9G008P8ML) and **Pop SFX** (AH-0MUBYSNGU0051XVO) — the
  established pickup-feedback convention this item extends to minerals.
- **Mineral collectable entity and constants** (AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT), **Shared
  mineral layer** (AH-0MUII3DHM008L7JF) and **Red mineral deposits**
  (AH-0MVJ79739008396I) — the collection/value semantics the chime must not
  change (a deposit pays one chime, one 10-value pickup).
- **SFX mix** (AH-0MVZVMZOQ00076QF) — the family-trim mechanism
  (`*_VOLUME_SCALE` named constants) that a quieter chime should follow rather
  than re-baking assets.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake ran from an **automated downtime dispatch** (no interactive producer
present), so the three feel-tuning choices below could not be answered in
session. Each records the **recommended option** that the brief has adopted as
its documented default, the evidence behind it, and an **OPEN QUESTION** marker
so the producer can override any of them without re-planning (each is a single
named constant / one-line recipe change).

- **Q1 — Pitch ladder and ceiling:** how far should the chime rise, and in what
  steps? (a) chromatic, +1 semitone per pickup, capped at +7; (b) one **A-minor
  scale degree** per pickup, capped at an octave; (c) +2 semitones per pickup.
  **Recommended: (b)** — the game's written tonal language is A minor (GDD §7.3
  A-minor conformance, docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md), and one scale step reads
  as "slightly" rising without going shrill on a long streak. **OPEN QUESTION
  (provisional default: b; `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]`).**
  Source: no interactive answer — auto-dispatched intake; precedent evidence:
  `playCountdownTickSound` / `COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES` (AH-0MV55OA93008OUL1) in
  `src/audio/effects.ts`.
- **Q2 — Reset gap ("a short period"):** how long without a pickup before the
  pitch returns to base? (a) 1.0 s; (b) 1.5 s; (c) 2.0 s. **Recommended: (b)** —
  long enough to bridge sweeping a scattered pair (≈0.3–0.8 s apart) and short
  enough that a fresh pass starts clean. **OPEN QUESTION (provisional default:
  b; `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS = 1500`, measured on game time).** Source: no
  interactive answer — auto-dispatched intake.
- **Q3 — Cue identity:** add a dedicated baked recipe or reuse the existing
  `aihell-mineral-tinkle` at a rising rate? (a) new `aihell-mineral-chime`
  recipe (seed 32292); (b) reuse `aihell-mineral-tinkle`. **Recommended: (a)** —
  the existing tinkle is the Mystery UFO **spill** cue and fires at the moment
  the spilled minerals appear, so reusing it would make a pickup
  indistinguishable from a spill. Reuse also would not let the pickup be
  gain-staged independently. **OPEN QUESTION (provisional default: a).**
  Evidence: `playMineralTinkleSound` + GDD §4.5 / `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
  row for `aihell-mineral-tinkle`; no suitable unused pickup chime exists in the
  manifest (checked `playPowerUpCollectPopSound`, `playPowerUpCollectSound` —
  both are power-up-specific).
- **Q4 — Granularity:** does a red 10-value deposit (or a pair collected in one
  frame) chime once or ten/twice? **Decided by reading the brief**: one chime
  per *collected mineral entity* (so a deposit is one chime, a pair is two
  rising chimes), and enemy absorption is silent — the request is about the
  player collecting. Recorded here for traceability; producer may override.

**Duplicate-work check:** `wl search` for `mineral`, `tinkle`, `chime`,
`collect sound` and `audio cue` returned no open or completed item covering a
mineral-pickup chime; the closest is the Mystery UFO feel layer, which
**deliberately** voices only the spill. Comment recorded on the work item.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU8QVX9G008P8ML** – PlayScene: add per-type power-up pickup activation audio (completed)
- **AH-0MTGS9DZ6001IFJR** – Update GDD audio design section and code comments (completed)
- **AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU** – Player has no audio (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muii3dhm008l7jf, 0mvi4j8r4002wtt6, 0mvj79739008396i, 0mvzvmzoq00076qf, absorption (+514 more)
- `README.md` — matched: absorption, acceptance, accepted, activation, add (+471 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mvzvmzoq00076qf, absorption, acceptance, activation, add (+427 more)

### Plan-session note (2026-11-19, automated dispatch)

The plan session also ran with no interactive producer, so no new questions were
asked: the four entries above already encode the only producer decisions this
work needs, each behind a provisional default. The plan treats them as settled
assumptions and every one is a single named constant or a one-line recipe
change, so a producer override at review needs no re-planning:

- `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]` (Q1, ladder + octave cap);
- `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS = 1500` game-time (Q2);
- a dedicated `aihell-mineral-chime` recipe at seed 32292 (Q3);
- one chime per collected mineral entity, silent on enemy absorption (Q4).

One engineering choice was decided in-session and recorded on the wiring child
rather than asked: the dispatch lives in the shared `CombatCoreScene` hook
(all six collection paths extend it and it owns the scene clock and the
reset/teardown seams), not in the Phaser-free `mineralLayer`.

# Mineral chime escalation spec tests

Part of **Chime whenever a mineral is collected** (AH-0MWNHEIV90047V91) — the
test-first slice for the pure pitch-escalation state machine. These tests are
written before the module exists (red) so the machine's behaviour is pinned
independently of any scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` exists and covers, driving the machine with
  an **injected clock only** (no wall clock, no Phaser, no audio mocking):
  - the first pickup sounds the **base** step (0 semitones → playback rate
    1.0);
  - each further pickup inside `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` advances exactly
    one ladder degree up `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES` (`[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]`);
  - a long streak **clamps** at the last ladder degree — it never exceeds one
    octave and never returns `undefined`/`NaN`/a negative rate for any
    non-negative pickup count;
  - a gap of exactly `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` resets to base, and a gap
    1 ms shorter does not (the boundary is pinned in both directions);
  - the explicit reset seam returns the streak to base;
  - two sequential streaks after a reset are independent (no shared/leaked
    state).
- Expected rates are computed as `2 ** (semitones / 12)` from the exported
  ladder, so the ladder (not a copy of its numbers) is the contract.
- The spec imports only the pure module — no `playCue` spy, no scene import.
- The cases fail before the implementation exists and pass afterwards with no
  weakening of their assertions (red → green).
- The pitch-escalation state machine is pure and unit-tested with an injected clock: rise per pickup, cap, reset after the gap, and reset on run restart / scene teardown; a dense burst is bounded and does not shotgun-stack chimes beyond the shared voice limiter (this item pins the pure part — the run-restart/teardown reset and the dense-burst bound are asserted by the wiring item).

## Minimal implementation

1. Create `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts`, one `describe` per rule above.
2. Hold a mutable `clock` variable in the test and pass it to every call —
   never `Date.now()`.
3. Keep the file Phaser-free.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` — new spec (the module does not exist yet).

## Dependencies

Blocks **Pure mineral chime escalation state machine** (test-first).

# Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading

## Problem statement

The target-aware config (hangar) screen marks **every** weapon row with its
matchup against the chosen hex's boss — green `▲ EFFECTIVE` when the boss is
weak to it, red `▼ RESISTED` when the boss resists it — but it does so even for
rows the player **cannot act on**: weapons they cannot buy (short of salvage,
`NEED 40 min`, or still ring-gated, `RING 2`) and owned weapons whose pricey
upgrade they cannot afford. Highlighting a recommendation the player cannot act
on reads as "buy this", so the intel lies about what is available right now.

## Users

- **The new player with no salvage** — "I have 0 minerals; every weapon row is
  lit up as if I could bring or upgrade it. Only light up what I can act on."
- **The ring-1 player** — "A ring-2 weapon is shown in bright red as if my
  loadout choice matters; I cannot buy it yet."
- **The accessibility-minded player** — "The matchup must still be readable
  without colour wherever it is shown." (Repo CVD policy: never colour-only.)
- **The producer/maintainer** — "One shared model decides the highlight, so the
  game and `GymHangar` cannot drift and no scene owns a second rule."

Example user stories:

- As a player with no salvage, I still read the boss's intel and the `▲`/`▼`
  verdicts, but only the rows I could actually buy or upgrade are highlighted.
- As a player with enough salvage for one weapon, that row is highlighted and
  the ones I cannot afford render as ordinary disabled rows.
- As a player equipping a weapon I already own, the `LOADOUT` column keeps its
  full matchup highlight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Rows with no available action are not highlighted.** In the hangar screen's
  unlock tree, a `weapon` row the player cannot act on right now — purchase
  states `unaffordable` (`NEED … min`) and `gated` (`RING n`), and upgrade
  states `upgrade-unaffordable` and `capped` (`MAX`) — renders with **no**
  strong/weak colour and **no** strong/weak background tint, keeping the
  ordinary row styling (muted colour, its price/shortfall or `MAX` intact).
- **Rows with an available action keep their highlight.** A `weapon` row whose
  own action is available — a `buyable` purchase row and an `upgradable` upgrade
  row — keeps exactly today's behaviour: `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` marker,
  strong/weak colour and tint.
- **The `LOADOUT` column is unchanged.** Every starting-weapon row in the
  deployment selector (owned weapons, always toggleable) keeps its marker,
  colour and tint, because equipping/unequipping it is always available.
- **The marker stays on every weapon row.** The `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED`
  text tag is appended wherever the weapon has a strong/weak verdict, including
  the non-highlighted rows, so the intel stays readable without colour (CVD
  policy) and only the colour/tint follows affordability.
- **The shared model decides, and the gym agrees.** Whether a row is highlighted
  is published by `buildHangarScreenModel`/`buildHangarUnlockRows` (data beside
  the existing `matchup` verdict), never derived from the render-time
  interactive/actionable flag, so the read-only `GymHangar` render shows exactly
  the game's highlight; a test asserts the model, the game render and the gym
  render agree for the same payload.
- **Automated tests cover the matrix.** Model-level and render-level tests for
  `buyable` + strong/weak, `unaffordable` + strong/weak, `gated` + strong/weak,
  `upgradable` + strong/weak, `upgrade-unaffordable` + strong/weak, `capped` +
  strong/weak, and a `LOADOUT` row of each strength; plus a test that a
  non-highlighted row keeps its marker, price and shortfall.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, GDD §8.2, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A player choosing a loadout only sees the boss-counter highlight on weapon rows
they can actually act on right now, while the `▲`/`▼` intel stays readable
everywhere — so the green/red marks are a promise the player can keep.

## Assumptions (documented; producer may override at review)

- **A1 — "Cannot buy" = `unaffordable` or `gated`.** Both mean the purchase
  cannot happen now (`canBuy` returns `unaffordable` for a salvage shortfall and
  `gated` for a not-yet-reached ring), so neither row is highlighted.
  (Producer Q2 = (a).)
- **A2 — Marker retained, colour suppressed.** A non-highlighted row keeps the
  `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` text marker and only loses the colour and backing
  tint, so it reads as a normal row whose matchup is still legible without
  colour. (Producer Q1 = (a).)
- **A3 — LOADOUT yes, upgrade tree no.** The `LOADOUT` equipped/unequipped column
  keeps its highlight for owned weapons (the action is always available); in the
  main upgrade/purchase tree the highlight follows the row's **own** action, so
  an owned weapon whose upgrade is `upgrade-unaffordable` (or `capped`) is **not**
  highlighted, while an `upgradable` one is. (Producer Q3: "equipped/unequipped
  column yes, main selection for upgrade no".)
- **A3.1 — `capped` (`MAX`) counts as "no available action".** A maxed row has
  nothing left to buy, so it is not highlighted; the player still sees the
  weapon highlighted in the `LOADOUT` column. Recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in
  case the producer would rather a maxed weapon keep its highlight.
- **A4 — Display only.** Prices, ring gating, ownership, the matchup resolver
  (`src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`) and the `TARGET INTEL` block are
  unchanged; this item changes only which rows are highlighted (parent
  AH-0MWMRWCY2001HWGR assumption A7 stands — the mechanical matchup is
  AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ).
- **A5 — No new persistence.** No payload schema or store change.
- **A6 — Existing fixtures must be re-baselined.** Today's matchup tests use a
  0-salvage payload whose weapons are all **owned**, so those rows are
  `upgrade-unaffordable` and (per A3) lose their colour: the rendered-colour
  assertion for `buy:spread` in `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` must change, and
  a fixture with salvage must be added to keep a positive highlight assertion.
  The `matchup` verdict and the `▲`/`▼` labels survive unchanged.

## Constraints

- **Model, not render, decides the highlight.** `renderHangarScreen` reports
  every row non-actionable in a read-only render (the gym), so keying the
  highlight off `actionable` would silently blank every mark in `GymHangar` and
  break gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **One shared code path.** No second matchup/highlight rule in `HangarScene`,
  `GymHangar` or the map; the pure model plus the one renderer stay the only
  place the rule lives.
- **Never colour-only.** The glyph tag stays on every weapon row with a verdict;
  a suppressed row must remain an ordinary readable row (price + shortfall, or
  `MAX`), not an unexplained blank.
- **No layout change.** No new rows or sections; `hangarLowestRowY` /
  bottom-row geometry are untouched.
- **No economy change.** The affordability verdicts are the economy's own
  (`canBuy`, `costToUpgrade`); this item only reads them.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Auto-buying the counter weapon, hiding non-weapon rows,
  dimming the `TARGET INTEL` block, or changing prices/gating are out of scope —
  record them as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Risks

- **Gym-parity regression (high).** Deriving the highlight from render-time
  `actionable` would blank every mark in the read-only gym; mitigated by
  publishing the decision in the model and asserting it in `GymHangar.test.ts`.
- **Test re-baseline churn (medium, expected).** Two existing tests assert a
  colour on rows that are now non-highlighted (0-salvage owned weapons); they
  must be updated deliberately, with a salvage-bearing fixture keeping the
  positive case covered.
- **Player surprise on `MAX` rows (low).** A maxed weapon loses its tree
  highlight (A3.1); the `LOADOUT` column still shows it, so the intel is never
  lost — flagged as an OPEN QUESTION for override.
- **Fixture blindness (medium).** No current fixture has a weapon it cannot
  afford, which is why this slipped through the parent epic; the new matrix adds
  one deliberately.

## Existing state

- `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) resolves a
  `matchup` for **every** `weapon`-kind row, regardless of the economy verdict,
  via `resolveBossMatchup(entry.weaponId, target)`, and appends the marker with
  `withMatchupMarker(...)`.
- The renderer's `rowColour(actionable, matchup)` returns
  `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` / `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR` **before** consulting
  `actionable`, and `rowBackground(matchup)` tints the row — so an
  `unaffordable` (`NEED 40 min`), `gated` (`RING 2`), `upgrade-unaffordable` or
  `capped` (`MAX`) weapon row renders in the bright highlight colour with its
  tint even though nothing can be bought on it.
- `HangarUnlockRow.state` already carries the economy verdict (`owned`, `gated`,
  `unaffordable`, `buyable`, `upgradable`, `upgrade-unaffordable`, `capped`);
  the information needed is present, it is simply not consulted by the highlight.
- `HangarWeaponOption` rows are built from `unlockedWeapons` only (owned, always
  actionable), so the `LOADOUT` column is already always highlighted — and per
  A3 keeps that.
- `GymHangar` renders the same model with **no handlers**, so every rendered row
  reports `actionable: false` while showing the game's colours; the highlight
  must therefore be model data (`src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` pins parity).
- Tests today: `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` ("marks every weapon row …",
  "renders the intel section, the glyph tags and the matchup colours") and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` ("renders the known target intel and ▲/▼
  matchup marks read-only") assert the marker/colour on rows from a 0-salvage
  fixture whose weapons are all **owned** (upgrade rows).

## Desired change

- **Publish the highlight decision in the model.** Beside `matchup`, expose
  whether that verdict should be *highlighted* for this row — true when the row's
  own action is available (`buyable` purchase, `upgradable` upgrade, and every
  `LOADOUT` weapon option), false for `unaffordable`, `gated`,
  `upgrade-unaffordable` and `capped` unlock rows — derived from the economy
  verdicts already on the row (no new economy rule).
- **Render from that flag.** `rowColour` / `rowBackground` consult the highlight
  flag (never the render-time `actionable` flag), so a non-highlighted row falls
  back to the existing row styling while highlighted rows keep today's colour
  and tint. The `▲`/`▼` marker keeps being appended unconditionally by
  `withMatchupMarker`.
- **Cover the matrix with tests** in `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` (model +
  render, with a salvage-bearing fixture for the positive cases) and the gym
  parity case in `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`.
- **Update the docs** that promise the current unconditional marking
  (`README.md` hangar/hex-map paragraphs, GDD §8.2, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`,
  `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *Known-ahead intel*).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — the per-row highlight flag in
  `buildHangarUnlockRows` / `buildHangarWeaponOptions`, and the colour/tint
  decision in `rowColour` / `rowBackground`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` — model + render tests for the `buyable` /
  `unaffordable` / `gated` / `upgradable` / `upgrade-unaffordable` / `capped` /
  `LOADOUT` matrix, and the re-baselined colour assertion.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — parity: the gym renders the same
  suppressed highlight for a non-actionable row.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — record the highlight rule for `GymHangar`.
- `README.md` — the hangar and hex-map paragraphs that describe the marks.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2 config-screen intel paragraph.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — § *Known-ahead intel* (the config screen
  marks "each weapon row").

## Related work

- **AH-0MWMRWCY2001HWGR — When starting a Hex War battle show the ship config
  screen** (completed): the parent epic that introduced the target-aware config
  screen and the unconditional marks this item narrows (children
  AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y pure resolver, AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN model/render,
  AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 gym parity + docs).
- **AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y — Weapon-vs-boss matchup resolver** (completed): the
  pure `resolveBossMatchup` verdict this item presents differently — unchanged.
- **AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat**
  (open): owns the mechanical matchup; this item stays display-only.
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY — Post-MVP Hangar War: hull upgrade bays as a reward
  axis** (open): future economy surface; unaffected but must not inherit a
  misleading highlight.
- Automated find-related report also surfaced `README.md`, `docs/Game Design
  Document.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` as keyword matches
  (documentation touch points).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Asked in-session of the producer; the item was flagged `needsProducerReview`
while the questions were open and is released on their answers.

- **Q1 — Should a non-highlighted weapon row also lose the ▲/▼ text marker, or
  only the colour/tint?**
  Options: (a) keep the marker, suppress colour + tint; (b) hide marker and
  colour together; (c) keep the marker in the muted colour with a `· LOCKED`
  suffix.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the item asks for colour to follow affordability, and
  keeping the tag preserves the CVD-safe intel the parent epic required.
  **Answer (producer): (a)** — keep the marker, suppress only the colour and the
  backing tint. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session. Now recorded as
  AC4 and assumption A2.
- **Q2 — Does "not able to buy" include ring-gated rows (`RING 2`), or only rows
  short of salvage (`NEED … min`)?**
  Options: (a) both; (b) only `unaffordable`.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a gated row is equally unbuyable now, and `canBuy`
  already reports it as `gated` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:528`).
  **Answer (producer): (a)** — both, any row the player cannot buy now. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session. Now recorded as AC1 and assumption A1.
- **Q3 — Do owned weapons keep their highlight when their *upgrade* is
  unaffordable or capped?**
  Options: (a) yes — ownership makes the weapon usable now; (b) no — mute the
  row.
  **Recommended:** (a) (ownership makes the weapon usable now).
  **Answer (producer): split — "if you mean in the equipped/unequipped column
  yes, if you mean in the main selection for upgrade, no."** So the `LOADOUT`
  equipped/unequipped column keeps the highlight for owned weapons, while the
  main purchase/upgrade tree highlights only rows whose own action is available
  (`buyable` / `upgradable`). Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session.
  This **supersedes** the earlier recommended (a) and is recorded as AC3/AC2 and
  assumption A3. Research: the 0-salvage fixtures make those tree rows
  `upgrade-unaffordable`, so their rendered-colour assertions must be
  re-baselined (assumption A6).
- **Q3.1 — Does a `capped` (`MAX`) row count as "no available action"?**
  **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION (producer) — drafted as "yes, not highlighted"
  (A3.1), because the row has nothing left to buy while the `LOADOUT` column
  still shows the weapon's matchup highlighted. Overriding this only changes one
  state in the highlight predicate.
data.title: Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Hangar: make owned power-ups installable in the deployment loadout

## Problem statement

A deployment currently installs **every** owned level-bearing power-up
automatically: `buildHangarDeployment` copies the whole
`hangarPermanentLevels(hangar).powerUps` list into `powerUpLevels`, and
`applyHangarWarDeployment` grants all of it (trimmed only by the shared
six-slot cap). Because `HangarLoadout` holds just `startingWeapons` and
`modifiers`, the hangar screen has no way to express *which* power-ups a
deployment installs — so a fleet that owns more counted kinds than the cap has
its build silently chosen for it by catalogue order.

## Users

- **Player preparing a deployment** — wants to curate the build for the
  upcoming hex.
  - *As a player, when I own five power-ups but want two of them installed
    alongside four weapons, I want to pick those two, so the six slots go to
    the kit I chose rather than to whatever I bought first.*
  - *As a player, I want the loadout I see on the hangar screen to be exactly
    the kit the run launches with, so I am not surprised mid-battle.*
- **Player with an existing save** — wants to keep flying what they flew
  before this feature, without re-fitting anything.
- **Designer / maintainer** — wants one selection model consumed by the game
  and `GymHangar`, reusing the shipped slot cap and permanent-grant seams, with
  no second power-up budget and no schema bump.

## Existing state (verified in code)

- **The model has no power-up slot.** `HangarLoadout`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is `{ startingWeapons: string[]; modifiers:
  string[] }`; `DeployedShip` mirrors the same three fields (hull +
  `startingWeapons` + `modifiers`).
- **Every owned level-bearing power-up is auto-installed.**
  `buildHangarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) maps
  `levels.powerUps` wholesale into `powerUpLevels`;
  `applyHangarWarDeployment` then caps the combined weapons+power-up list
  through `capDropIdsToSlotPool` and grants each row through
  `grantPermanentPowerUp` / `grantPermanentWeapon` (one grant per level), so
  the leftover rows are dropped by cap order, not by player choice.
- **Persistence is field-presence tolerant.** `parseLoadout`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) rebuilds the loadout from known
  fields only and defaults a missing/wrong-shaped loadout to empty; the payload
  is versioned (`version: 1`) but the GDD documents "migration is decided by
  field presence", so a new optional field needs no version bump.
- **Resolution filters to owned entries.** `resolveActiveLoadout` /
  `equipLoadout` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) drop catalogue-unknown
  or unowned ids, so a corrupt save can never install an unowned power-up.
- **The selector is weapons + modifiers only.** `buildHangarScreenModel`
  produces `HangarWeaponOption` and `HangarModifierOption` rows
  (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) with `toggleHangarWeapon` /
  `toggleHangarModifier` handlers; `GymHangar` renders the same model
  read-only, so any new row appears in both.
- **Consumption spends hull, weapons and modifiers only.**
  `consumeDeployedShip` removes the flown hull, starting weapons and modifiers
  (plus their bought level rows) and resets `activeLoadout` to
  `{ startingWeapons: [], modifiers: [] }`; power-up level rows are **not**
  spent today.

## Desired change

- Add an optional power-up selection to `HangarLoadout` and mirror it on
  `DeployedShip`, `parseLoadout` and `equipLoadout` — no schema/version bump.
- Render owned, level-bearing power-ups as toggleable rows in the hangar
  deployment selector, with the same equipped/unequipped affordance as weapons,
  through a `toggleHangarPowerUp` handler that routes through `equipLoadout`.
- Resolve the selection in `buildHangarDeployment` (only the selected rows reach
  `powerUpLevels`) and keep `applyHangarWarDeployment`'s grant loop and
  six-slot trim as the single grant seam.
- Make the displayed loadout equal the granted loadout: apply the same
  `capDropIdsToSlotPool` trimming in the screen model and render
  non-admitted rows as blocked/non-actionable rather than silently differing.
- Expose the selection to the auto-loadout selector (parent
  AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD) so its "balanced variety" fill can include power-ups.
- Keep gym↔game parity: `GymHangar` renders the same model read-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Owned level-bearing power-ups appear as toggleable rows in the hangar deployment selector, with a clear equipped/unequipped state.
- [ ] A deployment grants exactly the selected power-ups (and their permanent levels); deselected power-ups are not granted.
- [ ] The combined selected weapons + power-ups respect the shared six-slot cap, and the displayed loadout matches what the run grants.
- [ ] A save written before this feature (no selection field) deploys with the existing behaviour, with no schema bump.
- [ ] The auto-loadout selector can select power-ups once this lands.
- [ ] The game and `GymHangar` render from the same model.
- [ ] Automated tests cover the model, the resolve/grant path and the gym parity (including a red-first test for the new selection field and its default).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the GDD (§8.1 payload, six-slot loadout), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shipped slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` via `capDropIdsToSlotPool`)
  and the shipped permanent-grant seams; no second power-up budget.
- Additive persisted field only, in the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`
  pattern; empty/absent must stay legal and must not throw.
- Do not change power-up balance, the six-slot semantics, or which kinds carry
  a permanent level (consumables and field-pickup-only kinds stay unselectable).
- Installation is a loadout choice, not a new spend: the existing
  `consumeDeployedShip` rule is unchanged — a flown hull, starting weapons and
  modifiers are spent, and installed power-ups are not.
- No Phaser or storage access in the pure core/deployment modules; `GymHangar`
  stays read-only (no purchase/toggle handlers).

## Assumptions and decisions

- **A1 — Tri-state field.** The new field is optional: `undefined` (a save
  written before this feature) means "not chosen yet" and keeps today's
  behaviour (every owned level-bearing power-up installs); `[]` means a
  deliberate empty selection and installs none; a populated list installs
  exactly those ids. This keeps AC4 satisfiable while letting a player empty
  the selection — the same shape `HangarLoadout.startingWeapons` already has.
- **A2 — Selection is persisted in `activeLoadout`,** not as a parallel
  top-level field, so `resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` remain the single
  ownership filter and a corrupt save cannot install an unowned power-up.
- **A3 — Display equals grant via the shared cap predicate,** applied in the
  model as well as at grant time; grant-time trimming stays as the backstop for
  launch data from another build.
- **A4 — Installed power-ups are not consumed** (see Constraints). Power-up
  levels are permanent purchases; spending them per sortie would be an economy
  change this item explicitly excludes.
- **A5 — No producer questions were needed:** the seed description, the parent
  item (AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD) and the code above resolve every open point; the
  four decisions above are documented for confirmation at review.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Display/grant drift** (the reason AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX existed): mitigated by
  A3 — one predicate (`capDropIdsToSlotPool`) drives both the model and the
  grant, with a test asserting the two sets are equal.
- **Retro-fitting existing saves:** a naive default of "select nothing" would
  strip power-ups from every existing player's next sortie. Mitigated by A1
  (`undefined` ⇒ today's behaviour) and a test on a pre-feature payload.
- **Consumption regression:** adding a field to `DeployedShip` /
  `HangarLoadout` touches `consumeDeployedShip`'s reset shape. Mitigated by
  keeping the consumption rule unchanged (A4) and asserting the reset keeps the
  new field well-formed.
- **Row-count/layout pressure:** the right column already lays out weapons and
  modifiers by index (`hangarRightColumnLayout`); extra rows change nothing
  semantically but must not overlap. Mitigated by layout tests at a full
  catalogue.
- **Scope creep:** boss-matchup colouring for power-ups, auto-fit heuristics,
  and per-battle power-up spending belong to other items (parent
  AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD / AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY). They are recorded there, not
  pulled into this one.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarLoadout` and `DeployedShip` gain the optional power-up selection.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` filter the selection to owned, level-bearing ids; `consumeDeployedShip` reset shape stays valid.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `parseLoadout` reads the field with presence-based defaulting (A1), no version bump.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — `buildHangarDeployment` resolves only the selected rows into `powerUpLevels`; `applyHangarWarDeployment` cap/grant seam unchanged.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `HangarPowerUpOption` rows, cap-aware `buildHangarScreenModel`, `toggleHangarPowerUp`, keyboard/focus wiring and layout.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — the shared `capDropIdsToSlotPool` / level-bearing-kind predicates the model and the grant both use (no new budget).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — parity: renders the same read-only model.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` (or nearest equivalents), `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts` — red-first coverage of the model, the resolve/grant path and the parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.1 payload field and the six-slot loadout section.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the `GymHangar` row (guarded by `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`).
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — Candidate D loadout description, if it enumerates loadout fields.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD** — Automatically select strong weapons (parent; this
  item was spawned from producer decision Q2 = A to make power-ups
  installable, because the auto-fill can only choose from an installable set).
- **AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX** — Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap (completed;
  established the shared cap predicate used here).
- **AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9** — Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots
  (completed; established the `applyHangarWarDeployment` registry grant seam).
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — default-empty loadout decision (an empty selection
  is a legal deployment — the precedent for A1's `[]` case).
- **AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH** — Persist permanent levels through store and grant
  seam (completed; the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` pattern this field
  follows).
- **AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ** — Model the per-ring deployment loadout (completed).
- **AH-0MWKXPO5A007R5RB** — Power-up unlock-tree kind, owned set and authored
  entry (completed; the owned-set source the selector reads).
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY** — Post-MVP Hangar War: hull upgrade bays as a reward
  axis (open; adjacent loadout work, not blocking).

## Impact

Players can curate which owned power-ups a deployment installs, so the loadout
they see is the loadout they fly.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Does the new selection default to "all owned" or "none" for existing
saves?**
Answer (derived from the seed brief, no producer round needed): **all owned**,
via an optional (`undefined`) field. Evidence: the seed description's "preserve
the current default behaviour for saves without the new field"; current
behaviour verified in `buildHangarDeployment` (`powerUpLevels:
levels.powerUps.map(...)`) and `applyHangarWarDeployment`. Research: a "none"
default would silently strip power-ups from every live save on the next
sortie, contradicting the explicit constraint. Related:
AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (an *explicit* empty selection is still legal). Decision
recorded as assumption A1.

**Q2 — Does installing a power-up mean the fleet spends it on battle end, like
a weapon?**
Answer: **No.** `consumeDeployedShip` spends the hull, starting weapons and
modifiers (and their bought level rows) and never power-up level rows; power-ups
are permanent level purchases and the item's constraints forbid changing
power-up balance or economy. Decision recorded as assumption A4; the
consumption rule is left byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Q3 — Where does the selection live: a new top-level hangar field or inside
`HangarLoadout`?**
Answer: **inside `HangarLoadout`** (plus `DeployedShip`). Rationale:
`resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` are the shipped ownership filters, so a
parallel field would need a second filter and could install an unowned
power-up. Decision recorded as assumption A2.

**Q4 — Does the six-slot cap get enforced at selection time, at grant time, or
both?**
Answer: **both, from one predicate.** `applyHangarWarDeployment` already trims
weapons+power-ups through `capDropIdsToSlotPool`
(AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX); the screen model must apply the same predicate so the
displayed loadout equals the granted loadout (AC3), with grant-time trimming
kept as the backstop for launch data from another build. Decision recorded as
assumption A3.

**Q5 — Which power-up kinds are selectable?**
Answer: only **level-bearing** kinds — the same set `powerUpLevels` already
carries. Consumables (charge pools) and field-pickup-only kinds carry no
permanent level and are excluded, per the existing doc comment on
`HangarWarDeployment.powerUpLevels` (AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH AC5). No new rule.

**Plan revision note (2026-11-20):** re-read during planning; Q1–Q5 and
assumptions A1–A5 are unchanged and were reused without a new producer
round. No question was re-asked and no entry was duplicated.

**Open questions for the producer:** none. Items Q1–Q5 are answered from the
seed brief, the parent item and the shipped code, and are recorded as
assumptions A1–A5 for confirmation at review.

## Plan

Decomposed into eight child features in dependency order — one red-first
contract suite, five implementation slices (model → deployment → screen model →
scene wiring, plus the auto-loadout seam), the gym-parity slice and a docs/suite
closure. Each child is a vertical slice carrying its own tests and docs touch.

| # | Child | Type | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Red-first tests: power-up loadout selection (AH-0MWOWO5WX005HKWY) | task | — |
| 2 | Power-up loadout field and persistence (AH-0MWOWO6IJ006X5CC) | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Deployment grants only selected power-ups (AH-0MWOWO753006K7NJ) | feature | 2 |
| 4 | Hangar model: power-up selector rows (AH-0MWOWO7VY005BOZA) | feature | 3 |
| 5 | Hangar scene: power-up wiring and layout (AH-0MWOWO8KG006K0WJ) | feature | 4 |
| 6 | GymHangar parity for power-up rows (AH-0MWOWO9AS003FWJI) | feature | 4 |
| 7 | Auto-loadout power-up selection seam (AH-0MWOWO9X2005PB1G) | feature | 2, 3 |
| 8 | Power-up loadout docs and suite gate (AH-0MWOWOAJL005RN6M) | docs | 5, 6 |

**Vertical-slice phasing:** children 2–6 each cut through the layers they touch
(pure model + store + tests; deployment + tests; screen model + tests; scene +
layout/focus tests; gym + parity docs + guard). Between phases the next child's
description is reviewed and updated before implementation. Docs that describe
final behaviour (GDD, candidate doc, module JSDoc) land last in child 8 rather
than being scattered.

**Reuse, not reinvention:** the shared cap predicate (`capDropIdsToSlotPool`,
AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX), the permanent-grant seam (`applyHangarWarDeployment`,
AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9), the ownership filter (`ownedEntriesOf` /
`resolveActiveLoadout`) and the payload's presence-based migration are consumed
unchanged — no second power-up budget, no schema bump.

**Sequencing note for child 5:** the right column currently holds hulls,
weapons, modifiers and the compact saved-build block, and no viewport guard
exists yet; child 5 owns the full-catalogue layout test and may reduce the row
step (an allowed fix inside that child) if the new section overflows.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-20T11:40Z — plan run (downtime dispatch): read the intake brief and
  verified the shipped seams in `types.ts`, `hangarWarStore.ts`,
  `hangarEconomy.ts`, `hangarDeployment.ts`, `hangarScreen.ts`, `slots.ts` and
  `GymHangar.ts`; created 8 child features in test-first dependency order;
  wired 9 blocking edges; ran the six automated review stages and the AC
  coverage review (100% of the parent's criteria covered by children, no
  auto-created children needed). No new producer questions: the intake's
  Appendix Q1–Q5 answers were reused rather than re-asked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test module (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarAutoLoadout.test.ts`) pins the selector API over an injectable payload, catalogue and target definition — no scene, Phaser or DOM import.
- [ ] Tests assert an owned weapon named in the target hex's `weaknesses` (`resolveBossMatchup === 'strong'`) is always selected when the loadout is empty.

data.description:
## Summary

Add the one pure, boss-aware auto-loadout selector that the game and `GymHangar` consume, turning the F1 red contract green (parent AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD, AC1/AC2/AC3/AC7/AC8).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new pure module (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarAutoLoadout.ts`) exports a selector that, given a payload, a target hex definition and a catalogue, returns the suggested `startingWeapons` plus its slot accounting — no Phaser/DOM/scene import, no mutation, no throwing.
- [ ] Every owned weapon whose `resolveBossMatchup(weaponId, target) === 'strong'` is included, subject only to the variety cap and the slot budget.
- [ ] A `weak` weapon is never selected by any branch (explicit list or fill step).
- [ ] The variety cap admits at most one weapon per behaviour family, reusing the shipped descriptors (`aoe`/`bounce`/`hitscan`/`splits`/`orbit`, plain projectile) — no new taxonomy.
- [ ] The preference order is: `strong`, then at least one defensive power-up the deployment auto-grants, then highest permanent level, filling toward `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
- [ ] Defensiveness reuses the shipped classification (`UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS[id] === 'armour'`) rather than a new defensive list.
- [ ] Slot budgeting subtracts the owned power-up levels `buildHangarDeployment` will grant (`hangarPermanentLevels(...).powerUps`), so the selection plus grants never exceeds `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
- [ ] Deterministic and idempotent: no wall clock, no unseeded randomness; canonical ordering by catalogue order.
- [ ] The F1 contract tests pass unchanged.

- [ ] **Parent AC1 traced:** **AC1 — Strong weapons are auto-equipped when the loadout is empty.** Opening the hangar screen ahead of a battle with an empty loadout on a hex whose authored `weaknesses` name an owned weapon selects that weapon in `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` (via `resolveBossMatchup === 'strong'`); pinned by a pure selector test.
- [ ] **Parent AC2 traced:** **AC2 — Weak weapons are never auto-selected.** An owned weapon whose matchup is `weak` is never added by the auto-selector, and is not forced into the selection by the fill step.
- [ ] **Parent AC3 traced:** **AC3 — Variety then preference (Q3 = A then C).** The selector applies at most one weapon per behaviour family, then prefers `strong`, then at least one defensive power-up the deployment will auto-grant, then the highest permanent level, and fills toward the shared six-slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`) without exceeding it — accounting for the owned power-ups that also consume slots at grant time.
- [ ] **Parent AC7 traced:** **AC7 — One shared, pure rule.** The selector is pure and Phaser-free, lives in the shared core/model (not scene code), is consumed by the game and `GymHangar`, and reuses `resolveBossMatchup`, the shipped catalogue and the shared slot-cap helper — no second matchup or slot rule.
- [ ] **Parent AC8 traced:** **AC8 — Determinism and idempotence.** The selector is deterministic for a given (payload, target, catalogue) — no wall-clock, no unseeded draws — and re-applying it does not duplicate entries or oscillate the selection.

## Minimal Implementation

- New module beside `hangarEconomy.ts`; read ownership from `payload.hangar`, matchup from `weaponMatchup.ts`, levels from `hangarPermanentLevels`, the cap from `powerups/slots.ts`, families from `utils/weapons.ts`.
- Return a small result interface (suggested ids + counts + whether it differs from the current selection) so the model can present it without recomputing.

## Deliverables

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarAutoLoadout.ts`
- Green `src/core/hangarWar/hangarAutoLoadout.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Requires the F1 contract tests (they define the API).

**Key Files:**
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarAutoLoadout.ts` (new)
- `src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts` (read-only)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` (read-only: ownership, `hangarPermanentLevels`, `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS`)
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` (read-only: `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`, `capDropIdsToSlotPool`)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` (read-only: behaviour descriptors)
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` (read-only: the grant list the budget mirrors)

## Out of scope

- Scene/model wiring, the apply-suggested-buildout button and docs (later slices).
- Making power-ups loadout-selectable (AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z).

## Goal

Pin the power-up selection contract **red-first**, so every implementation child
in this plan turns a failing test green instead of inventing a rule. Scope is
tests only (plus the shared fixture the later children reuse); no production
behaviour changes here.

## Summary

A red-first contract suite for the optional power-up selection field, its
tri-state default, the ownership filter, the deployment grant and the
display-equals-grant invariant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Automated tests cover the model, the resolve/grant path and the gym parity (including a red-first test for the new selection field and its default).
- A red-first test suite covers the optional power-up selection field on `HangarLoadout` / `DeployedShip`, including its `undefined` default (a pre-feature payload keeps today's all-owned behaviour) and its `[]` (deliberate empty selection) case.
- Tests assert persistence reads the field by presence with no schema/version bump, and a save written before this feature (no selection field) round-trips byte-for-byte and still parses.
- Tests assert the resolve/equip path drops catalogue-unknown, unowned and non-level-bearing ids, so a corrupt save can never install an unowned power-up.
- Tests assert a deployment grants exactly the selected power-ups (and their permanent levels); deselected power-ups are not granted.
- Tests assert the combined selected weapons + power-ups respect the shared six-slot cap, and the displayed loadout matches what the run grants.
- Every new test fails for the intended reason before the implementation children land, with the red-first evidence recorded as a comment on this item.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts` with a fixture fleet owning more level-bearing power-ups than the cap allows.
2. Add the failing assertions to `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` (presence default, round-trip, corrupt value) and `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` (ownership/kind filter, consumption reset shape).

# Intensity-arc planner: series ingest and band config

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** high
**Parent:** AH-0MWPCLYYG007NUJY · first slice of the pure planner (`scripts/intensity-arc.mjs`).

## Goal

A pure planner that loads every capture's recorded action-intensity series and
join anchor, maps series time onto video time, and exposes the single
overridable band/target config object — failing loudly, never silently short,
when a band cannot be filled.

## Scope

- New `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` + `scripts/intensity-arc.d.mts`.
- **Reuse** these helpers from `scripts/capture-series.mjs` rather than
  re-deriving anything: `ACTION_INTENSITY_SERIES_EXTENSION`,
  `CAPTURE_ANCHOR_EXTENSION`, `hasActionIntensitySample`,
  `actionIntensitySeriesFileName`, `captureAnchorFileName`,
  `captureSeriesStem`.
- `DEFAULT_INTENSITY_ARC_CONFIG` — **the only** definition of the arc
  (`high` 0.65–0.75 / 10 s, `medium` 0.40–0.55 / 7 s, `medium+`
  0.55–0.65 / 7 s, `very high` ≥ 0.75 / 10 s, **in arc order**), plus
  `minWindowSeconds: 1.0`, `fadeSeconds: 0.3` (vidc's
  `DEFAULT_FADE_DURATION_MS`) and `sampleRateHz: 10`. Documented defaults per
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §6.6's knob-object pattern.
- **No `--arc` / spec parser.** The arc is not a user-selectable value: the
  intensity arc is the only behaviour of `capture:promo`, so the config object
  is tuned by editing it (a plain Node script, no rebuild). Validation rejects
  a malformed config at module load with an actionable message, so a retune
  cannot ship a broken arc.
- Ingest: for each candidate clip, read `<stem>.action.jsonl` and
  `<stem>.capture.json`; skip header-only/sample-less series and clips whose
  anchor is missing or `approximate` with **exactly one** warning each; fail
  with an actionable error when no usable capture remains.
- Join: `videoTimeMs(t) = t − offsetMs` clamped at 0, exactly as
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5 documents.
- Shared run-length helper (`longestWindowSeconds(band)`) used by both the
  shortfall diagnosis and (in the next item) window assembly.

## Key Files

- `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.d.mts` (new)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.test.ts` (extend)
- `scripts/capture-series.mjs` (reused, unchanged)

## Acceptance Criteria

- The planner loads `<stem>.action.jsonl` + `<stem>.capture.json` per capture, skips header-only/sample-less series and clips with a missing or `approximate` anchor with exactly one warning each, and fails with an actionable error when no usable capture remains; covered by unit tests over committed synthetic fixtures (no browser, no network).
- The four bands and their 7/7/10/10 s targets live in one documented config object, with **no CLI or flag override**; a band that cannot be filled fails naming band, required seconds and the longest available window; unit tested for both the satisfiable and the shortfall case.
- A malformed config object (unknown band name, non-positive duration, unordered arc) is rejected at load with an actionable message, unit tested — a retune can never ship a broken arc silently.
- Series time is mapped to video time with the anchor's `offsetMs` (`videoTimeMs = t − offsetMs`, clamped at 0), unit tested against a fixture whose plateau boundaries are known.

## Assumptions

- Band membership uses the instantaneous `intensity` field with inclusive
  `min` / exclusive `max`, except the top band which is `I ≥ min` (parent item
  assumption 1–2).

## Impact

A producer's recorded intensity series becomes readable, join-anchored data the promo edit can be planned from.

# Planner window selection and fade compensation

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** high
**Parent:** AH-0MWPCLYYG007NUJY · second slice of the pure planner: turn banded footage into the 34 s arc.

## Goal

`planIntensityArc(captures, config)` selects the actual footage windows — the
fewest non-overlapping windows that fill each band, in arc order, with the
fade overlap compensated so the **rendered** timeline totals 34 s.

## Scope

- Extend `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` with `planIntensityArc(...)` returning an
  ordered plan: `[{ band, sourceStem, inSeconds, durationSeconds, videoTimeSeconds }]`.
- Selection rules:
  - arc order **high → medium → medium+ → very high**;
  - windows are non-overlapping inside a source clip **and** never reused
    across bands (one window per unit of footage);
  - fewest windows per band reaching the target, minimum window length
    `minWindowSeconds` (1.0 s);
  - windows may come from different captures (pooled across the corpus).
- Edge nudging: window boundaries are nudged to local `smoothed` minima within
  a small bounded distance so a cut does not land mid-spike (parent assumption
  2). The bound and the nudge are documented in the module and unit tested.
- Fade compensation: `rendered = Σ durations − (clips − 1) × fadeSeconds`, so
  the planner adds `(clips − 1) × fadeSeconds` of footage, distributed across
  bands, to deliver 34 s rendered. The chosen formula is documented in the
  module and asserted by a test; the binding constraint is the rendered total,
  not any per-band sketch (parent AC3(d), assumption 3).
- Determinism of the plan itself: candidates are ordered by clip natural order,
  then earliest `t`; ties never depend on filesystem iteration order.

## Key Files

- `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` (extend)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.d.mts` (extend)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.test.ts` (extend)

## Acceptance Criteria

- The chosen windows (a) are non-overlapping within each source clip, (b) are ordered high → medium → medium+ → very high, (c) use the fewest windows reaching each target with a 1.0 s minimum, and (d) produce a rendered-timeline total of 34 s (fade overlap compensated); asserted on synthetic series with known-intensity plateaus plus a property test that no window is reused.
- A band that cannot be filled reports the shortfall (`band, required seconds, longest available window`) from the real selection pass, not from an estimate, and is unit tested on the `short-band` fixture.
- Window boundaries never cut mid-spike: each edge lies within the documented nudge bound of a local `smoothed` minimum, unit tested on a fixture with a spike adjacent to each band edge.
- Re-planning the same captures twice in one process and in a fresh process yields an identical plan array (deep equality); unit tested.

## Assumptions

- The per-band share of the inter-band fade overlap is an implementation
  detail; the AC binds the **rendered total** (34 s) and each band's rendered
  outcome, so the planner may choose the distribution that keeps windows
  contiguous.
- `--fade-duration` is the only softening mechanism (document transitions are
  not rendered yet: VC-0MWNW4SPX002J2SE / VC-0MWNW4T81005YFBJ), so joins are
  hard cuts in the document.

## Impact

A producer gets an arc cut from the measured action — 10 s of high, 7 s medium, 7 s medium+, 10 s very high — instead of filename order.

# OTIO document writer for the arc plan

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** high
**Parent:** AH-0MWPCLYYG007NUJY · emit the plan as an OpenTimelineIO 0.16.0 document `vidc` can compile.

## Goal

Serialise the arc plan as a valid OTIO 0.16.0 document (`Timeline.1` /
`Track.1` / `Clip.1`) whose clips carry a document-relative `target_url` and a
`source_range` in point, deterministically, so the edit decision is
hand-editable and reproducible.

## Scope

- New `scripts/otio-write.mjs` + `scripts/otio-write.d.mts`:
  `buildOtioDocument(plan, options)` → document object,
  `serialiseOtioDocument(document)` → byte-stable string (2-space JSON, one
  trailing newline).
- Labels `Timeline.1`/`Stack.1`/`Track.1`/`Clip.1`/`TimeRange.1`/
  `RationalTime.1`/`ExternalReference.1` **mirrored** from the `video_compiler`
  model (`src/otio/model.ts`, `OTIO_SCHEMA_VERSION = '0.16.0'`), with a module
  comment naming that repo as the source of truth. Plain JSON, **no new
  dependency** (parent constraint).
- One video track; one `Clip.1` per planned window in arc order.
  `media_reference` is an `ExternalReference.1` whose `target_url` is the clip
  basename relative to the document's directory (`gameplay-….webm`), never an
  absolute path.
- `source_range.start_time` = the window's in point, `source_range.duration` =
  the window length, both `RationalTime.1` at `rate: 30` (vidc's
  `DEFAULT_OTIO_RATE`) with values rounded to whole frames by a documented rule;
  a test pins the quantisation to ±1 frame of the planned window so the ±100 ms
  per-band acceptance tolerance stays reachable.
- `metadata` records the planner inputs: band thresholds, `fadeSeconds`, the
  arc spec, the source stems and the per-band achieved seconds, so an edit is
  auditable.

## Key Files

- `scripts/otio-write.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/otio-write.d.mts` (new)
- `scripts/otio-write.test.ts` (new)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` (consumes the plan type)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the planner twice on the same inputs produces a byte-identical `.otio`; ties resolve by clip natural order then earliest `t`; unit tested by double-run comparison.
- The emitted `.otio` parses as `Timeline.1`/`Track.1`/`Clip.1` with one video track, one `Clip.1` per window carrying a document-relative `target_url` and a `source_range` whose start/duration equal the planned window, and is accepted by `vidc timeline`/`vidc render` with no schema diagnostics; the parse assertions are unit tested, the `vidc` acceptance is a documented manual verification step.
- Every emitted `target_url` is a bare basename (no directory, no absolute path) that exists in the capture directory the plan was drawn from; unit tested, including a plan whose windows span two captures.
- `metadata` echoes the band thresholds, fade, arc spec and per-band achieved seconds used for the plan, asserted against the planner's own config object so the document can never record values the plan did not use.

## Assumptions

- Frame quantisation at rate 30 is acceptable: ±16.7 ms per boundary, well
  inside the ±100 ms per-band acceptance tolerance (AC7).

## Impact

A producer can open, tweak and re-render the promo edit in any OTIO editor instead of hand-picking timestamps.
data.title: OTIO document writer for the arc plan

# Wire `capture:promo` to vidc as an arc-planned document source

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** high
**Parent:** AH-0MWPCLYYG007NUJY · CLI surface, `vidc` handoff as a document source, and docs.

## Goal

A bare `npm run capture:promo` plans the intensity arc, writes
`capture-output/promo.otio`, and hands that document to `vidc render` as its
**explicit** timeline source. There is **no flag and no alternative mode**: the
intensity arc is the only behaviour this entry point has. An opt-in flag was
rejected as pointless — cut-to-the-action is the point of the command.

## Scope

- `scripts/render-promo.mjs`: remove the "forward `--dir` to `vidc` discovery"
  path. Every run plans → writes the document → hands it to `vidc`.
  `parseArgs`/`buildVidcArgv` stay pure and testable; the option surface is
  reduced to the options that still mean something:
  `--dir` (directory of captures to plan **from**), `--output` (the MP4, whose
  stem names the `.otio`), `--pattern` (capture-input filter, keeping today's
  default that excludes `.seekable.webm` / `.partial.webm`), `--format`,
  `--resolution`, `--fps`, `--fade-duration`, `--overwrite`, `--dry-run`,
  `--json`, `--vidc`, `--help`. `USAGE_TEXT` is rewritten to describe the arc —
  it must not advertise a flag that does not exist.
- Every run:
  1. discover candidate captures in `--dir` with the default pattern (or the
     `--pattern` filter);
  2. run the planner and the OTIO writer, **always rewriting**
     `<output>.otio` (`capture-output/promo.otio`) so a stale document can never
     drive a render;
  3. invoke `vidc render --timeline <promo.otio> --output <promo.mp4>` plus the
     surviving optional `--format`/`--resolution`/`--fps`/`--fade-duration`/
     `--overwrite`/`--json` flags. Never pass `--dir`, `--pattern` or
     `--recursive`: with a document source `vidc` ignores them silently, and
     `--timeline` must be the deliberate source rather than the auto-detected
     `<output>.otio` accident.
- **No `--arc` override and no CLI knob** for band thresholds or durations: the
  arc spec and thresholds live in `DEFAULT_INTENSITY_ARC_CONFIG` (previous
  item) and are tuned by editing that one object, per parent assumption 7.
  `--intensity-arc` and `--arc` become *unknown arguments*: exit 2 with the
  usage text, never a silently accepted no-op.
- `--dry-run`: print the arc plan (per-band windows, in points, achieved
  seconds) and the `vidc` argv to stdout, write no `.otio` and no MP4, and do
  not spawn `vidc` — so it works on a machine with no `vidc` installed.
- Missing-`vidc` remediation (exit 127 with the install hint) is unchanged.
- Docs: record the new consumer, the arc as the sole behaviour, and the removal
  of the concat-everything default in `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5
  (which currently says selection is no longer done in this repo) and in
  `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`; include the band/threshold defaults table, the
  drop-out of captures that have no series, the `--dry-run` output, and the
  `vidc render --dir` escape hatch for a plain whole-clip concat.

## Key Files

- `scripts/render-promo.mjs` (rewritten CLI surface + handoff)
- `scripts/render-promo.test.ts` (rewritten to the new contract, plus new cases)
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` (§7.5)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- A bare `npm run capture:promo` generates the document and invokes
  `vidc render` with `--timeline <dir>/promo.otio` and `--output <dir>/promo.mp4`,
  and the argv contains no `--dir`, `--pattern` or `--recursive`; asserted on
  the pure `buildVidcArgv` output.
- No flag selects or disables the arc: `--intensity-arc` and `--arc` are
  rejected as unknown arguments with the usage text and exit 2, asserted by a
  test (a silently accepted flag is a failure).
- `--dry-run` prints the arc plan and the `vidc` argv, writes no `.otio` and no
  MP4, and never spawns `vidc` (asserted with a mocked spawn, so the case runs
  without the binary).
- The document is rewritten on every real run: a pre-existing stale
  `promo.otio` is replaced, asserted by seeding a stale file and comparing the
  contents afterwards.
- Existing `render-promo` tests are rewritten to the new contract — argv
  forwarding of the surviving flags, exit-code propagation, `--json`
  passthrough and unchanged exit-127 missing-binary remediation — rather than
  left asserting the removed `--dir` discovery path. Tests are written first
  and the full `npm run test` gate is green.
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5 and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`
  document the arc as the sole behaviour, the band defaults, the drop-out of
  series-less captures and the `vidc render --dir` escape hatch; `--help`
  describes the arc and mentions no flag.

## Impact

A producer runs one command to get a promo whose cut follows the action they
recorded, and can inspect or hand-edit `capture-output/promo.otio` before
rendering.
