# Bot needs to be more accurate with its navigation — Intake Brief

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** bug · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

The competent bot's aim **lead** is effectively not running for the enemies it shoots at. `engage`
aims at `interceptPoint(...)` only when its chosen target exposes `vx`/`vy`, but the snapshot only
carries velocity for entities with a physics body — in practice `Asteroid` and `LaneTraffic`
(`src/entities/Asteroid.ts:418`, `src/entities/LaneTraffic.ts:145`). Every formation, `chaser`,
`diver` and `patroller` enemy moves by scripted position updates with no `vx`/`vy`
(`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:121`), so the bot aims at the target's **current** position and the shot
arrives after the target has moved — the ship "often misses its target". Where a lead *is* solved,
the trajectory model is a constant-velocity straight line and the projectile speed used for the
time of flight is the **enemy** bullet speed (`assumedBulletSpeed` = 200 px/s), not the ship's own
350 px/s, so the lead is over-estimated by 75 %. Meanwhile the bot already owns a better motion
model for the same entities — the per-hazard velocity/curvature tracker plus the movement-class
trajectory sampler that hazard avoidance runs — so the fix is to apply the **same calculations to
aim as are used to predict movement**, and to give the aim a small, configurable error so it is
deliberately imperfect rather than accidentally wrong.

## Users

- **Player watching the attract/demo bot** (primary): expects a pilot whose shots connect with the
  enemy it is chasing, not one that keeps missing a curving target.
- **Producer tuning the bot in `GymBotTuning`** (secondary): wants the lead/aim error as live knobs
  and a reproducible, test-backed accuracy number rather than a subjective "looks better".
- **Developer** (secondary): wants one trajectory definition shared by prediction and aim so the
  two cannot drift apart.

### Example user stories

- As a **viewer of the demo**, I want the bot's shots to hit the chaser that is curving toward the
  ship, so the demo reads as competent rather than broken.
- As a **producer**, I want a configurable aim error so the bot is beatable and human-looking, and a
  live slider to trade accuracy for fallibility.
- As a **developer**, I want the aim solve to consume the same velocity and movement-class
  prediction as hazard avoidance, so I fix prediction once and both features benefit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Aim lead uses the bot's own motion estimate, not the snapshot's.** The `engage` aim solve
  resolves its target's velocity from the bot-side tracker
  (`trackHazardVelocities` → `BotWorld.hazards[].vx/vy/curvature`, the same estimate the hazard
  predictor consumes) instead of the raw `BotEnemy.vx/vy` field. A moving formation/`chaser`/
  `diver`/`patroller` target that exposes no snapshot velocity is therefore led. When no estimate
  exists yet (cold start, stale, or an id-less fixture target) the solve reduces **exactly** to
  today's behaviour (aim at the current position).
- **AC2 — Solve inputs come from live physics.** The intercept solve takes the **player's**
  projectile speed and the **ship's live turn time**, not the bot's assumptions:
  `assumedBulletSpeed` (200 px/s, an enemy-bullet tell constant) is replaced as the aim
  time-of-flight input by the ship's live projectile speed (350 px/s `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` /
  per-weapon speed, carried through the snapshot seam the way `getThrusterConfig()`/
  `getRotationConfig()` already are), and the fixed `aimLeadAlignSeconds` alignment term is
  derived from the live rotation model (`angularStopDisplacement` + rotation accel/decel) with the
  constant retained only as the no-config fallback. A unit test pins 200 → 350 and the
  turn-time derivation.
- **AC3 — Predict the trajectory the target will actually fly.** For a target with a fitted velocity
  and a known movement class, the intercept point is solved by advancing the target along the
  **sampled class trajectory** (`advanceHazardMotion`, the single definition of each class's
  motion, already used by `predictMinimumSeparation`) and re-estimating time of flight each
  iteration; `roamer`/unknown class/disabled motion model reproduces the constant-velocity solve
  bit-for-bit, and a stationary target reproduces the current-position aim bit-for-bit. Wrap-aware
  (torus) behaviour from AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15 is preserved.
- **AC4 — Configurable, self-correcting aim error.** A new live-tuned `aimErrorRad` (radians,
  default small — ≈0.02 rad — and applied only to intents flagged as **aim**, never to
  survival/evade/travel) perturbs the committed aim bearing from the governor's dedicated seeded
  aim-error RNG stream (deterministic per run seed, no draw at `0`, so `0` is byte-for-byte today's
  behaviour). It is independent of the existing `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` degradation. The error is
  **adaptive, not fixed** (producer answer Q1): every confirmed hit on the engaged target multiplies
  the current error by `aimErrorDecay` (default ≈0.5, floored at 0), so a bot that keeps hitting
  zeroes in; the error is restored to `aimErrorRad` only after a **repositioning move** — the ship
  having moved `aimErrorResetDistance` px (default ≈60, torus-aware, measured from its position at
  the last hit) or having changed engagement target. All three knobs are live sliders via
  `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` / `GymBotTuning` and persisted in `src/data/bot-tuning.json`; the hit
  signal arrives through one shared scene seam (AC6), so the game and every gym feed it identically.
- **AC5 — Accuracy is measured, not asserted.** A deterministic headless aim-accuracy harness
  (seeded, fixed 60 Hz, a fixed seed list of at least three seeds, one scenario per movement class)
  reports shots fired / shots hit / mean miss distance for the new solve against the pre-change
  baseline, and a regression test asserts the pooled hit rate is strictly higher than the baseline
  and the mean miss distance lower, with `aimErrorRad = 0`. The measured before/after numbers are
  recorded on the work item.
- **AC6 — Single-sourced and gym-parity clean.** All behaviour lives in the shared `src/ai` code
  (plus the snapshot seam and the hit seam); `PlayScene`, `GymBotTuning` and every bot-bearing gym
  consume the same code, with no per-scene copy and no gym/game divergence introduced. The aim-hit
  signal is published from the shared `CombatScene` collision path — a hook beside the existing
  `onEnemyDestroyed` / `finaliseEnemyKill` seam (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:662`), plus the
  overridable `CombatScene.onEnemyDestroyed` precedent at line 1195 — never re-implemented per
  scene.
- **AC7 — Docs and tests.** `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.8 (rotation skills / lead) and the §12 knob
  list describe the new solve, the new knob and the accuracy harness; unit tests cover the solve,
  the speed/turn inputs and the error draw, and `src/ai/botRotationSkills.integration.test.ts` (or a
  sibling integration test) exercises the end-to-end aim. All related documentation is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
  Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The demo bot's shots now land on the enemy it is actually chasing — including curving and
formation enemies it currently aims behind — the bot visibly zeroes in while a burst keeps hitting
and gets its wobble back when it repositions, and designers get sliders to dial in how fallible it
looks.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** Shared behaviour stays in `src/ai/`; `PlayScene`, the shared
  `src/scenes/core/` code and every gym scene consume the same functions.
- **No physics constants in the bot layer.** Live ship values arrive through the `BotSnapshot` seam
  (the `getRotationConfig()` / `getThrusterConfig()` precedent), never hard-coded in `src/ai/`.
- **Deterministic and cheap.** No wall clock, seeded RNG only, same inputs → same output; the per-tick
  path stays allocation-free/bounded (it runs for every engage tick inside the 50-enemy perf
  envelope).
- **Telemetry schema unchanged.** Accuracy is measured in the test/harness layer; no new telemetry
  event kinds are introduced by this item.
- **Out of scope (record, do not absorb).** Re-driving the real enemy entities from
  `advanceHazardMotion` (a substantially larger predictor/entity unification); telemetry
  shots-fired/hit events; per-pod orbit-weapon lead; enemy aim accuracy (this item is the ship's
  aim).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — stale or cold tracked estimate.** The tracker needs two ticks of history, so the first
  engagement tick has no velocity. Mitigation: the documented exact fallback to the current-position
  aim, covered by a unit test.
- **Risk — the class model is not the entity's real movement.** `advanceHazardMotion` is the
  predictor's own definition; a class whose real entity diverges would still mis-lead. Mitigation:
  the AC5 harness measures per class so a diver/chaser regression is visible, and unifying the
  entities with the model is recorded as an explicit follow-up rather than silently absorbed.
- **Risk — over-leading a reverser.** Formation enemies drift and reverse; a long lead on an enemy
  that turns back over-leads further than no lead. Mitigation: the class sampler's bounded horizon
  and iteration count, plus the `aimLeadEnabled` off-switch, and the per-class measurement in AC5.
- **Risk — per-tick cost.** The aim solve runs on every engage tick near the 50-enemy perf envelope.
  Mitigation: reuse the existing bounded sampler (`HAZARD_MOTION_MAX_SAMPLES`) and its scratch
  buffers; no per-tick allocation.
- **Risk — a hit signal that lies.** Counting hits on *any* enemy (a stray bullet, an AOE, a ram)
  would sharpen the aim for the wrong reason. Mitigation: only a hit on the **engaged target** decays
  the error, and the repositioning reset keeps a streak from surviving a change of victim.
- **Risk — repositioning definition mismatch.** A distance-only rule could re-arm the error mid-fight
  during a slow strafe, or never re-arm it in a hugging fight. Mitigation: `aimErrorResetDistance` is
  a live knob, the target change also re-arms, and the AC5 harness reports the shot mix (led vs
  unled) so the rule is tuned on numbers.
- **Risk — scope creep into entity/predictor unification**, telemetry shot events or weapon-specific
  lead. Mitigation: all three are listed as out of scope; they become linked work items if wanted.
- **Assumption** — the turn actuator (deadband, inertia-aware hold) is correct; only the aim target
  changes. **Assumption** — 350 px/s is the representative ship projectile speed (pod weapons at
  300 px/s are accepted as within the aim error). **Resolved by the producer (Q1)** — the error is a
  dedicated `aimErrorRad` that decays on hits and re-arms on a repositioning move.

## Existing state

- Aim lead today: `engage` calls `interceptPoint` only when `best.point.vx/vy` are non-zero
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts:212`), passing `t.assumedBulletSpeed` (200 px/s) as the
  **projectile** speed and `t.aimLeadAlignSeconds` (0.25 s default, 0.35 s shipped tuning) as the
  alignment term.
- `interceptPoint` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts:197`) is a pure constant-velocity
  iterated lead; wrap-aware since AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15, but it never consults a movement class.
- Shot speed: travelling player bullets use `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 350`
  (`src/core/constants.ts:378`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:1114`); pod bullets use 300
  (`src/utils/weapons.ts:689`). `assumedBulletSpeed = 200`
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts:444`) is described in
  `src/ai/tuningFields.ts:126` as the *enemy*-bullet speed for fire tells — it is reused here for
  the ship's time of flight.
- Motion model that already exists and is already trusted for prediction:
  `trackHazardVelocities` (`src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts:178`, velocity + curvature from a
  bounded position history), `resolveEnemyMovementClass`
  (`src/ai/framework/enemyMovementClass.ts:75`, archetype → class mirror of
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) and `advanceHazardMotion`
  (`src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts:595`), consumed by `predictMinimumSeparation`. Its
  docstring states the evaluation arena advances live hostiles with the same call, so prediction and
  "actual movement" are meant to be one definition.
- Aim error that already exists: `BotInputGovernor` perturbs aim-flagged intents by
  `maxAimErrorRad × (1 − skill)` from a dedicated seeded stream
  (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts:943`), default `skill = 1` (off).
- The ship auto-fires (no aim gate on the trigger), so accuracy is entirely "is the nose where the
  target will be".
- Hit feedback does not exist: player-bullet damage is applied in
  `CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:576`) and kills are
  finalised once in `finaliseEnemyKill` / `onEnemyDestroyed` (`:662`, `:1195`), but nothing tells the
  bot whether an aimed shot connected — `BotSnapshot.player` (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:76`) carries no
  hit signal, so AC4's adaptive error needs a new seam.
- Shot accuracy is not currently measured: the evaluation harness has kills and player hits but no
  shots-fired event (`docs/TELEMETRY.md` §event kinds).

## Desired change

- Resolve the engaged target's motion from the tracker (AC1) and keep the raw-snapshot path as the
  cold-start fallback.
- Carry the ship's live projectile speed and rotation config through the snapshot seam and feed the
  real values into the solve (AC2), plus the aim-hit count the governor needs for AC4.
- Add a class-aware intercept that samples `advanceHazardMotion`, converging time of flight against
  the sampled trajectory, and reduce exactly to the legacy solve when the class/estimate is
  unknown (AC3).
- Add `aimErrorRad` as a seeded, aim-only, live-tunable error that decays on confirmed hits and
  re-arms on a repositioning move (AC4), fed by a new shared aim-hit seam (AC6).
- Add the headless accuracy harness and record its before/after numbers (AC5).
- Update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and the knob documentation (AC7).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — `engage` aim solve: consume the tracked motion and
  class, pass the live shot speed and turn time.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `interceptPoint`: add the class-sampled variant and
  the live turn-time input, preserving exact fallbacks.
- `src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts` — reuse `advanceHazardMotion` (no new trajectory code).
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — expose the engaged target's tracker estimate to the aim path
  (hazards already carry `vx`/`vy`/`curvature`/`movementClass`).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — carry the ship's live projectile speed, rotation config (if not already
  present) and the aim-hit count through the structural source seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — publish the aim-hit hook beside `onEnemyDestroyed` /
  `finaliseEnemyKill` (single-sourced for the game and every gym).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — thread the hit count (and the
  reposition state the governor derives from the snapshot) into the bot without local logic.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`, `src/data/bot-tuning.json` —
  the new knob plus the `assumedBulletSpeed` description fix.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — `aimErrorRad` / `aimErrorDecay` / `aimErrorResetDistance` in the
  governor tunables, the seeded draw and the hit-decay / reposition-reset state.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`, `behaviours.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botRotationSkills.integration.test.ts`, plus the new aim-accuracy harness — tests.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — §9.8 and the §12 knob table.

## Related work

- **Bot rotation skills (AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98)** — introduced the lead solve, the inertia-aware turn
  hold and the `skill` aim error; this item continues that work by fixing the solve's inputs.
- **Predict enemy movement (bot) (AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN)** — built the hazard velocity tracker this
  item reuses for aim.
- **Movement-class seam for bot hazards (AH-0MWM0C6OW006G5SE)**, **Class-shaped hazard trajectory
  prediction (AH-0MWM0C9F9006HNXV)**, **Sampled prediction in steering and kiting
  (AH-0MWM0CB2Q003Y6AB)** — the class model and sampler the aim solve should share.
- **Seam-aware aim and intercept (AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15)** — the torus solve that must be preserved.
- **Bot needs to be better at avoiding enemies (AH-0MWLUIOH9001XBJ3)** — the sibling play-testing
  item on prediction fidelity for *avoidance*; same diagnosis, different consumer.
- Duplicate check performed — no completed item already satisfies these acceptance criteria.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Questions were queued for the producer at intake time and answered in an interactive producer
reply (2026-11-21). The brief above reflects the accepted answers; the recommended option and the
producer's extra condition are recorded per entry.

- **Q1 (answered) — What should the configurable aim error be, and what should it default to?**
  - Options: (a) a new dedicated `aimErrorRad` (radians) applied to aim intents only, default small
    (≈0.02 rad), independent of the existing `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` degradation; (b) reuse
    `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` and simply ship a default `skill < 1`; (c) declare a per-shot *hit*
    probability and deliberately throw the shot wide on a failed roll.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — a dedicated knob leaves the existing skill degradation intact for
    "make the bot worse on purpose" and gives one unambiguous number to tune; (c) would be a
    different (probability) model and much harder to make believable.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **"(a) — but once the bot hits the error should be
    reduced until they make a repositioning move."** Source: producer reply in this session.
    Research: the governor already owns a dedicated seeded aim-error stream
    (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts:943`), so the decay/reset state lives beside it and needs no new RNG;
    shortening the error on a hit requires a hit signal the bot does not have today, so AC4 now
    carries the adaptive rule and AC6 the shared seam that feeds it. AC4 was rewritten to specify
    `aimErrorDecay` (multiplicative, floored at 0) and `aimErrorResetDistance` (the repositioning
    move), so both halves of the producer's condition are testable.
- **Q2 (answered) — What does "the same calculations for predicting movement as those used in
  actual movement" mean in scope?**
  - Options: (a) reuse the bot-side trajectory model the hazard predictor already uses (tracked
    velocity/curvature + `advanceHazardMotion`), leaving the enemy entities untouched; (b) also
    re-drive the real enemy entities from `advanceHazardMotion` so prediction and entity code are
    literally the same call site (much larger, touches every enemy and gym).
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it delivers the requested prediction fidelity in the bot layer only, with
    no entity/gym churn; (b) is the natural follow-up once (a) proves the model is faithful.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(a)**. Source: producer reply in this session. (b) stays
    recorded as explicit out-of-scope in *Constraints* and becomes a follow-up item if wanted.
- **Q3 (answered) — How should "more accurate" be evidenced?**
  - Options: (a) a deterministic headless harness reporting shots fired / hits / mean miss distance
    per movement class, with a regression assertion against the pre-change baseline; (b) unit-level
    assertions on the solve only (no end-to-end number); (c) add telemetry shot events and compare
    recorded runs.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it produces a number the producer can quote and needs no telemetry
    schema change; (c) is a much bigger change for the same evidence.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(a)**. Source: producer reply in this session. No
    telemetry schema change; the harness numbers are recorded on the work item as AC5's evidence.
- **Assumption (not a question): title scope.** The title says "navigation" while the seed body
  ("It often misses its target") is about aim. Researched `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts`,
  `steering.ts`, `botHumanLike.ts` and the snapshot seam (see *Existing state*); the defect found is
  target-prediction/aim accuracy, and the fix also tightens the ship's own turn-time prediction
  (which is navigation-adjacent). Treated as an aim/prediction-accuracy item.
- **Assumption: turn control is already adequate.** `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` (0.05 rad) and the
  inertia-aware turn hold from AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98 are assumed correct; this item changes what the
  nose is aimed at, not how the nose is turned.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15** – Seam-aware aim and intercept (completed)
- **AH-0MWM0C6OW006G5SE** – Movement-class seam for bot hazards (completed)
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** – Extract common enemy base class for regular enemies (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv1dusm2005hl98, 0mvi4qdn90037din, 0mwm0c9f9006hnxv, 0mwm0cb2q003y6ab, absorb (+549 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv1dusm2005hl98, absorb, absorbed, ac1, ac2 (+499 more)
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — matched: 0mv1dusm2005hl98, 0mvi4qdn90037din, 0mwm0c9f9006hnxv, 0mwm0cb2q003y6ab, ac1 (+472 more)



## Plan: decomposition into features (2026-11-21)

Decomposed into **8 vertical slices** in test-first, dependency order. Each slice carries the code,
its tests and (where it changes behaviour) the documentation its own consumers read; a consolidated
documentation slice closes parent AC7 because the aim solve, the knob table and the harness are one
narrative section (§9.8/§12) that reads badly if split.

| # | Child | Type | Covers | Depends on | Est. |
|---|-------|------|--------|-----------|------|
| 1 | Aim-accuracy harness and pre-change baseline (AH-0MWR04UJ5008H5WQ) | task | AC5 (measurement) | — | ~3h |
| 2 | Tracker-derived aim velocity (AH-0MWR04X10002VNDG) | feature | AC1 | 1 | ~2h |
| 3 | Live physics inputs in the aim solve (AH-0MWR04ZDU0005O8J) | feature | AC2 | 2 | ~2h |
| 4 | Class-sampled intercept solve (AH-0MWR051U6003BDB9) | feature | AC3 | 3 | ~3h |
| 5 | Shared aim-hit seam (AH-0MWR054VE006YSLN) | feature | AC6 | 1 | ~2h |
| 6 | Adaptive aim error knobs (AH-0MWR057Q8004PBOD) | feature | AC4 (+AC6 delivery) | 4, 5 | ~3h |
| 7 | Accuracy regression proof and recorded numbers (AH-0MWR05EZE0044Z01) | task | AC5 (proof) | 1–4, 6 | ~2h |
| 8 | Aim solve documentation and knob docs (AH-0MWR05J320041SAA) | docs | AC7 | 1–6 | ~2h |

**Why this order**

- **Measurement first.** The harness (slice 1) and its pinned pre-change baseline exist before any
  behaviour changes, so "more accurate" is a comparison against a recorded number rather than an
  opinion, and slice 7 turns it into an assertion.
- **One aim call site at a time.** Slices 2 → 3 → 4 each touch `engage`'s aim solve; doing them
  serially means each lands with an exact-fallback parity test before the next changes the same
  lines.
- **The error is last.** The adaptive aim error (slice 6) consumes the hit signal from slice 5 and
  perturbs the solve from slice 4, so it cannot land before either.
- **Docs close the loop** after the behaviour is real (slice 8), and the docs assertions are what
  stop §9.8/§12 drifting from the code.

**Between slices:** review the next slice's description against what actually landed, update it
(and this table) before starting, and keep the per-class harness numbers on this item current.

**Estimate:** the plan-stage effort/risk run over the eight slices reports **Small / Medium**
(O 8.5 h · M 14.5 h · P 22 h → **14.33 h expected**, **18.33 h recommended**, 76 % confidence) — a
refinement of the intake estimate (10.25 h / 15.25 h) that now carries real per-slice inputs. The
item stays **Small** and **Medium** risk, so no plan-approval pause was required.

**Review outcome:** all seven parent acceptance criteria are owned by exactly one slice (AC5 by two:
measurement in slice 1, proof in slice 7), the AC coverage review returns `proceed`, and no new
clarifying questions were needed — the producer's intake answers (Q1–Q3, recorded in the Appendix
above) resolve every open choice.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-21 — created slices 1–8 with the table above; wired 15 dependency edges
  (2←1, 3←2, 4←3, 5←1, 6←4+5, 7←1–4+6, 8←1–6); appended the plan to the description; stage →
  `plan_complete` after the AC coverage review returned `proceed`.

### Appendix: planning-session questions

- **Q (plan, 2026-11-21) — are any further producer decisions needed to cut this into slices?**
  Answer: **no** — intake Q1 (dedicated `aimErrorRad` with decay-on-hit / re-arm-on-reposition,
  option a), Q2 (reuse the bot-side trajectory model, option a) and Q3 (deterministic headless
  accuracy harness, option a) are recorded in the Appendix above and settle every branch the
  decomposition faced. No follow-up questions were raised; nothing is left OPEN QUESTION at plan
  time. Source: this work item's Appendix (producer reply, 2026-11-21) plus the brief's AC1–AC7,
  *Key Files* and *Risks and assumptions* sections, which the slices restate rather than reinterpret.

# Aim-accuracy harness and pre-change baseline — Feature 1 of 8

**Parent:** AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP · **Effort:** ~3h · **Risk:** Medium

## Summary

No shot is measured today: the evaluation harness counts kills and player hits but has no
shots-fired / shots-hit / miss-distance metric, so "the bot is more accurate" cannot be asserted.
This feature builds the deterministic headless aim-accuracy harness and records the **pre-change
baseline** the later features must beat.

## Target outcome

A seeded, fixed-60 Hz harness flies the live competent brain in the headless arena against one
hostile field per movement class and reports, per class and pooled, shots fired / shots hit / mean
miss distance. Its baseline numbers are pinned in the repo so the improvement assertion in
Feature 7 is a comparison against a recorded number, not against a moving target.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A headless aim-accuracy harness (in `src/ai/eval/`, sibling of `hazardMotionSweep.test.ts`)
  flies the live competent brain in `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` at a fixed 60 Hz over a **fixed,
  documented seed list of at least three seeds**, with **one scenario per movement class**
  (`chaser`, `diver`, `patroller`, `formation`, `roamer`).
- The harness reports, per movement class and pooled: **shots fired**, **shots hit**, **hit rate**
  and **mean miss distance** (the perpendicular miss distance from the shot's line to the target
  it was aimed at, measured at the target's closest approach), and exposes them through a typed
  result object consumed by tests.
- A miss is attributed to the shot's aimed target (not merely "some enemy in the field"), so the
  metric cannot be inflated by splash or by a shot that hits a different body.
- The harness is deterministic: two runs with the same seed and config produce byte-identical
  metrics; no wall clock, seeded RNG only.
- The **pre-change baseline** numbers (current `engage` solve, `aimLeadEnabled` on) are recorded in
  the harness's module documentation and in a committed fixture, and a test asserts the pinned
  baseline reproduces on re-run (so a later behaviour change cannot silently redefine "baseline").
- The harness makes no production behaviour change: with the fixture unchanged, existing suites are
  byte-for-byte unaffected.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

- New `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.test.ts` plus a small helper module (e.g.
  `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.ts`) that drives `runArena` over the seed/class matrix and folds the
  arena's per-tick player-bullet / hostile state into the shot table.
- Shot attribution: tag each player bullet with the engaged target id at spawn time (arena-side tag
  only — no game change), then resolve hit/miss on the bullet's lifecycle end.
- Miss distance from the recorded bullet track and the aimed target's track at closest approach.
- Committed baseline fixture (JSON or a typed constant) + a re-run test pinning it.
- Module header documents the seeds, the 60 Hz tick, the scenarios and the metric definitions
  (mirroring `hazardMotionSweep.test.ts`'s "what is measured" section).

## Constraints / risky assumptions

- Deterministic, wall-clock free; bounded run time (the sweep precedent keeps a full matrix under a
  few seconds per seed).
- The harness must observe the *shipped* aim path (`engage` → governor), not a re-implementation;
  the metrics are only evidence if the code under test is the game's code.
- Assumption: the headless arena's player-bullet model (travelling bullets at the loadout's speed)
  is a faithful enough stand-in for the game's shots; the harness documents the divergence.
- The pinned baseline is a **recorded observation** — snapping it must not become a way to pass a
  regression. Feature 7 asserts *strictly better than* this fixture, never "equal to a fresh run".

## Dependencies

None. This feature is the test-first slice and must land before the implementation features.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.test.ts` — the harness test (new)
- `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.ts` — shot table, attribution and metric folding (new)
- `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.baseline.json` — the pinned pre-change baseline (new)
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — consumed as-is (per-tick hostile/bullet state), extended only if a
  bullet→aimed-target tag cannot be derived from the existing snapshot
- `src/ai/eval/hazardMotionSweep.test.ts` — the seeded-sweep pattern being mirrored
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — the aim path under measurement (read-only here)

# Tracker-derived aim velocity — Feature 2 of 8

**Parent:** AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP · **Effort:** ~2h · **Risk:** Medium

## Summary

`engage` leads only when the chosen target exposes `vx`/`vy`, and the snapshot carries velocity for
just `Asteroid`/`LaneTraffic`. Formations, chasers, divers and patrollers move by scripted position
updates with no body velocity, so the bot aims at the current position and misses a moving target.
The bot-side hazard tracker already holds the estimate the predictor uses; this feature feeds it to
the aim solve.

## Target outcome

The aim solve resolves the engaged target's velocity from the tracker estimate on
`view.world.hazards[]` (matched by the target's stable `id`), so a target with no snapshot velocity
is led. With no estimate available the solve reduces exactly to today's current-position aim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC1 (restated — this feature owns it):** **AC1 — Aim lead uses the bot's own motion estimate, not the snapshot's.** The `engage` aim solve resolves its target's velocity from the bot-side tracker (`trackHazardVelocities` → `BotWorld.hazards[].vx/vy/curvature`, the same estimate the hazard predictor consumes) instead of the raw `BotEnemy.vx/vy` field. A moving formation/`chaser`/ `diver`/`patroller` target that exposes no snapshot velocity is therefore led. When no estimate exists yet (cold start, stale, or an id-less fixture target) the solve reduces **exactly** to today's behaviour (aim at the current position).
- `engage` resolves the aim target's velocity from the tracked hazard estimate
  (`BotWorld.hazards[].vx/vy`) selected by the target's stable `id`, used **before** the raw
  `BotEnemy.vx/vy` snapshot field; a target with an estimate and no snapshot velocity is led.
- Precedence is explicit and tested: tracked estimate → snapshot `vx`/`vy` → current position
  (stationary). Each step is covered by a unit test on the engage behaviour.
- A target that exposes an id the hazard list does not contain (an id-less fixture target, a
  mineral, a drop, the boss) resolves to the previous behaviour **exactly**: no velocity estimate,
  aim point is the target's current position, no behavioural delta.
- When the hazard list carries a zero-vector estimate (cold start / stationary) the solve aims at
  the current position and the same intercept invocation is skipped, so the first engagement tick
  after acquiring a target is byte-for-byte today's shot.
- The wrap-aware (torus) route to the aim point from AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15 is preserved: the led
  point for a target whose shortest path crosses a seam still runs through `wrappedDelta`.
- The feature introduces no new allocation on the per-tick path: the target→hazard lookup is
  allocation-free (existing hazard scan or a reused lookup), asserted by the existing
  allocation/determinism checks (or a focused unit test).

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

- In `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts`, replace the `(targetVx !== 0 || targetVy !== 0)`
  snapshot gate with a shared resolver — e.g.
  `resolveAimTargetMotion(target, view.world.hazards, t)` returning `{ vx, vy, hazard? }` — that
  prefers the tracked estimate.
- Keep the existing `t.aimLeadEnabled` off-switch and the exact stationary fallback.
- Unit tests in `behaviours.test.ts` for the three precedence steps, the id-less fixture, and the
  cold-start zero-vector case; one torus case to pin wrap behaviour.
- Comment the resolver with the "one estimate for prediction and aim" rationale (parent AC1/AC6).

## Constraints / risky assumptions

- Shared code only (`src/ai/`); no scene logic, no gym/game divergence.
- Deterministic and allocation-free per tick; the resolver runs on every engage tick.
- Assumption: `BotHazardPoint.id` correlates with `ContentTarget.id` (both derive from the
  snapshot's bot-side id) — asserted directly by the unit tests.
- Assumption: a cold-start estimate is absent or zero, so the fallback is genuinely exact.

## Dependencies

- Feature 1 (aim-accuracy harness and baseline) — the harness measures this change in Feature 7.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — `engage` aim solve; the new motion resolver
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `BotHazardPoint` (`id`/`vx`/`vy`/`curvature`/`movementClass`),
  consumed as-is
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `ContentTarget.id` / `enemyTargets` identity
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts` — precedence and fallback tests

# Live physics inputs in the aim solve — Feature 3 of 8

**Parent:** AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP · **Effort:** ~2h · **Risk:** Medium

## Summary

The lead solve uses the **enemy** bullet speed (`assumedBulletSpeed` = 200 px/s) as the ship's time
of flight — the ship's own travelling shot flies at 350 px/s (`PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED`) — so the lead
is over-estimated by 75 %; and the alignment term is a fixed `aimLeadAlignSeconds` constant rather
than the ship's live turn time. Both inputs must come from live physics through the existing
snapshot seam, mirroring the established `resolvePlayerSpeed` precedence (explicit tuning override >
live ship config > compiled default).

## Target outcome

The intercept solve receives the ship's **live projectile speed** and a **turn time derived from
the live rotation model**, with the compiled constants retained only as the no-config fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC2 (restated — this feature owns it):** **AC2 — Solve inputs come from live physics.** The intercept solve takes the **player's** projectile speed and the **ship's live turn time**, not the bot's assumptions: `assumedBulletSpeed` (200 px/s, an enemy-bullet tell constant) is replaced as the aim time-of-flight input by the ship's live projectile speed (350 px/s `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` / per-weapon speed, carried through the snapshot seam the way `getThrusterConfig()`/ `getRotationConfig()` already are), and the fixed `aimLeadAlignSeconds` alignment term is derived from the live rotation model (`angularStopDisplacement` + rotation accel/decel) with the constant retained only as the no-config fallback. A unit test pins 200 → 350 and the turn-time derivation.
- The bot snapshot carries the ship's live projectile speed through the structural source seam — a
  new optional getter on `BotPlayerSource` beside `getThrusterConfig()` — populated by every
  snapshot builder the game and gyms use, with the compiled `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` used only when
  the source exposes nothing.
- The bot snapshot carries the ship's live rotation config (rotation speed, acceleration,
  deceleration) through the same seam, and the aim's alignment term is derived from it
  (`angularStopDisplacement` + the rotation accel/decel model) rather than the fixed
  `aimLeadAlignSeconds`; the constant remains the documented no-config fallback.
- Precedence is explicit and tested, mirroring `resolvePlayerSpeed`: an explicit tuning override
  wins, otherwise the live ship value is used, otherwise the compiled default.
- A unit test **pins 200 → 350**: with a live ship and default tuning, the projectile speed fed to
  the intercept solve is the ship's (350), not `assumedBulletSpeed` (200); and the enemy-bullet
  tell usage of `assumedBulletSpeed` is unchanged (it still models enemy fire tells).
- A unit test pins the turn-time derivation: the derived alignment term equals the value computed
  from the supplied rotation config, and reproduces the constant when no rotation config is
  supplied.
- `assumedBulletSpeed`'s tuning description is corrected to state that it is the **enemy**-bullet
  tell constant and no longer the ship's aim time-of-flight input.
- `PlayScene`, `GymBotTuning` and every bot-bearing gym supply the same live values (no per-scene
  derivation), verified by a parity assertion.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

- Extend `BotPlayerSource` (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts`) with `getRotationConfig?()` and a live
  projectile-speed getter; add `rotation?: BotRotationConfig` and `shotSpeed?: number` to
  `BotPlayer`.
- Populate them where the snapshot is built (`buildBotSnapshot` reads the structural source; the
  scenes already hold `player.getRotationConfig()` for the governor).
- In `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, add a `resolveShotSpeed(t, liveShotSpeed)` sibling of
  `resolvePlayerSpeed`, and derive the alignment term in the engage solve from the snapshot's
  rotation config with the constant as fallback.
- Feed both into the `interceptPoint` call in `behaviours.ts`.
- Update `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` description for `assumedBulletSpeed`; add unit tests in
  `src/ai/botSnapshot.test.ts`, `tuningFields.test.ts` and `behaviours.test.ts`.

## Constraints / risky assumptions

- **No physics constants in the bot layer** (parent constraint): live values arrive via the
  snapshot seam; compiled defaults live in `src/core/constants.ts` and are imported, not
  duplicated as literals in `src/ai/`.
- Pod weapons at 300 px/s are accepted as within the aim error (parent assumption) — the solve uses
  the primary travelling shot's speed, documented as such.
- Assumption: the turn actuator itself is correct (parent assumption); this feature changes only
  the inputs to the estimate, not the actuator.
- Deterministic: the derivation is a pure function of the snapshot config.

## Dependencies

- Feature 2 (tracker-derived aim velocity) — both features edit the same `engage` aim call site, so
  this lands after it.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — `BotPlayerSource` / `BotPlayer` seam additions
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — `resolveShotSpeed` and the alignment-term derivation
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — pass the live speed and turn time into the solve
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `angularStopDisplacement` reuse for the turn time
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` — `assumedBulletSpeed` description correction
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — supply the live values to the
  snapshot source (no local derivation)
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.test.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts` — tests

# Class-sampled intercept solve — Feature 4 of 8

**Parent:** AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP · **Effort:** ~3h · **Risk:** Medium

## Summary

`interceptPoint` is a constant-velocity straight-line lead: it never consults the movement class, so
a curving chaser, a committed diver, an attacking patroller or a reversing formation is led along a
line it will not fly. The predictor already samples each class's trajectory with
`advanceHazardMotion`; this feature makes the aim solve use the same definition of motion.

## Target outcome

For a target with a fitted velocity and a known movement class, the intercept point is solved by
advancing the target along its **sampled class trajectory** with the time of flight re-estimated
each iteration, so the shot is aimed where a curving target will actually be. Unknown class,
`roamer` or a disabled motion model reproduces the constant-velocity solve bit-for-bit, and a
stationary target reproduces the current-position aim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC3 (restated — this feature owns it):** **AC3 — Predict the trajectory the target will actually fly.** For a target with a fitted velocity and a known movement class, the intercept point is solved by advancing the target along the **sampled class trajectory** (`advanceHazardMotion`, the single definition of each class's motion, already used by `predictMinimumSeparation`) and re-estimating time of flight each iteration; `roamer`/unknown class/disabled motion model reproduces the constant-velocity solve bit-for-bit, and a stationary target reproduces the current-position aim bit-for-bit. Wrap-aware (torus) behaviour from AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15 is preserved.
- A new sampled intercept (sibling of `interceptPoint` rather than a behavioural change to it)
  advances the target along `advanceHazardMotion` with the **same step/horizon discipline** the
  predictor uses (`HAZARD_MOTION_MAX_SAMPLES` and its scratch buffers), converging the time of
  flight against the sampled trajectory and returning the intercept point.
- `roamer`, an unknown/absent movement class, or the motion model disabled
  (`hazardMotionModelEnabled = false`) reproduces `interceptPoint`'s output **bit-for-bit** —
  asserted by a parity test over a table of inputs (velocity, alignment term, iterations, speed).
- A stationary target (zero estimate) aims at its current position bit-for-bit, including the
  torus-wrapped position case.
- Each class is covered by a unit test on a constructed snapshot: `chaser` (homing arc),
  `diver` (committed dive vector), `patroller` (patrol then attack run), `formation` (drift plus
  edge reversal); each asserts the sampled intercept differs from the straight-line lead in the
  direction the class curves and matches a reference computation.
- Wrap-aware (torus) behaviour from AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15 is preserved: the sampled trajectory and
  the shot's time of flight both run on the wrapped shortest route, asserted by a seam-crossing
  case.
- The solve is deterministic and allocation-free on the per-tick path: fixed sample count, reused
  scratch state, no wall clock, no RNG; repeated calls on the same inputs return identical points
  (asserted).
- `engage` consumes the sampled solve only when a tracked estimate and a real class exist, and falls
  back to `interceptPoint` otherwise, so no existing test's expected aim point changes without an
  explicit, documented motion-model-on case.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

- Add `interceptPointClassAware(shooter, target, motion, movementClass, shotSpeed, alignSeconds,
  iterations, tunables, world)` to `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` (or a sibling module
  beside `hazardMotionModel.ts` if steering would gain a heavy import).
- Reuse `advanceHazardMotion` per iteration: advance the target from its current position for the
  current time-of-flight estimate (a `HazardMotionScratch` copy), measure the wrapped distance to
  the ship, update the time of flight, repeat; bound steps with the existing max-sample constant.
- Wire it into the `engage` aim call site; keep `interceptPoint` untouched for the fallback.
- Tests: `steering.test.ts` (parity table, per-class reference values, torus seam, determinism,
  allocation bound) and `behaviours.test.ts` (which solve `engage` selects for each class/estimate).

## Constraints / risky assumptions

- Reuses the predictor's trajectory definition — **no new trajectory code** (parent AC3/constraint).
- Bounded work per decision tick: the existing max-sample constant caps the sampling; the
  converged iteration count must not multiply that cap beyond the current per-tick budget (document
  the product and keep it at or below the sampler's current worst case, or early-out when the
  estimate is zero).
- Assumption: `advanceHazardMotion` is a faithful-enough model of each class's real movement over a
  bounded lead horizon (the harness in Feature 7 measures each class, so a divergence is visible).
- Risk — over-leading a reversing formation: the bounded horizon and `aimLeadEnabled` off-switch are
  the mitigations; the per-class harness numbers tune the horizon, not the pass bar.

## Dependencies

- Feature 3 (live physics inputs) — the solve consumes the live shot speed and turn time.
- Feature 2 (tracker-derived aim velocity) — supplies the estimate and the class.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `interceptPoint` and the new sampled intercept
- `src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts` — `advanceHazardMotion` (reused, unchanged) and the
  max-sample constant
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — solve selection in `engage`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts` — tests

# Shared aim-hit seam — Feature 5 of 8

**Parent:** AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP · **Effort:** ~2h · **Risk:** Medium

## Summary

The adaptive aim error (Feature 6) needs to know when an aimed shot connected, and the bot has no
such signal: player-bullet damage is applied in `CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` and kills are
finalised in `finaliseEnemyKill` / `onEnemyDestroyed`, but nothing reaches the governor. This
feature publishes one shared hit seam from the combat core and threads it to the bot in the game and
every gym, with no per-scene identity logic.

## Target outcome

A confirmed player-bullet hit on an enemy is published once, from the shared `CombatScene` collision
path, to whichever bot governor the scene runs — identically in `PlayScene` and every bot-bearing
gym — carrying the struck enemy's bot-side identity so the governor can tell whether it hit the
target it was aiming at.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC6 (restated — this feature owns it):** **AC6 — Single-sourced and gym-parity clean.** All behaviour lives in the shared `src/ai` code (plus the snapshot seam and the hit seam); `PlayScene`, `GymBotTuning` and every bot-bearing gym consume the same code, with no per-scene copy and no gym/game divergence introduced. The aim-hit signal is published from the shared `CombatScene` collision path — a hook beside the existing `onEnemyDestroyed` / `finaliseEnemyKill` seam (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:662`), plus the overridable `CombatScene.onEnemyDestroyed` precedent at line 1195 — never re-implemented per scene.
- A protected, no-op-by-default hook is added beside the existing `onEnemyDestroyed` /
  `finaliseEnemyKill` seam and invoked from the shared `damageEnemyWithBullet` path for **every
  damage point actually applied** (including AOE and wave-laser hits that route through that seam),
  never per scene.
- The struck enemy is mapped to its **bot-side identity** by the shared id resolver the snapshot
  builder already uses, so the governor compares like with like; an enemy the bot cannot identify
  produces no signal.
- The hit signal is delivered to the bot through the shared `src/ai` code (a small helper the scenes
  call, e.g. `notifyAimHit(governor, enemy)`), so `PlayScene` and every bot-bearing gym contain no
  identity or decay logic of their own.
- `PlayScene` and `GymBotTuning` are wired to the seam; the gym-parity guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity assertions still pass with
  no duplicated body introduced.
- A unit test proves the hook fires exactly once per applied damage point and **not** for a ram, a
  wall bounce, an enemy-bullet/player hit, or a shielded hit that applied no damage.
- With no bot present (or the governor absent), the seam is inert: the game's behaviour and existing
  scene tests are byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

- Add `protected onPlayerBulletHitEnemy(_enemy: TEnemy): void {}` in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
  and call it from `damageEnemyWithBullet` where damage is actually applied (`applied` increments),
  before/after finalisation as appropriate so a lethal hit still reports once.
- Export a shared id resolver from `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` (`botEntityId(source)`) reused by
  `buildBotSnapshot` so the scene seam and the snapshot agree on identity.
- Add `notifyAimHit(governor, enemy)` in `src/ai/` (thin: resolve id, call
  `governor.noteAimHit(id)`), overridden in `PlayScene` and `GymBotTuning` to forward the hook.
- Tests: a `CombatScene`-level unit test for the hook's firing rules, plus a gym-parity assertion
  that the game and the gym publish through the same hook.

## Constraints / risky assumptions

- Single-sourced (parent AC6): the hook lives in the shared core, and both the game and gyms consume
  it; no duplicated bodies (the repo-wide equivalence guard enforces this).
- Only genuine damage-applying hits count — a ram, an enemy bullet hitting the player, a wall bounce
  or a zero-damage (shielded) contact must not report.
- Deterministic and cheap: the seam runs on the collision path, not per tick, and does no allocation
  beyond what the resolver already needs.
- Assumption: the bot-side id resolver (`WeakMap`-backed in `botSnapshot.ts`) is stable for an
  entity's lifetime, so a hit reported from the collision path matches the id the brain aimed at.

## Dependencies

- Feature 1 (aim-accuracy harness and baseline) — the harness's hit accounting is the evidence that
  the seam and the aim solve agree.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — the hit hook beside `onEnemyDestroyed` / `finaliseEnemyKill`
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — shared bot-side id resolver (`botEntityId`)
- `src/ai/aimHit.ts` — the `notifyAimHit` helper (new, beside the governor)
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — `noteAimHit` entry point (state lives in Feature 6)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — hook overrides forwarding to the bot
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body / gym-parity guard

# Adaptive aim error knobs — Feature 6 of 8

**Parent:** AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP · **Effort:** ~3h · **Risk:** Medium

## Summary

The bot's aim should be deliberately imperfect rather than accidentally wrong, and — per the
producer's answer to Q1 — the error should shrink while the bot keeps hitting and come back when it
repositions. The governor already perturbs aim intents from a dedicated seeded RNG stream for
`skill`/`maxAimErrorRad`; this feature adds a separate, live-tuned, self-correcting `aimErrorRad`.

## Target outcome

An `aimErrorRad` (radians, default ≈0.02) perturbs only aim-flagged intents from the governor's
seeded aim-error stream; every confirmed hit on the engaged target multiplies the current error by
`aimErrorDecay` (≈0.5, floored at 0); the error is restored to `aimErrorRad` after a repositioning
move (`aimErrorResetDistance` px, torus-aware, from the position at the last hit) or a change of
engagement target. All three knobs are live sliders and persisted in `bot-tuning.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC4 (restated — this feature owns it):** **AC4 — Configurable, self-correcting aim error.** A new live-tuned `aimErrorRad` (radians, default small — ≈0.02 rad — and applied only to intents flagged as **aim**, never to survival/evade/travel) perturbs the committed aim bearing from the governor's dedicated seeded aim-error RNG stream (deterministic per run seed, no draw at `0`, so `0` is byte-for-byte today's behaviour). It is independent of the existing `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` degradation. The error is **adaptive, not fixed** (producer answer Q1): every confirmed hit on the engaged target multiplies the current error by `aimErrorDecay` (default ≈0.5, floored at 0), so a bot that keeps hitting zeroes in; the error is restored to `aimErrorRad` only after a **repositioning move** — the ship having moved `aimErrorResetDistance` px (default ≈60, torus-aware, measured from its position at the last hit) or having changed engagement target. All three knobs are live sliders via `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` / `GymBotTuning` and persisted in `src/data/bot-tuning.json`; the hit signal arrives through one shared scene seam (AC6), so the game and every gym feed it identically.
- `aimErrorRad` (default ≈0.02 rad), `aimErrorDecay` (default ≈0.5) and `aimErrorResetDistance`
  (default ≈60 px) exist as governor tunables and are exposed as live sliders in
  `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`, round-tripped into the governor overrides, and seeded into every
  shipped config in `src/data/bot-tuning.json`.
- The error is drawn from the governor's **dedicated seeded aim-error stream** (the same stream
  `applySkillError` uses, or a documented sibling derived from the run seed) and applied only to
  intents with `aim === true`; survival, evade and travel intents are byte-for-byte unaffected.
- At `aimErrorRad = 0` **no draw is consumed** and the committed decision is byte-for-byte today's
  — asserted by a determinism test that runs the same seed with the knob at 0 and compares the full
  input stream.
- The error is independent of the existing `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` degradation: both can be non-zero
  at once, each with its own magnitude, and a test pins the combined behaviour.
- A confirmed hit on the **engaged target** (the id the committed intent was aiming at) multiplies
  the current error by `aimErrorDecay`, floored at 0; a hit on any other enemy does not.
- The error is restored to `aimErrorRad` when the ship has moved `aimErrorResetDistance` px
  (torus-aware) from its position at the last hit, **or** when the engagement target changes;
  both rules are unit-tested, including the torus seam case.
- The hit signal arrives only through the shared seam from Feature 5 (no scene-local counter), and
  the committed intent carries the target identity the governor compares against.
- Deterministic per run seed: same seed, same inputs → identical error sequence (no wall clock).

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

- Add the three tunables to `BotGovernorTunables` in `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` (beside
  `maxAimErrorRad`), with documented defaults and disabled-at-0 semantics.
- Track `currentAimErrorRad` in the governor; multiply on `noteAimHit(id)` when `id` matches the
  committed intent's target id; re-arm on target change and on displacement past the reset distance
  (measured with the shared wrapped-distance helper).
- Extend `SteeredIntent` with `targetId?: number`, set by `engage` from the best target's `id`; the
  governor compares against it.
- Apply the perturbed bearing in the same place `applySkillError` runs (compose with it), rotating
  the committed bearing and re-deriving the cardinals.
- Add the three `tuningFields` entries, the `bot-tuning.json` values and round-trip tests in
  `src/ai/tuningFields.test.ts`; unit tests for decay/reset/determinism in
  `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`.

## Constraints / risky assumptions

- A hit signal that lies would sharpen the aim for the wrong reason: only the engaged target counts
  (Feature 5 supplies the id), and a target change re-arms the error.
- A distance-only reset could re-arm mid-fight during a slow strafe, or never in a hugging fight:
  `aimErrorResetDistance` is a live knob and the harness reports the shot mix so it is tuned on
  numbers rather than by feel.
- Deterministic and allocation-free per tick; the decay/reset state is three numbers plus one
  position on the governor.
- Assumption: composing a multiplicative decay over a seeded uniform draw preserves the "seeded,
  reproducible" property the parent requires.

## Dependencies

- Feature 5 (shared aim-hit seam) — the hit signal and the bot-side identity.
- Feature 4 (class-sampled intercept solve) — the committed intent's target identity/hit path lands
  after the solve it perturbs.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — the three tunables, the decay/re-arm state and the perturbed bearing
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — set `targetId` on the committed aim intent
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` — the three live sliders
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — seeded defaults for every shipped config
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.test.ts` — tests
- `src/ai/botRotationSkills.integration.test.ts` — end-to-end aim with the knob live

# Accuracy regression proof and recorded numbers — Feature 7 of 8

**Parent:** AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP · **Effort:** ~2h · **Risk:** Medium

## Summary

Feature 1 recorded the pre-change baseline; the solve, the live inputs and the adaptive error have
landed. This feature turns the harness into an assertion: pooled hit rate strictly higher than the
recorded baseline and mean miss distance strictly lower, with `aimErrorRad = 0`, plus the per-class
numbers written back to the parent work item as evidence.

## Target outcome

An automated test proves the new aim solve is more accurate than the pre-change baseline, per class
and pooled, and the measured before/after numbers are recorded on the parent work item so "more
accurate" is a number rather than an opinion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC5 (restated — this feature owns it):** **AC5 — Accuracy is measured, not asserted.** A deterministic headless aim-accuracy harness (seeded, fixed 60 Hz, a fixed seed list of at least three seeds, one scenario per movement class) reports shots fired / shots hit / mean miss distance for the new solve against the pre-change baseline, and a regression test asserts the pooled hit rate is strictly higher than the baseline and the mean miss distance lower, with `aimErrorRad = 0`. The measured before/after numbers are recorded on the work item.
- A regression test runs the Feature 1 harness against the **pinned pre-change baseline** fixture and
  asserts the pooled hit rate is **strictly higher** and the pooled mean miss distance **strictly
  lower**, with `aimErrorRad = 0` so the measurement is of the solve, not of the fallibility knob.
- The test reports (and its failure message names) the per-class numbers, so a chaser/diver/patroller
  regression is visible even when the pooled total improves.
- The per-class result table is recorded on the parent work item (AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP) as a comment:
  shots fired / shots hit / hit rate / mean miss distance, baseline versus new, per class and pooled.
- The measurement is deterministic: the assertion reproduces on re-run with the documented seed list;
  no wall clock, no unseeded randomness.
- If a class cannot meet the bar, the finding is recorded and a follow-up work item is created —
  the pool bar is never relaxed and the baseline fixture is never retuned to pass.
- The harness and its assertion run inside the normal test suite (no manual step required for the
  proof to be re-verified), within the suite's runtime budget.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

- Extend `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.test.ts` with the before/after comparison against the committed
  baseline fixture, using the same seeds, tick rate and class scenarios.
- Print the comparison table on failure (seed, class, fired/hit/hit-rate/miss-distance) so triage is
  immediate.
- Post the measured table to the parent work item with `wl comment add` once the numbers are stable.
- Keep the run time bounded: reuse the sweep's seeding/tick budget patterns; if the matrix is slow,
  run the pooled assertion over all seeds and per-class over a documented subset (never fewer than
  the parent's three seeds for the pooled figure).

## Constraints / risky assumptions

- Evidence must come from the shipped aim path in the headless arena, not a re-implementation.
- Telemetry schema unchanged (parent constraint): the numbers live in the harness/test layer.
- Risk — a brittle baseline: the fixture is a recorded observation of the pre-change solve; a future
  intentional tuning change must record a **new** baseline deliberately, with a work-item note, never
  by silently re-running the harness.
- Assumption: the arena's bullet/hostile model is faithful enough for a relative comparison (the
  harness documents the divergence).

## Dependencies

- Features 2, 3, 4 and 6 (tracker velocity, live inputs, class-sampled solve, adaptive error) — the
  change being measured.
- Feature 1 (harness and baseline fixture).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.test.ts` — the regression assertion (extends Feature 1's harness)
- `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.ts` — metric folding and the baseline comparison table
- `src/ai/eval/aimAccuracy.baseline.json` — the pinned baseline fixture committed by Feature 1
  (read-only here except for a documented re-baseline)

# Aim solve documentation and knob docs — Feature 8 of 8

**Parent:** AH-0MWPOET5A002IPTP · **Effort:** ~2h · **Risk:** Low

## Summary

The aim solve, its live inputs, the class-sampled intercept, the aim-hit seam and the new adaptive
error knobs change what the documented bot does. `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.8 and the §12 knob table
still describe the constant-velocity lead and the old knob set, and the docs test asserts the
document's contents.

## Target outcome

A developer can read one document section and understand how the bot now aims — tracked estimate,
live shot speed and turn time, class-sampled intercept, adaptive aim error and its decay/reset rules,
and the accuracy harness/numbers — and the knob table names every new live slider.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC7 (restated — this feature owns it):** **AC7 — Docs and tests.** `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.8 (rotation skills / lead) and the §12 knob list describe the new solve, the new knob and the accuracy harness; unit tests cover the solve, the speed/turn inputs and the error draw, and `src/ai/botRotationSkills.integration.test.ts` (or a sibling integration test) exercises the end-to-end aim. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.8 documents the new aim solve: the tracked-estimate precedence
  (tracked → snapshot → current position), the live projectile speed and derived turn time, the
  class-sampled intercept with its exact fallbacks, and the preserved torus behaviour.
- §12 (the live bot-tuning gym knob list) documents `aimErrorRad`, `aimErrorDecay` and
  `aimErrorResetDistance`, including the decay-on-hit / re-arm-on-reposition rule and what `0` means
  for each.
- The accuracy harness is documented (where it lives, the seeds, the metric definitions, the
  recorded baseline and current numbers) so the evidence is reproducible from the docs alone.
- The module-level doc comments of the changed `src/ai` code match the document (no contradiction
  between code comment and §9.8), and `assumedBulletSpeed` is consistently described as the
  enemy-bullet tell constant.
- The docs assertions in `src/ai/framework/botFrameworkDocs.test.ts` (and any knob-description tests
  in `src/ai/tuningFields.test.ts`) guard the new content, so a later edit cannot silently drop it.
- Any wiki or docs-site entry that describes the bot's aim is updated to match (or explicitly
  recorded as unchanged with the reason).

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

- Rewrite the aim-lead paragraph(s) of §9.8 and add the accuracy-harness subsection; extend the §12
  knob table with the three new rows.
- Add docs assertions for the new content to `botFrameworkDocs.test.ts` (the existing pattern:
  `it('documents …')` with a content regex/`toContain`).
- Update the changed modules' header comments in the same change so the code and the doc cannot
  diverge.
- Check `README.md` / any docs-site bot page for statements about aim lead and update or record
  why not.

## Constraints / risky assumptions

- UK English; the project's documentation voice (see the existing §9.8 and `docs/TELEMETRY.md`).
- No behaviour change in this feature — documentation and its assertions only.
- Assumption: no telemetry documentation changes are needed (parent constraint: no new event kinds).

## Dependencies

- Features 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 (the behaviour being documented) — the doc must describe what shipped.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — §9.8 (rotation skills / lead) and §12 (live knob list)
- `src/ai/framework/botFrameworkDocs.test.ts` — docs assertions
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`, `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — header comments kept in step
- `./README.md` — bot/aim cross-reference, if it makes a lead claim
